-+++          "text": "# S5-REV-C verdict: APPROVE",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Reviewed `git diff 07ef5c5..40ee65c` (S5 work) on top of full-file reads of every touched module, the pre-S5 baseline (`git show 07ef5c5:…` / `827e655:…` for the v0.1.0 snapshot format), all 5 gates, and 3× full-suite flake runs. S5-B (the agent that crashed before reporting) got the hardest scrutiny per instructions: every one of its six items was re-derived from the contract and the code, not from any implementer claim.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "No P0s. One P1 (contract-mandated design gap with an exotic trigger — should fix at close), seven P2s. Sandbox output-filter rule respected: the icon byte length was verified with `stat -c %s` (5430), not with filtered cat/rg output.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Findings",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P0 (blocks approval)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "None.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P1 (should fix before release)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **`sysproxy.rs:153-154, 418-421, 440-445` — Opaque tri-state leaves OUR values, not the user's, in place after a connect/disconnect cycle.** Two facets of one root gap (the contract's \"Opaque → leave untouched, that is the user's data\" ignores that `set()` overwrites those very values first): - **(a) Silent proxy-enable flip via type-mismatched `ProxyEnable`** — the exact scenario the review brief called out. With `ProxyEnable` present as a non-DWORD (e.g. REG_SZ `\"0\"`, written by some third-party proxy switchers): `set()` unconditionally writes DWORD 1 (`sysproxy.rs:418`); `snap_dword` records `Opaque` (`:344-348`); `restore` takes `EnableAction::Leave` (`:444`) and writes nothing. Result: after disconnect, `ProxyEnable` is still DWORD 1 pointing at the now-dead local HTTP inbound — every WinINET consumer is blackholed until the user manually disables the proxy. This is a *regression vs v0.1.0*, where the failed typed read snapshotted `0` and restore wrote 0 (disabled = fail-safe). Failure scenario is concrete; trigger is rare (Windows itself always writes DWORD there). - **(b) Exotic-typed REG_SZ values are destroyed by `set()` itself** — for a REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_BINARY `ProxyServer`/`ProxyOverride`/`AutoConfigURL`, the unconditional `reg_set_string` loop (`:419-421`) replaces the user's value with our REG_SZ string before restore ever runs; `Opaque → Leave` then preserves *our* tunnel address, not the user's data. The S2-REV-C P2-5 goal is only half-achieved (restore no longer deletes — but `set` already clobbered).",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P2 (nits)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **`supervisor.rs:371,382` — residual check-then-act window in the exit-race fix.** The gates narrow the ~1 s re-set window to the gate→side-effect span, but a stop landing *after* the net-merge gate still lets `netmerge::on` complete up to `BOND_WAIT` = 15 s after an `emergency_stop` restored the proxy (and `sysproxy::set` for ~ms). Suggested: re-check `stop` *after* each side effect and best-effort undo (`sysproxy::restore` / `netmerge::off`). 2. **`sysproxy.rs:193-216` — `save_snapshot` is not atomic** (create_new + write_all, no fsync/rename). A crash mid-write leaves a truncated `sysproxy.json`; `load_snapshot` then errors and every caller drops the error (`let _ =` at `supervisor.rs:304,335,410,494,550,653`), so all future restores silently no-op — proxy stays enabled across reboots until the file is hand-deleted. Reuse the `fsutil` temp+fsync+rename pattern; log restore errors somewhere visible. 3. **`supervisor.rs:728` + `core_proc.rs:249,286` — `listen: \"localhost\"` passes `ensure_loopback_listen` (and now `Config::validate`) but `wait_for_port`/`socks_probe` parse `\"localhost:10808\"` as a `SocketAddr` → connect always fails at step 2 with \"invalid address\".** Pre-existing inconsistency (not an S5 regression); consider resolving localhost at load or rejecting with a precise message. 4. **`main.rs:213-222` — `join_reader` discards already-collected output when the 1 s grace expires** (grandchild inheriting the pipe), and the TimedOut path detaches readers entirely (documented). Bounded, no hang possible; doctor may show an empty version line.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Contract-item verification",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### S5-A (config + main CLI)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **Loopback validation in `Config::validate` — VERIFIED.** `config.rs:273` calls `ensure_loopback_listen` inside `validate()`; `Config::load` → `validate` covers generate/doctor/connect uniformly (connect keeps its own in-sequence check). Tests: `validate_accepts_loopback_listen_values` (127.0.0.1 + localhost), `validate_rejects_non_loopback_listen` (192.168.1.5, message names the value AND \"loopback\"), `validate_rejects_listen_that_is_not_an_ip`. (See P2-3 for the pre-existing localhost/SocketAddr tension.) 2. **`--config=PATH` equals form — VERIFIED.** `split_args` (`main.rs:75-101`) accepts space and both equals forms, errors on missing/ empty path, last flag wins; usage text updated (`main.rs:475-478`); five parsing tests incl. edge cases. 3. **doctor `xray version` bounded + windowless — VERIFIED.** `run_bounded` (`main.rs:168-197`): explicit `Duration`, 50 ms `try_wait` slices, kill+ reap on timeout, pipes drained on reader threads (no chatty-child false timeout); CREATE_NO_WINDOW added for Windows (`main.rs:270-276`); timeout reported as `[fail] … timed out and was killed`. Unix tests exercise both the fast-child and the 250 ms-budget-kills-sleep-30 paths. 4. **`main.rs` `write_private` → fsutil — VERIFIED.** `main.rs:134-136` delegates; credential doc retained; test asserts exact contents + no temp sibling left. 5. **Empty `proxyOverride` semantics — VERIFIED.** Absent field → serde container default (full LAN bypass list); explicit value verbatim; explicit `\"\"` stays `\"\"` (`config.rs:184-188` documents the deliberate non-defaulting).",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### S5-B (runtime files — the agent that never reported; re-derived from scratch)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **Snapshot tri-state, no silent deletes — VERIFIED with one P1.** Checked: `SnapValue` untagged serde round-trips all three states distinctly (`null` / plain value / `{\"opaqueKind\":…}`); malformed markers are errors, never silent Absent; `str_action`/`enable_action`/`string_write_plan` mappings (Absent→delete/0, Value→write, Opaque→Leave) with an all-Opaque snapshot test incl. file round-trip; mid-set half-applied comment present (Snapshot doc + set site). **Backward compatibility verified against the REAL v0.1.0 on-disk format** (read `git show 827e655:src/sysproxy.rs`: old struct = `proxyEnable: u32` always a number + `Option<String>` → null/string for the other three; same field names/casing): the legacy test (`snapvalue_serde_tri_state_and_legacy_format`) parses exactly that shape, and old-number→Value / old-null→Absent reproduce v0.1.0 restore behavior exactly — it is not a self-referential roundtrip. **P1-1 above** is the gap: `Opaque ProxyEnable` → proxy left ENABLED after restore (silent flip), and `set()` clobbers exotic-typed REG_SZ values so `Leave` preserves our data, not the user's. 2. **`ProxyOverride` verbatim incl. empty — VERIFIED.** No skip-when-empty branch remains in `set`; `set_string_plan` (`sysproxy.rs:175-180`) always emits the override; test `set_plan_writes_override_verbatim_even_when_empty`. 3. **supervisor `write_private` → fsutil — VERIFIED.** `supervisor.rs:796-799` delegates; test `write_private_is_atomic_and_private` (contents, unix 0600, no temp sibling). 4.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### S5-C (tray polish)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **`spawn_detached` logs failures — VERIFIED.** `tray.rs:887-891` maps the spawn Result through `log_err` (`:476`, stderr writeln, never eprintln); fire-and-forget preserved. 2. **Icon test pins the asset — VERIFIED.** 16×16 DIB header asserted (biSize 40, width 16, height 32) and total length pinned at 5430; true byte length confirmed with `stat -c %s assets/icon.ico` = **5430** (output-filter rule); the comment's arithmetic (6 + 2·16 + 4264 + 1128, AND-mask rows padded to 32 bits) checks out. 3. **Status-dump test cleans up — VERIFIED.** `tray.rs:1416-1418` `remove_dir_all` at the end. 4. **Exit tooltip — VERIFIED (additive, with caveat).** EXIT_TIP NIM_MODIFY inserted between the NIM_DELETE and the disconnect worker; diff-confirmed the ladder's ordering/timing untouched; SAFETY comments remain 1:1 with unsafe blocks — counted 34 `unsafe {` vs 34 `SAFETY:` (was 33/33; the diff adds exactly one of each); `exit_tip_fits_nif_tip_cap` test. Caveat (P2-7b): it can only render when the NIM_DELETE failed.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### S5-D (ship hygiene)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **release.yml lints on tag — VERIFIED.** `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` added BEFORE test/build; toolchain step now installs `components: rustfmt, clippy`. 2. **CI caching — VERIFIED.** `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` on all three ci.yml jobs and the release job, default keying, no custom paths. 3. **Server config mode — VERIFIED.** 0640 root:nogroup + the User=nobody/`id -gn nobody` verify note; `bash -n` green; the script's summary line updated; its own `xray run -test` runs as root during setup so it can still read the file. 4. **QUICKSTART zip list — VERIFIED.** All 8 contents + folder-name note; the README sentence matches the ACTUAL release.yml Package step (verified it really copies server/setup-xray-reality.sh into the zip). P2-7c: the \"multitunnel-v0.3.0\" example reads oddly for the v0.2.0 release.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Cross-cutting: no test touches the real registry (sysproxy tests are pure helpers + temp dirs; windows-only registry code is cfg-gated and never exercised by tests) or any non-loopback network; all stub listeners use the quit-flag + nonblocking-accept pattern with bounded joins (the S2 hang class); no panics on garbage input found in non-test code (poison-tolerant locks, no unwrap/expect outside tests); `netmerge.rs`/`elevate.rs`/`xrayconf.rs`/ `error.rs`/`lib.rs`/`src/bin/tray.rs` untouched by S5 as expected.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Gate results (tails)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "- `cargo fmt --check` → clean, exit 0 (no output). - `cargo test` → `test result: ok. 103 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 6.06s` (lib) · `test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; … finished in 0.25s` (multitunnel bin) · `0 passed` (tray bin) · `0 passed` (doc-tests). - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Checking multitunnel v0.2.0 … Finished \\`dev\\` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4.08s` (zero warnings). - `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` → `Checking multitunnel v0.2.0 … Finished \\`dev\\` profile … in 9.99s` (zero warnings). - `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --release` → `Finished \\`release\\` profile [optimized] target(s) in 26.87s`; both artifacts verified PE32+ (`multitunnel.exe` console 3,243,008 B, `multitunnel-tray.exe` GUI 3,210,752 B).",

-+++        {
-+++          "text": "No flakes, no hangs — every run finished far inside the 300 s kill threshold; the slowest individual tests are the bounded supervisor lifecycle tests (core-death/give-up, exit-race boundaries), all deterministic by design.",

-+++      "id": "report:s6-rev-b",

-+++      "title": "S6-REV-B verdict: APPROVE",

-+++      ],
-+++      "passages": [
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "# S6-REV-B verdict: APPROVE",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Reviewer lens: BUILD / PORTABILITY (windows-gnu cross) / DEPENDENCY + LICENSE HYGIENE / CI + RELEASE PACKAGING / DOCS ACCURACY / TEST QUALITY. Scope: `git diff d721cba..HEAD` (S6 waves 1-3, 49 files, +15319/−216) read as FULL files (all 7 new crates, root wiring src/{real_service,profiles,main,lib}.rs, both workflows, scripts/mingw-zig-shims.sh, Cargo.toml/lock, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, README/QUICKSTART), plus independent runs of every gate. Frontier verified at 6df8767.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Zero P0. Three P1 (release-gate scope regression, stale MSRV claim, stale THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES). Eight P2 notes + 7 backlog confirmations. All 8 gates green; all three exes verified PE32+ with the correct subsystems; no copyleft license anywhere in the 391-package lockfile.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Gates",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "All gates run by me, in order, with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/target-rev-b` (cold dir; removed at the end):",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "| # | Gate | Result | |---|------|--------| | 1 | `cargo fmt --all --check` | **PASS** (no output, exit 0) | | 2 | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (host) | **PASS** (exit 0; one non-fatal cargo manifest warning, see P2-2) | | 3 | `sh scripts/mingw-zig-shims.sh /tmp/shims-b` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | **PASS** (exit 0; same non-fatal manifest warning) | | 4 | `cargo test --workspace` | **PASS** — 321 passed / 0 failed (mt-app 18, mt-engine 4+2 golden+3 lifecycle, mt-links 64, mt-m3 13, mt-net 44, mt-platform 25, root 140 lib + 8 bin + 0 tray, mt-service 0) | | 5 | `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **PASS** — multitunnel.exe **PE32+ console**, multitunnel-tray.exe **PE32+ GUI** (this command builds the root package only; mt-app.exe comes from gate 6 — verified by deleting mt-app.exe and re-running: not rebuilt) | | 6 | `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p mt-app` | **PASS** — mt-app.exe **PE32+ console** (the iced window app binary) | | 7 | `cargo check -p mt-app --no-default-features` | **PASS** (the real-service path linked into multitunnel.exe) | | 8 | `cargo check -p mt-platform --features embedded` | **PASS** (repeated with a real `MT_EMBED_ENGINE=<zip>` fixture: also PASS — the documented release embed path compiles) |",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Extra verifications beyond the required gates: `cargo check --features mock-gui` PASS; `cargo check -p mt-app` (default mock) PASS; workspace YAML parses (both workflows, `yaml.safe_load`); trigger lines verified **bytewise** (`od -An -c`: ci.yml `branches: [main]` + `pull_request:`, release.yml `tags: [\"v*\"]` — no S4-style phantom). One output-filter scare (`rg -rn` = replace-with-\"n\" mangled \"smoke\" → \"n\") was self-inflicted and resolved by re-reading source: `--smoke` exists as documented at crates/mt-app/src/app.rs:177/5052/5410.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Findings",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P0 (blocks approval)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "None.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "- All builds and gates pass (above), including windows-gnu release of all three exes with the correct PE subsystems — no host-only dependency found (reqwest+rustls+ring compile under the zig shims; iced tiny-skia renderer links cleanly with no wgpu in the tree). - **License sweep: no GPL/AGPL/LGPL/MPL/CDDL/SSPL/EUPL anywhere.** All 391 external packages in Cargo.lock verified against the actual `license` field: 291 from the local registry tarballs (`/home/z/my-project/tools/cargo/registry/cache`), the remaining 100 (wasm/android/objc target-gated deps never extracted on this host) via the crates.io API at their **exact locked versions**. Distinct expressions are all permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, BSL-1.0, Unicode-3.0, Unlicense, CDLA-Permissive-2.0). Two dual/triple-OR crates carry a copyleft *option* that we do not elect: `self_cell 1.3.0` (\"Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only\", pulled by cosmic-text) and `r-efi` (\"MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later\", UEFI-only target) — OR-licensed means the permissive term is chosen; no contamination, but the elections should be recorded in the notices refresh (folded into P1-3).",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P1 (should fix before release)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **NEW — .github/workflows/release.yml:20-25 — release gate still scoped to the root package; the 7 new S6 crates are untested at tag time.** `cargo fmt --check` (no `--all`), `cargo clippy --all-targets` (no `--workspace`) and `cargo test` (no `--workspace`) cover only the root package = 148 of the 321 workspace tests; none of mt-links/mt-net/ mt-engine/mt-m3/mt-platform/mt-service/mt-app's own tests, lints or fmt run on a `v*` tag, and the workflow's own comments (S2-REV-B P1-1, \"a v* tag must never ship an untested build — tag pushes bypass ci.yml\") state exactly the guarantee that no longer holds — and all seven crates are *linked into* the shipped multitunnel.exe. ci.yml's test/lint/cross-check legs are all correctly `--workspace`, so the exposure is a tag cut from a commit whose main-push CI hasn't completed or was skipped; still a regression of a documented invariant. Fix: add `--workspace` / `--all` to the three gate lines (cheap, no downside on windows-latest).",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "2. **NEW — Cargo.toml:8 (echoed at README.md:218) — `rust-version = \"1.78\"` is now false; the effective MSRV is 1.97.** `material-colors 0.5.0` (mt-m3's color engine) declares `rust-version = \"1.97.0\"`; uuid 1.29.3 needs 1.89, tokio 1.54.1 needs 1.85, iced 0.13.1 needs 1.80. Cargo hard-fails dependency rust-version at build time, so a 1.78 toolchain cannot resolve the workspace at all — the field (and README's \"Stable Rust (MSRV 1.78)\") is misleading for packagers. The new member crates declare no `rust-version` at all. Fix: bump the root field to the true floor (≥ 1.97, or simply drop the claim / pin to the toolchain CI uses), update README, and consider `workspace.package.rust-version` inheritance for the members. Build is green on the sandbox's 1.100.0, so this is metadata/doc accuracy, not a broken build.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "3. **NEW — THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:14-28 — notices not updated for the S6 dependency explosion; the file's own rule (\"Update it whenever Cargo.lock gains a new dependency\") is violated by ~375 additions.** The table still lists only the v0.2 set (serde/regex/windows-sys/winreg + subcrates). Missing entirely: iced + its tree (winit, tiny-skia, softbuffer, cosmic-text, iced_*), tokio, reqwest + rustls + ring + hyper + quinn, zip/sha2/hex/base64/uuid/url/percent-encoding/thiserror/tracing/ async-trait/anyhow/futures/ipnet/bytes and everything else new. Also missing, non-crate but license-relevant: **iced_graphics 0.13.0 embeds `fonts/FiraSans-Regular.ttf` (SIL OFL-1.1) and `fonts/Iced-Icons.ttf` compiled into every shipped GUI binary** — OFL is permissive but requires its notice on redistribution; and the permissive elections for `self_cell` (Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only → Apache-2.0) and `r-efi` (→ MIT) should be recorded (see P0 section — verified, nothing contaminating). The Xray-core row's framing (\"downloaded by the user … it only launches processes the user installed\") is also stale for v0.3, where mt-platform downloads and installs the engine itself (D14) — downloading from XTLS's releases at user trigger is still not redistribution, but the sentence should be re-worded. The pre-existing zmij/itoa-URL nit (S5-REV-B P2-7) rides along in the same refresh. No license incompatibility exists (P0 sweep above); this P1 is the completeness obligation before the v0.3 zip ships the notices file into end-user hands.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P2 (notes)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **NEW — .github/workflows/release.yml:25,34-43 — mt-app.exe is never built or packaged by the release job, and nothing documents that decision.** `cargo build --release` at the workspace root builds only the root package (verified empirically: deleting mt-app.exe and re-running the equivalent zigbuild does not recreate it), so the MSVC release leg never produces the third exe, and the `$required` list / zip contains only multitunnel.exe + multitunnel-tray.exe. Functionally the zip is fine: the all-in-one GUI is reachable as `multitunnel gui` inside multitunnel.exe (real service, mt-app default-features off), and the standalone mt-app.exe is MockService-only (crates/mt-app/src/main.rs:14-46) — shipping it as-is would give users a fake-backend GUI. But the stage acceptance (\"PE32+ console + tray + gui\") is only proven by the sandbox gate + ci.yml's *debug* cross-check, never in release config on MSVC. Decide and document: either (a) declare mt-app.exe dev-only and keep it out of the zip (my recommendation), or (b) build `-p mt-app --release` too and give it a real-backend story. One sentence in release.yml/README suffices.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "2. **NEW — crates/mt-m3/Cargo.toml:11 — unused `thiserror = \"2\"` dependency (cargo emits a manifest warning on every clippy run).** The crate's own docs (crates/mt-m3/src/lib.rs:61) record it as \"frozen but currently unused\". The contract's allowed-deps list permits thiserror but does not require it; the warning is noise today but any future cargo promoting `cargo::unused_dependencies` past `warn` (or a stricter CI lint pass) turns it red. Remove the dep (and the doc sentence), or use it.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "3. **NEW — Cargo.lock — thiserror 1.0.69 + 2.0.21 duplication is forced, not fixable (informational).** All iced 0.13.x crates, calloop, quinn, smithay-client-toolkit, window_clipboard etc. still pin thiserror 1, so the workspace's thiserror-2 crates cannot collapse it. Same story for base64 0.22/0.23 (mt-links vs reqwest/hyper-util), getrandom 0.2/0.3/0.4, redox_syscall ×4, windows-sys 0.52/0.59/0.61 — normal transitive duplication, no action available short of downgrades. Answering focus #4 explicitly: the two thiserror majors are needed.",

-+++          "text": "4. **NEW — docs statements now wrong (docs refresh is a planned separate step; listing only what is FALSE, not demanding new v0.3 docs):** README.md:8 \"One crate, two binaries\" (now a workspace of 8 crates / 3 exes); README.md:169-177 CLI reference omits `import` (stale since v0.2) and the new `profiles`/`gui` (the binary's own usage at src/main.rs:563- 571 is correct); README.md:218 MSRV 1.78 (see P1-2); QUICKSTART.md steps 2-3 (install net-merge; manually download/place `xray.exe`) now describe the legacy v0.2 path — v0.3 bonds in-process (mt-net) and self-provisions the engine on first connect (D14); QUICKSTART's zip-contents list (lines 17-20) still matches release.yml exactly. Also src/main.rs:564 usage prints \"(none) start the tray app (Windows)\" while no-args actually errors with a pointer to multitunnel-tray.exe — pre-existing nit.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "5. **NEW — harness/CONTRACTS-S6.md:328-329 vs .github/workflows/ci.yml — the `--smoke` flag is described as the CI verification of the GUI, but no workflow ever runs it.** The smoke *code path* is unit-covered (crates/mt-app/src/app.rs run_smoke test; the orchestrator ran `multitunnel gui --smoke` manually per LEDGER), but the \"run 3 s headless then exit 0 (CI)\" promise is unwired. Cheap add to the ubuntu test leg (`cargo run -q --bin multitunnel -- gui --smoke` or `cargo run -q -p mt-app -- --smoke`) to catch GUI-side regressions (view construction, theme derive) on every push. Optional, since the in-process test covers the same code.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },

-+++          "text": "6. **NEW — crates/mt-engine/tests/lifecycle.rs:10 — the whole child-process lifecycle suite is `#![cfg(unix)]`,** so spawn/port-up/kill/respawn/ budget-exhaustion/kill-on-drop never execute on the windows-latest test leg (they run on ubuntu, and the CREATE_NO_WINDOW surface compiles on windows-gnu clippy). Accepted-by-contract (the fake engine is python3), but worth one line in the crate docs' known-limitations so nobody assumes Windows CI exercises process supervision.",

Harmless; bump to `--release` if a cheap belt is wanted. (Disk/time cost on the runner.)",

-+++          "text": "8. **Backlog confirmations (all unchanged, all in v0.2 root code untouched by S6 — parked as accepted):** localhost listen inconsistency (src/ real_service.rs:589-590 binds fixed 127.0.0.1; sysproxy override literal \"localhost\" at real_service.rs:698 — same shape as v0.2); join_reader 1 s grace (src/main.rs, untouched); restore-error surfacing (sysproxy, untouched); snapshot downgrade doc (sysproxy.rs, untouched); **CI cache keying** (Swatinem default keys at ci.yml:19/39/65 + release.yml:17; the zig-using legs — lint *and* cross-check — still don't key on zig 0.17.1; same theoretical staleness S5-REV-B P2-3 described, no worse); no-snapshot-disable UX; disconnect-latency tray note. Positive deltas since S5: release.yml now hard-requires README.md and QUICKSTART.md in `$required` (S5-REV-B P2-4 is FIXED, release.yml:34-43); the zmij URL nit remains (rides with P1-3).",

-+++        {
-+++          "text": "# S6-REV-C verdict: APPROVE",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Reviewed `git diff d721cba..6df8767` (S6 waves 1–3) on top of full-file reads of every new module (`crates/mt-{links,net,engine,m3,platform,service,app}`, `src/real_service.rs`, `src/profiles.rs`, `src/main.rs` diffs, workspace `Cargo.toml`), the frozen spec (harness/CONTRACTS-S6.md), the design laws (DECISIONS.md D5/D9/D10/D14), and the S2 supervisor/sysproxy contracts the new paths had to preserve. Sandbox rules obeyed: the leftover-debug-print finding below was byte-verified with `od -An -c` (not filtered output), and no credential-like string from any config file was copied into this report (test vectors referenced are the synthetic CONTRACTS-S6 set).",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "No P0s. Five P1s (one debug leftover, two regressions of deliberately-fixed prior guarantees, one fail-open law regression, one routing-policy regression), plus P2 notes. All 6 gates green.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Gates",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "| gate | command | result | |------|---------|--------| | 1 | `cargo fmt --all --check` | **PASS** (no output, exit 0) | | 2 | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | **PASS** (exit 0, 1m09s) | | 3 | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | **PASS** (exit 0, 1m02s). Note: the brief's literal `--target x86_64_pc_windows_gnu` (underscores) is rejected by cargo — dashes required. One non-failing cargo-manifest lint appears: `mt-m3` unused dependency `thiserror` (P2-12); it does not trip `-D warnings` (rustc flag). | | 4 | `cargo test --workspace` | **PASS** — 321 tests, 0 failed, 0 ignored (18+4+2+3+64+13+44+25+140+8 across suites, ~16s slowest suite). | | 5 | `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **PASS** (exit 0, 3m03s) | | 6 | `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p mt-app` | **PASS** (exit 0, 37s) |",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Findings",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P0 (blocks approval)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "None.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P1 (should fix before release)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:336` — leftover debug `eprintln!` in the production liveness path.** `child_addr_if_alive()` — called on EVERY engine connect/probe (i.e. per proxied connection) — contains `eprintln!(\"[dbg-eng] probe pid={pid:?} tw={tw:?}\")` in non-test code. Byte-verified with `od -An -c` (sandbox output-filter rule). This violates global contract rule 5 (\"tracing for diagnostics, no println! in libs\") and will spam stderr of `multitunnel gui` with one line per tunnel connection. It leaks no credentials (pid + try_wait result only) but is exactly the class of leftover that must not ship. One-line deletion.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "2. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:450-461` — the v0.2 kill-on-close Job Object was not ported; `xray.exe` is orphaned on abnormal GUI death.** The module doc claims \"the exact `core_proc` discipline\", but `src/core_proc.rs:583-618` (added by the 2026-11-17 v0.2-audit REV-C#2 backport, commit ff0abb4) puts the child in a Windows Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so the *kernel* guarantees \"the core cannot outlive this process\". `ManagedEngine` relies solely on `Drop::kill_current()`, which does not run on `TerminateProcess` (Task Manager kill), console Ctrl+C (the C-runtime exits without unwinding), power loss, or panic-abort — the precise scenarios the v0.2 audit fixed. Normal window close is safe (runtime drop cancels tasks → Arc chain → Drop → kill), so the orphan trigger is abnormal death; the orphan then runs an open REALITY tunnel with a loopback listener indefinitely. Restore the job-object wrapper (cfg(windows)) around the spawned child, or route spawns through `core_proc`.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "3. **`src/real_service.rs:919-949,688-714` + `crates/mt-app/src/app.rs:831-842` + `src/main.rs:605-625` — the GUI path loses the S2 supervisor's fail-open/self-heal contract for the system proxy (D5).** Three facets, one root cause (RealService has no supervision loop and no lifecycle hook): **(a)** closing the GUI window while Connected (or Ctrl+C on the console host) never calls `disconnect()`/`sysproxy::restore` — no `window::close` subscription, no exit hook in `cmd_gui`; the registry keeps pointing at the now-dead `127.0.0.1:10809`. **(b)** Nothing heals a stale snapshot at startup: v0.2 `connect` step 0 is \"sysproxy::restore() best-effort\" (supervisor.rs:25, contract line); `RealService::connect_flow` has no equivalent, and `disconnect()` in a fresh instance is a no-op (`sysproxy_set=false`), so a crashed run leaves browsing blackholed until the user manually fixes Windows settings or completes a full connect→disconnect cycle. **(c)** Engine give-up does not restore: after `ManagedEngine` exhausts its respawn budget the outbound errors permanently while `RealService` state stays `Connected` and the system proxy stays set — the v0.2 supervisor restored the proxy on restart exhaustion (supervisor.rs:20-22, D5). Keep-first `save_snapshot` (sysproxy.rs:219-223) does protect the user's original values from being overwritten, so this is recoverable-but-stuck, not data loss. Distinct from the parked \"no-snapshot-disable UX\" backlog item: v0.2 had all three recovery paths; v0.3's GUI has none.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "4. **`src/real_service.rs:696-699,587-588` — LAN/private traffic no longer bypasses the tunnel when the GUI system proxy is on (regression of a stated top-3 design principle).** `lib.rs:22` lists \"LAN/private traffic bypasses the tunnel\" as a project invariant, implemented in v0.2 twice over: the proxy override default is the full LAN bypass list `localhost;127.*;10.*;192.168.*;…;<local>` (config.rs:134-139) AND the generated Xray config routes `geoip:private → direct` (xrayconf.rs:66). The S6 RealService path writes a hard-coded `ProxyOverride=\"localhost\"` only, and the `Router` starts with an empty rule list whose default action is `Proxy` (SettingsFile default rules = `Vec::new()`). Net effect with `system_proxy=true`: requests to 192.168.x/10.x/172.16-31.x (router admin pages, printers, NAS) are sent through the VLESS tunnel to the remote server — breaking local access and leaking LAN hostnames/IPs to the tunnel operator. Fix: seed the default rules with a private-CIDR → direct rule (or route private IPs direct in `ProxyServer::establish`) and write the v0.2 LAN bypass override.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "5. **`crates/mt-platform/src/engine.rs:129-133` (via `crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:412`) — engine-download errors echo the full request URL, which can carry a credential (D9).** `ReqwestFetch::fetch` propagates `reqwest::Error` via `?`; its `Display` includes the full URL (\"error sending request for url (…)\"). The chain `ensure() → \"engine \\`{tag}\\`: binary download failed: {e}\" → connect error string → GUI LogLine + tracing` therefore prints whatever `$MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE_URL` contains — and user-set download-mirror URLs with embedded tokens (`https://host/xray.zip?token=…`) are a common pattern; the token then persists in GUI logs and any pasted bug report. mt-links solved exactly this with `reqwest::Error::without_url()` (subscription.rs:100-108) — mt-platform needs the same treatment in `fetch` (and `error_for_status` on the same line).",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### P2 (notes)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "1. **`src/real_service.rs:661,932-934` — stale `disconnect_requested` flag can spuriously abort one later connect.** A `disconnect()` landing in the window between the post-probe flag check (line 661) and session installation sets the flag but leaves the session Connected; the flag is consumed only by a later `connect_flow`, which then aborts itself right after its probe (one lost connect click, self-healing thereafter). Clear the flag at `begin_connect` or after session install. NEW. 2. **`crates/mt-app/src/app.rs:524-531` — the GUI cannot cancel a Connecting session.** `ConnectToggle(false)` only acts when `cur == Connected`; while Connecting the switch silently bounces back. The service already implements cancellation (`disconnect_requested` honored after the probe) — the GUI just never calls it in that state. NEW. 3. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:316-324,428-430` + `src/real_service.rs:1015-1020` — two engines with the same profile tag race on shared files.** `test_latency` on the active profile while connected builds a second `ManagedEngine` with the same tag; both write `engine-<tag>.tmp` → `engine-<tag>.json` (one can truncate the other's in-flight temp; the fsutil single-writer assumption from S5-REV-C P2-6 is now reachable) and append to the same log handle. Worst case is a corrupt config → one failed spawn → retry; the misdirected port mostly self-corrects. Include the port or a nonce in the config/log filename, or serialize per-tag. NEW. 4.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "### Verified-clean highlights (no findings)",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "- **D10/D9 redaction**: every link.rs/migrate.rs error carries lengths only; ignored query params log NAMES only (link.rs:246-248); subscription failures are numbered-line + redacted; `profiles` CLI never prints identity; engine errors carry tag/port/binary-path at most; no `tracing` site in the new code interpolates `identity`/`public_key`/`uuid` (grepped). The one gap is P1-5. The mt-links percent-decode policy (decode query values/userinfo, never authority; pbk/sid alphabet-validated after decode) deviates from v0.2's stricter \"no percent-decoding of stored fields\" but is the frozen S6 contract's \"parse liberally\", keeps `parse(render(p)) == p` a fixed point, and D10 strictness still gates the engine path (`endpoint_from_profile`: VLESS×Reality×Tcp×vision-or-absent, polite credential-free errors). - **mt-platform zip install**: zip-slip is closed by basename allowlist + `..`/`:`/leading-`/` rejection + flat extraction into a private staging dir; SHA256SUMS is verified at locate-time exactly per D14 (advisory warn by default, `MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE_STRICT=1` refuses — by design, not a bug); the staging→rename swap with backup+restore makes partial installs crash-safe; reqwest is `default-features = false` + `rustls-tls` (validation on, no `danger_accept_*` anywhere in the workspace). - **mt-net data plane**: socks5/http parsers are total-budget (10 s) and size-bounded (16 KiB head, wire-length-bounded ATYP reads), reject non-UTF-8/zero-length domains, answer BIND/UDP with REP 07 and unknown ATYP with REP 08; CONNECT authority forms incl.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "## Verdict rationale",
-+++          "kind": "title"
-+++        },
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "The S6 expert crates are individually solid: parsers are panic-free and credential-redacted, the data plane matches its frozen contract in every detail I could pin down, the zip installer's zip-slip and atomicity story is sound, and all six gates pass with a 321-test suite. What keeps this at five P1s rather than a BLOCK is that none of them is an exploitable hole, credential *value* leak to a remote party, data loss, or a reachable panic/deadlock — the closest to the P0 bar are the D5 fail-open regression (P1-3) and the LAN-bypass regression (P1-4), both of which require the user to enable the system-proxy feature and both recoverable by manual action. But they are real regressions against deliberately-fixed guarantees (the v0.2-audit Job Object, the S2 stale-heal/give-up contract, the \"LAN bypasses the tunnel\" invariant), and P1-1/P1-5 are trivial fixes, so all five should land before the v0.3 release ships. APPROVE per D6 (zero P0s), with the P1 list as the release blocker checklist.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        }
-+++      ]
-+++    },

-+++          "text": "# v0.2.0-AUDIT-B (build/portability/license, on the recycled Nov-12 tree) — agent-0faf5e78 APPROVE. 0 P0 / 2 P1 / 5 P2. Key P1s: (1) restart-campaign loop only tested in its degenerate max=0 form — CampaignOutcome::Restarted and the max>0 exhaustion path have zero coverage; (2) S2 process/lifecycle semantics have zero runtime coverage on Windows (rig is unix-only) and the rig sets system_proxy:true — porting it naively to Windows CI would mutate the real HKCU registry of the runner. -+++          "text": "# v0.2.0-AUDIT-C (correctness/security, on the recycled Nov-12 tree) — agent-ac1cd5f2 APPROVE. 0 P0 / 3 P1 / 10 P2. Key P1s: (1) connect validates liveness only via port+probe — a foreign listener on socksPort with a dead own core yields Ok/Connected + endless restart churn (repro'd empirically via public API); (2) no Job Object kill-on-close — the xray child survives Ctrl+C (the documented CLI exit) and can never be stopped afterwards; (3) sysproxy snapshot write not atomic + corrupt snapshot errs forever while callers swallow → system proxy permanently stuck (defeats D5 fail-open). Verified: 52/52 tests, zigbuild green, both exes correct subsystems; 10/10 adversarial SOCKS5 probes against the real socks_probe (partial reads, ATYP 02/03/04 variants, silent server, overflow) — no panics/hangs; zero unwrap/expect in non-test code; connect order + D5 give-up path exact.",

-+++          "text": "## Current position - Stage: S14 IN FLIGHT, two tracks. (a) DONE — user directive \"store agentic memory as data graphs accessible to all agents and use retrieval augmented generation (RAG)\": typed graph store harness/memory/store/memory_graph.json (schema v1; 16 node types / 14 edge rels, evidence-gated; sources = PM durable sections, STATE/DECISIONS/LEDGER, agent-reports, consensus, git tags + full log, curated/). Session closed the WIP gaps: unused_mut fix, rustfmt, test helper S14 fields (no-report default exercises the S12 fallback), 6 new tests (carrier_score incl.",

-+++      "title": "Task E (core) — saturation-aware redistribution: when one adapter hits its bandwidth ceiling, spill traffic to the rest (S14, gated — release pending)",
-+++      "tags": [
-+++        "gated",

-+++          "anchor": "carrier_score"
-+++        }
-+++      ],
-+++      "passages": [
-+++        {
-+++          "text": "Task E core: user reported traffic still not split evenly — when one adapter reaches its maximum bandwidth, the remaining traffic does NOT split over to the remaining adapters. v0.7.0's balanced/priority (D23) spread per-connection load but stream-mode saturation spill was missing. S14 fix (started at commit f4a26ca, completed + gated this session): each endpoint measures per-carrier inbound rate and reports it to the peer piggybacked on 1 s PINGs; scheduler keeps EWMA assignment rate per carrier; carrier_score = assign_bps / max(deliver_bps, PROBE_BPS 32 KiB/s); Balanced picks least relative load (capacity-proportional spreading — aggregate = SUM of paths); Priority spills at score >= 1.15 (PRIORITY_SPILL_RATIO); reorder cap 4->16 MiB with a backpressure overflow path (would_overflow + REORDER_PAUSE) instead of failing the session; falls back to S12 least-queued behavior when the peer sends no reports. Gates passed: fmt, workspace clippy -D warnings, 404/0 workspace tests. REMAINING: windows-gnu clippy, zigbuild, release v0.8.0, real-setup verification.",
-+++          "kind": "body"
-+++        }
-+++      ]

-+++#!/usr/bin/env python3
-+++"""test_graph.py — tests for the agentic memory graph + RAG retrieval.

-+++
-+++import json

-+++class GraphBuildTests(unittest.TestCase):
-+++    """Build correctness: schema, determinism, curated merge."""
-+++
-+++    @classmethod
-+++    def setUpClass(cls):
-+++        cls.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
-+++        cls.out1 = Path(cls.tmp.name) / "g1.json"
-+++        cls.out2 = Path(cls.tmp.name) / "g2.json"
-+++        cls.store1 = build_graph.build(cls.out1)
-+++
-+++    @classmethod
-+++    def tearDownClass(cls):
-+++        cls.tmp.cleanup()
-+++
-+++    def test_schema_valid(self):
-+++        s = self.store1
-+++        self.assertEqual(s["schema_version"], 1)
-+++        self.assertEqual(s["node_count"], len(s["nodes"]))
-+++        self.assertEqual(s["edge_count"], len(s["edges"]))
-+++        graph_store.validate_nodes_edges(s["nodes"], s["edges"])
-+++
-+++    def test_expected_node_families_present(self):
-+++        ids = {n["id"] for n in self.store1["nodes"]}
-+++        for expected in (
-+++            "project:multitunnel", "protocol:pstack", "protocol:memory-graph",
-+++            "pm:architecture", "pm:playbook", "pm:contracts", "state:current",
-+++            "decision:D17", "decision:D23", "decision:D24",
-+++            "ledger:s13", "release:v0.7.1", "task:saturation-aware-split",
-+++            "task:e-ui-logo-titlebar-tray", "bug:uneven-traffic-split",
-+++            "component:mt-bond", "commit:f4a26ca",
-+++        ):
-+++            self.assertIn(expected, ids, f"missing node {expected}")
-+++
-+++    def test_deterministic_rebuild(self):
-+++        build_graph.build(self.out2)
-+++        self.assertEqual(self.out1.read_bytes(), self.out2.read_bytes(),
-+++                         "rebuild must be byte-identical (no wall-clock)")
-+++
-+++    def test_curated_release_edges(self):
-+++        rels = {(e["src"], e["dst"]) for e in self.store1["edges"]}
-+++        for task, rel in (
-+++            ("task:charts-rendering-fix", "release:v0.6.0"),
-+++            ("task:stream-bonding", "release:v0.6.2"),
-+++            ("task:balanced-priority-scheduling", "release:v0.7.0"),
-+++            ("task:status-page-layout", "release:v0.7.1"),
-+++            ("task:saturation-aware-split", "bug:uneven-traffic-split"),
-+++        ):
-+++            self.assertIn((task, rel), rels, f"missing curated edge {task}->{rel}")
-+++
-+++    def test_git_evidence_edges(self):
-+++        edges = {(e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"]) for e in self.store1["edges"]}
-+++        self.assertIn(("release:v0.7.1", "commit:e38a37a", "built_from"), edges,
-+++                      "release tag -> commit edge missing")
-+++        self.assertIn(("commit:f4a26ca", "ledger:s14", "part_of"), edges,
-+++                      "wip(s14) commit -> ledger stage edge missing")
-+++

-+++class RetrievalTests(unittest.TestCase):
-+++    """RAG retrieval quality: BM25 ranking + graph expansion."""
-+++
-+++    @classmethod
-+++    def setUpClass(cls):
-+++        cls.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
-+++        cls.store = build_graph.build(Path(cls.tmp.name) / "g.json")
-+++
-+++    @classmethod
-+++    def tearDownClass(cls):
-+++        cls.tmp.cleanup()
-+++
-+++    def _top_ids(self, query: str, k: int = 6, expand: int = 1) -> list[str]:
-+++        res = graph_store.retrieve(self.store, query, k=k, expand=expand)
-+++        self.assertTrue(res, f"no results for {query!r}")
-+++        return [r["node"] for r in res]

-+++#!/usr/bin/env python3
-+++"""write_memory.py — the agent WRITE path into the MultiTunnel memory graph.
-+++
-+++Agents (main session, subagents, future sessions) append durable knowledge
-+++without touching the builder. Writes land in harness/memory/curated/
-+++(merged last at build time — curated wins on node-id collision) and the
-+++store is rebuilt immediately. Validation is strict (whitelisted types/rels,
-+++endpoints must exist); a failed rebuild rolls the curated change back.
-+++
-+++Usage (from repo root):
-+++
-+++    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py \\
-+++        --node id=task:next-thing type=task title="Next thing" \\
-+++        passage="What and why." tag=next source=harness/memory/LEDGER.md
-+++
-+++    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py \\
-+++        --edge src=task:next-thing dst=project:multitunnel rel=part_of \\
-+++        evidence="roadmap item"
-+++
-+++    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py --list          # curated ids
-+++"""
-+++
-+++from __future__ import annotations
-+++
-+++import argparse
-+++import json
-+++import shutil
-+++import subprocess
-+++import sys
-+++import tempfile
-+++from pathlib import Path
-+++
-+++sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))

-+++from build_graph import DEFAULT_OUT, MEM, build  # noqa: E402

-+++CURATED = MEM / "curated"

-+++def parse_kv(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
-+++    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
-+++    for it in items:
-+++        if "=" not in it:
-+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] expected KEY=VALUE, got: {it!r}")
-+++        k, v = it.split("=", 1)
-+++        out.setdefault(k, []).append(v)
-+++    return out
-+++
-+++
-+++def read_json(path: Path, default: dict) -> dict:
-+++    if path.exists():
-+++        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
-+++    return default
-+++
-+++
-+++def write_json(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:

-+++    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
-+++                    encoding="utf-8")
-+++
-+++

-+++        if k not in kv:
-+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] --node requires {'/'.join(need)}=… (missing {k})")

-+++                         f"whitelist: {', '.join(graph_store.NODE_TYPES)}")
-+++    node = {
-+++        "id": kv["id"][0],
-+++        "type": kv["type"][0],
-+++        "title": kv["title"][0],
-+++        "tags": kv.get("tag", []),

-+++                    for f in kv.get("source", ["harness/memory/curated/"])],
-+++        "passages": [{"text": t, "kind": "body"} for t in kv["passage"]],
-+++    }

-+++    nodes["nodes"].sort(key=lambda n: n["id"])

-+++    print(f"[✓] node upserted: {node['id']} ({len(nodes['nodes'])} curated)")
-+++
-+++
-+++def do_edge(kv: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
-+++    need = ("src", "dst", "rel")
-+++    for k in need:
-+++        if k not in kv:
-+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] --edge requires {'/'.join(need)}=… (missing {k})")
-+++    if kv["rel"][0] not in graph_store.EDGE_RELS:
-+++        raise SystemExit(f"[!] unknown rel {kv['rel'][0]!r}; "
-+++                         f"whitelist: {', '.join(graph_store.EDGE_RELS)}")
-+++    edge = {
-+++        "src": kv["src"][0],
-+++        "dst": kv["dst"][0],
-+++        "rel": kv["rel"][0],
-+++        "evidence": kv.get("evidence", ["agent-curated"])[0],
-+++    }
-+++    edges = read_json(CURATED / "edges.json", {"edges": []})
-+++    edges["edges"] = [e for e in edges["edges"]
-+++                      if (e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"])
-+++                      != (edge["src"], edge["dst"], edge["rel"])]
-+++    edges["edges"].append(edge)
-+++    edges["edges"].sort(key=lambda e: (e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"]))
-+++    write_json(CURATED / "edges.json", edges)
-+++    print(f"[✓] edge upserted: {edge['src']} --{edge['rel']}--> {edge['dst']}")
-+++
-+++
-+++def rebuild_with_rollback(store_out: Path) -> None:

-+++
-+++
-+++def main() -> int:
-+++    global CURATED
-+++    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
-+++    ap.add_argument("--node", nargs="+", metavar="KEY=VALUE",
-+++                    help="node fields: id type title passage [tag source]")
-+++    ap.add_argument("--edge", nargs="+", metavar="KEY=VALUE",
-+++                    help="edge fields: src dst rel [evidence]")

-+++                    help="list curated node ids + edges")
-+++    ap.add_argument("--no-rebuild", action="store_true",
-+++                    help="skip the store rebuild (rarely wanted)")

-+++    ap.add_argument("--store-out", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT,
-+++                    help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # test hook
-+++    args = ap.parse_args()
-+++
-+++    CURATED = args.curated
-+++
-+++    if args.list:
-+++        nodes = read_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", {"nodes": []})
-+++        edges = read_json(CURATED / "edges.json", {"edges": []})

-+++        for e in edges["edges"]:

-+++        return 0
-+++
-+++    if not args.node and not args.edge:

-+++
-+++    if args.node:
-+++        do_node(parse_kv(args.node))
-+++    if args.edge:
-+++        do_edge(parse_kv(args.edge))
-+++    if not args.no_rebuild:

-+++    return 0
-+++
-+++
-+++if __name__ == "__main__":
-+++    try:
-+++        raise SystemExit(main())
-+++    except BrokenPipeError:  # e.g. `write_memory.py --list | head`

-+++#!/usr/bin/env python3
-+++"""query_memory.py — RAG retrieval over the MultiTunnel agentic memory graph.
-+++
-+++Any agent (session start, subagent, future session) can pull relevant project
-+++memory with one command from the repo root:
-+++
-+++    python3 query_memory.py "saturation aware traffic split"
-+++    python3 query_memory.py "tray icon quick settings" --prompt
-+++    python3 query_memory.py "verification gates" -k 8 --json
-+++
-+++Retrieval = BM25 (lexical, title-boosted) + graph-neighborhood expansion
-+++(typed edges, 0.5^hop score decay). Modes:
-+++    default   ranked human-readable passages with sources + graph links
-+++    --json    structured results + induced subgraph (for programmatic agents)
-+++    --prompt  paste-ready RAG context pack (inject into any agent prompt)
-+++
-+++The store is rebuilt automatically if missing. It lives at
-+++harness/memory/store/memory_graph.json; rebuild it with
-+++`python3 harness/memory/build_graph.py` (also run by update_memory.py).
-+++"""
-+++
-+++from __future__ import annotations
-+++
-+++import argparse
-+++import json
-+++import subprocess
-+++import sys
-+++from pathlib import Path
-+++
-+++REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
-+++sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "harness" / "memory"))
-+++
-+++import graph_store  # noqa: E402
-+++from build_graph import DEFAULT_OUT  # noqa: E402
-+++
-+++
-+++def ensure_store(store_path: Path) -> dict:
-+++    if not store_path.exists():
-+++        print(f"[i] store missing — building {store_path}", file=sys.stderr)
-+++        subprocess.run(
-+++            [sys.executable, str(REPO / "harness" / "memory" / "build_graph.py")],
-+++            check=True)
-+++    return graph_store.load_store(store_path)
-+++
-+++
-+++def main() -> int:
-+++    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
-+++        description="RAG retrieval over the MultiTunnel memory graph")
-+++    ap.add_argument("query", help="what to look for (natural language or keywords)")
-+++    ap.add_argument("-k", type=int, default=5,
-+++                    help="top hits (default 5; neighbors may add more)")
-+++    ap.add_argument("--expand", type=int, default=1,
-+++                    help="graph expansion hops (default 1; 0 = BM25 only)")
-+++    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", dest="as_json",
-+++                    help="structured JSON output")
-+++    ap.add_argument("--prompt", action="store_true",
-+++                    help="paste-ready RAG context pack for a consuming agent")
-+++    ap.add_argument("--store", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT,
-+++                    help="store path (default: %(default)s)")
-+++    args = ap.parse_args()
-+++
-+++    store = ensure_store(args.store)
-+++    results = graph_store.retrieve(store, args.query, k=args.k,
-+++                                   expand=args.expand)
-+++
-+++    if args.as_json:
-+++        ids = [r["node"] for r in results]
-+++        print(json.dumps({
-+++            "query": args.query,
-+++            "k": args.k,
-+++            "expand": args.expand,
-+++            "as_of": store.get("as_of"),
-+++            "results": results,
-+++            "subgraph": graph_store.induced_subgraph(store, set(ids)),
-+++        }, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
-+++    elif args.prompt:
-+++        print(graph_store.format_prompt(args.query, results, store))
-+++    else:
-+++        print(graph_store.format_human(args.query, results))
-+++    return 0
-+++
-+++
-+++if __name__ == "__main__":
-+++    raise SystemExit(main())

-+++    #[test]
-+++    fn would_overflow_mirrors_the_insert_boundary() {
-+++        // S14: the endpoint's backpressure path polls would_overflow BEFORE
-+++        // inserting — it must agree exactly with insert's Overflow check.
-+++        let mut rb = ReorderBuffer::new(16);
-+++        assert!(rb.insert(5, vec![0u8; 10]).is_ok());
-+++        assert!(!rb.would_overflow(6), "10 + 6 == cap 16 fits");
-+++        assert!(rb.would_overflow(7), "10 + 7 > cap 16 overflows");
-+++        // An insert that would_overflow rejects must be the same size that
-+++        // insert() errors on — the pause loop's invariant.
-+++        let probe = vec![0u8; 7];
-+++        assert_eq!(rb.would_overflow(probe.len()), rb.insert(6, probe).is_err());
-+++        assert_eq!(rb.buffered_bytes(), 10, "rejected insert left state intact");
-+++        // Once the gap ahead of seq 5 drains (in-order 0..=4 flushes the
-+++        // buffered 5), the previously-rejected frame fits — the backpressure
-+++        // pause resolves instead of erroring.
-+++        for seq in 0..5u64 {
-+++            assert!(rb.insert(seq, vec![0u8; 4]).is_ok());
-+++        }
-+++        assert_eq!(rb.buffered_bytes(), 0, "seq 5 flushed by the 0..=4 run");
-+++        assert!(!rb.would_overflow(7));
-+++        assert!(rb.insert(6, vec![0u8; 7]).is_ok());
-+++    }
-++ }

--## Scheduling & bonding modes (v0.7) — even spreading and adapter priority
-+## Scheduling & bonding modes (v0.7/v0.8) — even spreading and adapter priority
- 
- The merge policy picks which bonded adapter carries each NEW connection
- (Settings → Network), and — in stream mode — how every connection's BYTES
- are striped across the carriers:
- 
--- `balanced` (default, v0.7) — each new connection goes to the adapter
--  carrying the least traffic RIGHT NOW (a 1 s byte-rate estimate plus a
--  small per-connection reserve). A fat download stops hogging one NIC and
--  the spread evens out by BYTES, not by connection count. With three or
--  more adapters this is the fix for "one adapter carries almost
--  everything, the last one rarely sees traffic".
-+- `balanced` (default, v0.7; capacity-aware in v0.8) — each new
-+  connection goes to the adapter carrying the least traffic RIGHT NOW
-+  (a 1 s byte-rate estimate plus a small per-connection reserve). A fat
-+  download stops hogging one NIC and the spread evens out by BYTES, not
-+  by connection count. With three or more adapters this is the fix for
-+  "one adapter carries almost everything, the last one rarely sees
-+  traffic".
- - `round-robin` — connections alternate across every ticked adapter;
-   even by connection count, not by bytes (one big flow still dominates
-   its adapter).
--- `priority` (v0.7) — adapters fill in the priority order you set on the
--  Adapters tab (↑/↓, or tick to append): adapter #1 takes everything
--  until its measured bandwidth saturates (a ramp/plateau detector on its
--  live rate), then the overflow spills to #2, and so on. When #1's load
--  drops, it takes the traffic back automatically.
-+- `priority` (v0.7; capacity-aware in v0.8) — adapters fill in the
-+  priority order you set on the Adapters tab (↑/↓, or tick to append):
-+  adapter #1 takes everything until its measured bandwidth saturates,
-+  then the overflow spills to #2, and so on. When #1's load drops, it
-+  takes the traffic back automatically.
- - `lowest-latency` — each connection takes the adapter with the best
-   smoothed (EWMA) RTT.
- - `failover` — everything rides the first healthy adapter; the others
-   stay idle until it dies.
- 
- In stream bonding mode the same policy drives the frame scheduler:
--`balanced` sends each frame down the carrier with the least writer
--backpressure (fast NICs naturally take more), `priority` fills carriers
--in the Adapters-tab order until one backs up. Upgrading from v0.6.x? The
--stock `round-robin` setting migrates to `balanced` once; an explicit

-+`balanced` sends each frame down the carrier with the least RELATIVE
-+load, `priority` fills carriers in the Adapters-tab order until one
-+saturates. Upgrading from v0.6.x? The stock `round-robin` setting
-+migrates to `balanced` once; an explicit re-choice of `round-robin`
-+persists.
-+
-+### Saturation-aware spreading (v0.8) — when one adapter maxes out
-+
-+v0.7 measured saturation indirectly (byte counters, writer-queue
-+backpressure). v0.8 measures it DIRECTLY: every second each carrier's
-+PING carries a report of how many bytes/s that path actually DELIVERED,
-+and both ends compare it with what they OFFERED (an EWMA on each side).
-+The score is relative load — offered ÷ delivered:
-+
-+- `balanced` picks the carrier with the LOWEST score, so a Wi-Fi link
-+  pinned at its ceiling (offered 1.6 MiB/s, delivered 1.0) immediately
-+  loses the next frames to the Ethernet link with headroom. Spreading
-+  is proportional to capacity: a 10:1 bandwidth mismatch yields ~10:1
-+  byte shares, not a 50/50 split that just overflows the slow path.
-+- `priority` keeps filling adapter #1 until its score crosses 1.15
-+  (offered ≥ 15% over delivered) or its writer queue backs up — then it
-+  spills to #2, and takes the traffic back the moment #1's score drops
-+  again.
-+- A carrier with no report yet (fresh, or an older peer) is probed at
-+  32 KiB/s instead of looking free, so unknown paths earn trust before
-+  they attract load — and a dead path that never reports never wins a
-+  frame.
-+
-+This is the fix for "when one adapter reaches its maximum bandwidth, the
-+rest of the traffic does not split over to the remaining adapters":
-+saturation is now measured per-path, per-second, at both ends.
- 
- To use **every adapter for a single connection at the same time**, set
- bonding mode to `stream` (Advanced): the bytes of every connection are

-+---## Scheduling & bonding modes (v0.6) — beyond round-robin
-+--+## Scheduling & bonding modes (v0.7) — even spreading and adapter priority
-+-- 
-+-- The merge policy picks which bonded adapter carries each NEW connection
-+---(Advanced tab):
-+---
-+---- `round-robin` (default) — connections alternate across every ticked
-+---  adapter; both NICs carry traffic.
-+--+(Settings → Network), and — in stream mode — how every connection's BYTES
-+--+are striped across the carriers:
-+--+
-+--+- `balanced` (default, v0.7) — each new connection goes to the adapter
-+--+  carrying the least traffic RIGHT NOW (a 1 s byte-rate estimate plus a
-+--+  small per-connection reserve). A fat download stops hogging one NIC and
-+--+  the spread evens out by BYTES, not by connection count. With three or
-+--+  more adapters this is the fix for "one adapter carries almost
-+--+  everything, the last one rarely sees traffic".
-+--+- `round-robin` — connections alternate across every ticked adapter;
-+--+  even by connection count, not by bytes (one big flow still dominates
-+--+  its adapter).
-+--+- `priority` (v0.7) — adapters fill in the priority order you set on the
-+--+  Adapters tab (↑/↓, or tick to append): adapter #1 takes everything
-+--+  until its measured bandwidth saturates (a ramp/plateau detector on its
-+--+  live rate), then the overflow spills to #2, and so on. When #1's load
-+--+  drops, it takes the traffic back automatically.
-+-- - `lowest-latency` — each connection takes the adapter with the best
-+---  smoothed (EWMA) RTT, so the faster link naturally takes more
-+---  connections than a blind alternation. (v0.6 also fixes the policy
-+---  parser: the GUI's hyphenated names were silently falling back to
-+---  round-robin before.)
-+---- `failover` — everything rides the first healthy adapter; the second
-+---  stays idle until it dies.
-+---
-+---To use **both adapters for a single connection at the same time**, set
-+--+  smoothed (EWMA) RTT.
-+--+- `failover` — everything rides the first healthy adapter; the others
-+--+  stay idle until it dies.
-+--+
-+--+In stream bonding mode the same policy drives the frame scheduler:
-+--+`balanced` sends each frame down the carrier with the least writer
-+--+backpressure (fast NICs naturally take more), `priority` fills carriers
-+--+in the Adapters-tab order until one backs up. Upgrading from v0.6.x? The
-+--+stock `round-robin` setting migrates to `balanced` once; an explicit
-+--+re-choice of `round-robin` persists.
-+--+
-+--+To use **every adapter for a single connection at the same time**, set
-+-- bonding mode to `stream` (Advanced): the bytes of every connection are
-+-- split across all ticked adapters and re-merged by `mt-merge-server` on
-+-- the tunnel server — see "Stream bonding (v0.5)" above.

-+-++- **What**: MultiTunnel — Rust rewrite of BondTunnel; zero-dependency all-in-one
-+-++  (v2rayN import + net-merge), Material You GUI. Repo: github.com/maniesh-NR/MultiTunnel.
-+-++- **Data path**: Windows client → local SOCKS/HTTP → ProxyServer → BondOutbound
-+-++  → N carriers (one per bonded NIC, VLESS+REALITY via Xray `sendThrough`,
-+-++  engine self-provisioned D14) → VM Xray (public 8443) → freedom → mt-merge-server
-+-++  (127.0.0.1:7443) → real target. Reverse symmetric. Auth at the Xray edge.
-+-++- **Two bond modes**: per-connection (default) and stream bonding (D17 framing,
-+-++  needs the VM merge daemon; carriers verified by PING/PONG before schedulable).
-+-++- **Scheduling (D23, v0.7.0)**: five merge policies in mt-net — round-robin,
-+-++  failover, lowest-latency (EWMA), **balanced** (stock default; pressure =
-+-++  rate_bps + active_conns × 128 KiB/s reserve), **priority** (user order; #1
-+-++  fills until bandwidth plateaus (ramp detector, ≥3 flat ticks + rate ≥ 0.85 ×
-+-++  capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s), then spills). Stream-mode frame scheduler is
-+-++  policy-aware too (least writer backpressure / 512 KiB queue high-water).
-+-++  Adapter priority == saved `bonded_adapters` ORDER; Adapters tab = ordering UI
-+-++  (selected rows first, #n chips, ↑/↓).
-+-++- **Crates**: mt-net (proxy servers, merge, policy), mt-bond (stream framing,
-+-++  carrier scheduling, daemon), mt-engine (ManagedEngine lifecycle),
-+-++  mt-links (vless:// + subscriptions), mt-platform (Win32 adapter FFI),
-+-++  mt-service (service trait + real_service), mt-m3 + mt-app (Material You GUI,
-+-++  iced). Root crate = CLI binaries (multitunnel, tray, mt-app).
-+-++- **Hard rules**: config schema camelCase + versioned migrations (D8); no
-+-++  secrets in repo (D9) — token lives in ../upload/, backup.sh reads it;
-+-++  fail-open routing (D5); GUI never dies invisibly (D15); vendored iced under
-+-++  `vendor/` + `[patch.crates-io]` (D21) — upstream 0.13.0 has 4 patched bugs
-+-++  (damage NaN total-order, clip mapping, fill_text bounds, HiDPI transform
-+-++  order); CI timestamps UTC; rustc 1.100.0 + zig 0.14.1 + cargo-zigbuild
-+-++  (D2), windows target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.

-+--+/// A carrier whose writer queue exceeds this many BYTES counts as
-+--+/// SATURATED for the `Priority` policy — its socket provably cannot keep

-+--+/// carrier hovers near zero, a bottlenecked one grows without bound, so
-+--+/// the spill decision lands within a fraction of a second at any real
-+--+/// rate difference.
-+--+pub const PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER: u64 = 512 * 1024;

-+--+/// Pure carrier pick (the D17 round-robin, made policy-aware in S11).
-+--+/// Returns the SLOT INDEX to send the next frame on:
-+--+/// - `Failover`       — first live carrier (idx order).
-+--+/// - `RoundRobin`     — rotate over live carriers (cursor).
-+--+/// - `LowestLatency`  — best sampled RTT (known beats unknown, ties keep
-+--+///   the earlier carrier).
-+--+/// - `Balanced`       — least queued bytes; ties rotate via the cursor.
-+--+///   A fast adapter drains its queue quicker and naturally takes more
-+--+///   frames — capacity-proportional even spreading.
-+--+/// - `Priority`       — first carrier in USER ORDER whose queue is under
-+--+///   [`PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER`]; when every carrier backs up, the
-+--+///   least-queued one takes the excess.
-+--+fn pick_carrier_index(
-+--+    policy: mt_net::MergePolicy,
-+--+    slots: &[CarrierSlot],
-+--+    cursor: &mut u64,
-+--+) -> Option<usize> {
-+--+    if slots.is_empty() {
-+--+        return None;
-+--+    }
-+--+    match policy {
-+--+        mt_net::MergePolicy::Failover => Some(slots[0].idx),
-+--+        mt_net::MergePolicy::RoundRobin => {
-+--+            let s = slots[(*cursor % slots.len() as u64) as usize];
-+--+            *cursor = cursor.wrapping_add(1);
-+--+            Some(s.idx)
-+--+        }
-+--+        mt_net::MergePolicy::LowestLatency => {
-+--+            let mut best = 0;
-+--+            for i in 1..slots.len() {
-+--+                let (b, c) = (slots[best], slots[i]);
-+--+                let b_known = b.rtt_ms > 0;
-+--+                let c_known = c.rtt_ms > 0;
-+--+                if (c_known && !b_known) || (c_known == b_known && c.rtt_ms < b.rtt_ms) {
-+--+                    best = i;
-+--+                }
-+--+            }
-+--+            Some(slots[best].idx)
-+--+        }
-+--+        mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced => {
-+--+            let min = slots.iter().map(|s| s.queued).min().expect("non-empty");
-+--+            let tied: Vec<usize> = (0..slots.len())
-+--+                .filter(|&i| slots[i].queued == min)
-+--+                .collect();
-+--+            let pick = tied[(*cursor % tied.len() as u64) as usize];
-+--+            *cursor = cursor.wrapping_add(1);
-+--+            Some(slots[pick].idx)
-+--+        }
-+--+        mt_net::MergePolicy::Priority => {
-+--+            for s in slots {
-+--+                if s.queued < PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER {
-+--+                    return Some(s.idx);
-+--+                }
-+--+            }
-+--+            slots.iter().min_by_key(|s| s.queued).map(|s| s.idx) // every carrier backs up → least queued
-+--+        }
-+--+    }
-+--+}

-+-++-## Scheduling & bonding modes (v0.6) — beyond round-robin
-+-+++## Scheduling & bonding modes (v0.7) — even spreading and adapter priority
-+-++ 
-+-++ The merge policy picks which bonded adapter carries each NEW connection
-+-++-(Advanced tab):
-+-++-
-+-++-- `round-robin` (default) — connections alternate across every ticked
-+-++-  adapter; both NICs carry traffic.
-+-+++(Settings → Network), and — in stream mode — how every connection's BYTES
-+-+++are striped across the carriers:
-+-+++
-+-+++- `balanced` (default, v0.7) — each new connection goes to the adapter
-+-+++  carrying the least traffic RIGHT NOW (a 1 s byte-rate estimate plus a
-+-+++  small per-connection reserve). A fat download stops hogging one NIC and
-+-+++  the spread evens out by BYTES, not by connection count. With three or
-+-+++  more adapters this is the fix for "one adapter carries almost
-+-+++  everything, the last one rarely sees traffic".
-+-+++- `round-robin` — connections alternate across every ticked adapter;
-+-+++  even by connection count, not by bytes (one big flow still dominates
-+-+++  its adapter).
-+-+++- `priority` (v0.7) — adapters fill in the priority order you set on the
-+-+++  Adapters tab (↑/↓, or tick to append): adapter #1 takes everything
-+-+++  until its measured bandwidth saturates (a ramp/plateau detector on its
-+-+++  live rate), then the overflow spills to #2, and so on. When #1's load
-+-+++  drops, it takes the traffic back automatically.
-+-++ - `lowest-latency` — each connection takes the adapter with the best
-+-++-  smoothed (EWMA) RTT, so the faster link naturally takes more
-+-++-  connections than a blind alternation. (v0.6 also fixes the policy
-+-++-  parser: the GUI's hyphenated names were silently falling back to
-+-++-  round-robin before.)
-+-++-- `failover` — everything rides the first healthy adapter; the second
-+-++-  stays idle until it dies.
-+-++-
-+-++-To use **both adapters for a single connection at the same time**, set
-+-+++  smoothed (EWMA) RTT.
-+-+++- `failover` — everything rides the first healthy adapter; the others
-+-+++  stay idle until it dies.
-+-+++
-+-+++In stream bonding mode the same policy drives the frame scheduler:
-+-+++`balanced` sends each frame down the carrier with the least writer
-+-+++backpressure (fast NICs naturally take more), `priority` fills carriers
-+-+++in the Adapters-tab order until one backs up. Upgrading from v0.6.x? The
-+-+++stock `round-robin` setting migrates to `balanced` once; an explicit
-+-+++re-choice of `round-robin` persists.
-+-+++
-+-+++To use **every adapter for a single connection at the same time**, set
-+-++ bonding mode to `stream` (Advanced): the bytes of every connection are
-+-++ split across all ticked adapters and re-merged by `mt-merge-server` on
-+-++ the tunnel server — see "Stream bonding (v0.5)" above.

-+-+++// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-+-+++// S11 carrier scheduling (pure)
-+-+++// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-+-+++
-+-+++/// Scheduler snapshot of one LIVE carrier (the pure picker's input).
-+-+++#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
-+-+++struct CarrierSlot {
-+-+++    /// Carrier slot index == link index == the user's adapter priority
-+-+++    /// order (links are built one per bonded adapter, in settings order).
-+-+++    idx: usize,
-+-+++    /// Bytes queued for the socket writer (the live backpressure).
-+-+++    queued: u64,
-+-+++    /// Last PING round trip in ms (0 = no sample yet).
-+-+++    rtt_ms: u32,
-+-+++}
-+-+++
-+-+++/// A carrier whose writer queue exceeds this many BYTES counts as
-+-+++/// SATURATED for the `Priority` policy — its socket provably cannot keep
-+-+++/// up with the offered rate. 512 KiB ≈ 8 max-size frames: a healthy
-+-+++/// carrier hovers near zero, a bottlenecked one grows without bound, so
-+-+++/// the spill decision lands within a fraction of a second at any real
-+-+++/// rate difference.
-+-+++pub const PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER: u64 = 512 * 1024;
-+-+++
-+-+++/// Pure carrier pick (the D17 round-robin, made policy-aware in S11).
-+-+++/// Returns the SLOT INDEX to send the next frame on:
-+-+++/// - `Failover`       — first live carrier (idx order).
-+-+++/// - `RoundRobin`     — rotate over live carriers (cursor).
-+-+++/// - `LowestLatency`  — best sampled RTT (known beats unknown, ties keep
-+-+++///   the earlier carrier).
-+-+++/// - `Balanced`       — least queued bytes; ties rotate via the cursor.
-+-+++///   A fast adapter drains its queue quicker and naturally takes more
-+-+++///   frames — capacity-proportional even spreading.
-+-+++/// - `Priority`       — first carrier in USER ORDER whose queue is under
-+-+++///   [`PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER`]; when every carrier backs up, the
-+-+++///   least-queued one takes the excess.
-+-+++fn pick_carrier_index(
-+-+++    policy: mt_net::MergePolicy,
-+-+++    slots: &[CarrierSlot],
-+-+++    cursor: &mut u64,
-+-+++) -> Option<usize> {
-+-+++    if slots.is_empty() {
-+-+++        return None;
-+-+++    }
-+-+++    match policy {
-+-+++        mt_net::MergePolicy::Failover => Some(slots[0].idx),
-+-+++        mt_net::MergePolicy::RoundRobin => {
-+-+++            let s = slots[(*cursor % slots.len() as u64) as usize];
-+-+++            *cursor = cursor.wrapping_add(1);
-+-+++            Some(s.idx)
-+-+++        }
-+-+++        mt_net::MergePolicy::LowestLatency => {
-+-+++            let mut best = 0;
-+-+++            for i in 1..slots.len() {
-+-+++                let (b, c) = (slots[best], slots[i]);
-+-+++                let b_known = b.rtt_ms > 0;
-+-+++                let c_known = c.rtt_ms > 0;
-+-+++                if (c_known && !b_known) || (c_known == b_known && c.rtt_ms < b.rtt_ms) {
-+-+++                    best = i;
-+-+++                }
-+-+++            }
-+-+++            Some(slots[best].idx)
-+-+++        }
-+-+++        mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced => {
-+-+++            let min = slots.iter().map(|s| s.queued).min().expect("non-empty");
-+-+++            let tied: Vec<usize> = (0..slots.len())
-+-+++                .filter(|&i| slots[i].queued == min)
-+-+++                .collect();
-+-+++            let pick = tied[(*cursor % tied.len() as u64) as usize];
-+-+++            *cursor = cursor.wrapping_add(1);
-+-+++            Some(slots[pick].idx)
-+-+++        }
-+-+++        mt_net::MergePolicy::Priority => {
-+-+++            for s in slots {
-+-+++                if s.queued < PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER {
-+-+++                    return Some(s.idx);
-+-+++                }
-+-+++            }
-+-+++            slots.iter().min_by_key(|s| s.queued).map(|s| s.idx) // every carrier backs up → least queued
-+-+++        }
-+-+++    }
-+-+++}

-+-+++mod scheduling_tests {
-+-+++    use super::*;
-+-+++
-+-+++    fn slot(idx: usize, queued: u64, rtt_ms: u32) -> CarrierSlot {
-+-+++        CarrierSlot {
-+-+++            idx,
-+-+++            queued,
-+-+++            rtt_ms,
-+-+++        }
-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    fn pick1(policy: mt_net::MergePolicy, slots: &[CarrierSlot]) -> Option<usize> {
-+-+++        let mut cursor = 0u64;
-+-+++        pick_carrier_index(policy, slots, &mut cursor)
-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    #[test]
-+-+++    fn failover_takes_the_first_live_carrier() {
-+-+++        let slots = [slot(0, 900_000, 0), slot(1, 0, 0), slot(2, 0, 0)];
-+-+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Failover, &slots), Some(0));
-+-+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Failover, &[]), None);
-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    #[test]
-+-+++    fn round_robin_cycles_the_cursor() {
-+-+++        let slots = [slot(0, 0, 0), slot(1, 0, 0), slot(2, 0, 0)];
-+-+++        let mut cursor = 0u64;
-+-+++        let seq: Vec<usize> = (0..4)
-+-+++            .map(|_| {
-+-+++                pick_carrier_index(mt_net::MergePolicy::RoundRobin, &slots, &mut cursor).unwrap()
-+-+++            })
-+-+++            .collect();
-+-+++        assert_eq!(seq, vec![0, 1, 2, 0]);
-+-+++        assert_eq!(cursor, 4);
-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    #[test]
-+-+++    fn lowest_latency_prefers_sampled_rtt_then_known_over_unknown() {
-+-+++        // Fastest sampled carrier wins.
-+-+++        let slots = [slot(0, 0, 120), slot(1, 0, 0), slot(2, 0, 45)];
-+-+++        assert_eq!(
-+-+++            pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::LowestLatency, &slots),
-+-+++            Some(2),
-+-+++            "known 45 ms beats unknown and known 120 ms"
-+-+++        );
-+-+++        // A sample beats no sample (0 = not yet measured).
-+-+++        let unknowns = [slot(0, 0, 0), slot(1, 0, 300)];
-+-+++        assert_eq!(
-+-+++            pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::LowestLatency, &unknowns),
-+-+++            Some(1)
-+-+++        );
-+-+++        // All unknown → first.
-+-+++        let all_unknown = [slot(0, 0, 0), slot(1, 0, 0)];
-+-+++        assert_eq!(
-+-+++            pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::LowestLatency, &all_unknown),
-+-+++            Some(0)
-+-+++        );
-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    #[test]
-+-+++    fn balanced_picks_the_least_backlogged_carrier() {
-+-+++        // The user's exact complaint shape: one adapter carries the fat
-+-+++        // flow (deep queue), the others are nearly drained.
-+-+++        let slots = [

-+-+++            slot(1, 120_000, 40),
-+-+++            slot(2, 5_000, 55),
-+-+++        ];
-+-+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots), Some(2));
-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    #[test]

-+-+++        let slots = [slot(0, 0, 0), slot(1, 0, 0), slot(2, 0, 0)];
-+-+++        let mut cursor = 0u64;
-+-+++        let seq: Vec<usize> = (0..3)
-+-+++            .map(|_| {
-+-+++                pick_carrier_index(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots, &mut cursor).unwrap()
-+-+++            })
-+-+++            .collect();

-+-+++    }
-+-+++
-+-+++    #[test]
-+-+++    fn priority_fills_in_order_until_the_queue_backs_up() {
-+-+++        // Everything below the high-water mark rides carrier 0.
-+-+++        let healthy = [slot(0, 100_000, 30), slot(1, 0, 40), slot(2, 0, 55)];

-+-+++/// Advance one link's load estimate by one tick (pure; unit-tested).

-+-+++/// * `dt` — the tick's wall length (rate = delta/dt).
