-++      "id": "decision:D1",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D1 — Rust instead of Go (user directive, 2026-11-12)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D1"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "The Go prototype is superseded. All production code is Rust. Design contracts (mux off, loopback inbounds, ordering, fail-open) carry over unchanged.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D10",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D10 — vless:// importer is REALITY-only and strict (2026-11-17)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D10"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "MultiTunnel generates exactly one protocol shape (xrayconf: VLESS/TCP/ REALITY/xtls-rprx-vision, chrome fp, spiderX /). `multitunnel import` therefore accepts only links it can faithfully represent: security=reality, type=tcp, flow absent or xtls-rprx-vision; uuid 8-4-4-4-12 hex; pbk exactly 43 unpadded base64url chars; sid empty or 1-16 hex. Unknown query params are ignored (other clients append extras such as headerType, path, alpn, allowInsecure). No percent-decoding of stored fields (uuid/host/port/sni/ pbk/sid never carry escapes; the remark fragment is display-only, not stored). Error messages never echo uuid/pbk values (D9). config.json is patched as RAW JSON — only the server block is replaced — so user-customized ports/paths/behavior survive and relative paths are not re-rooted by a resolve() round-trip. Writes go through write_private (fsutil atomic, S5). Missing config → template first, then patch. (Feature built on a stale-tree session and salvaged onto the frontier after the 7th rollback.)",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D11",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D11 — All-in-One pivot (user directive, 2026-11-17)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D11"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "v0.3 north star: one app, zero user-installed dependencies, v2rayN + net-merge functions out of the box, Material You GUI, Rust core. The user never manually installs an Xray core or net-merge: the engine is located, verified, downloaded (or embedded at build time) by mt-platform; link spreading moves in-process into mt-net. The managed Xray engine remains the REALITY specialist until S7's native port (stock rustls cannot do the REALITY ClientHello auth; a faithful port needs a custom TLS 1.3 stack — tracked, not rushed).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D12",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D12 — S6 execution: Mixture of Experts + strangler workspace (2026-11-17)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D12"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "Stage S6 runs as parallel expert agents, one crate each (mt-links, mt-net, mt-engine, mt-m3, mt-platform; then mt-app), contracts frozen in harness/CONTRACTS-S6.md; the orchestrator owns the workspace root, wiring and integration. The root package keeps v0.2 behavior green at EVERY commit (branch protection requires green CI on main pushes) — new code lands beside it in crates/, migration of root modules happens gradually.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D13",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D13 — GUI: iced + mt-m3 Material You system (2026-11-17)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D13"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "iced 0.13 (MIT, pure Rust, no system webview — keeps the zero-dependency promise) with a hand-built Material Design 3 token system (mt-m3: dynamic color from a seed, light/dark, type scale, shape, state layers). The existing raw-win32 tray stays (D4) as the always-running companion; the iced window app (mt-app) is the full v2rayN-class GUI. Prefer the tiny-skia renderer for cross-compile robustness.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D14",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D14 — Engine self-provisioning, never silent (2026-11-17)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D14"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "Engine resolution order: $MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE → exe-dir/engine → config-dir/engine (sha256-verified against SHA256SUMS; strict mode refuses mismatch) → build-time embedded zip (MT_EMBED_ENGINE) → explicit user-triggered download (GitHub latest, URL overridable). `locate()` never downloads; only `ensure()` may, and the GUI/CLI surfaces it.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D15",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D15 — Bare launch = GUI; a GUI app never dies invisibly (2026-11-18)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D15"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User report on the v0.3.0 release: \"multitunnel.exe does not show a GUI when opened. There does not appear to be any launch activity.\" Root cause: the no-args default was the `tray` command, which only printed a pointer to the separate multitunnel-tray.exe and exited 1 — a console-subsystem double-click flashes a console for a fraction of a second. The build was never broken; the product's front door was. v0.3.1 rules: 1. Bare launch defaults to `gui` (`command_from`, regression-tested). 2. Windows console policy (`console_mode`): a console-subsystem GUI launch detaches its console via FreeConsole ONLY when the process is the sole console user (GetConsoleProcessList == 1 — Explorer double-click, autostart Run key, `start`); a terminal launch shares the console and keeps it. Call failures conservatively read as \"shared\" — never detach a console we might share. Side effect: the parked C-P2-10 autostart concern is largely resolved (autostarted console exe now opens the GUI with no lingering console). 3. Never-die-invisibly: GUI launch errors surface as a MessageBoxW when no shared console exists (`alert_error`), and a panic hook (`install_panic_dialog_hook`) shows panics the same way in flash-death processes. stderr remains the primary channel whenever a console survives the process. 4. `gui_args()`: the `gui` dispatch arm must accept an EMPTY argv tail — `&cmd_args[1..]` panicked on the bare launch (a hidden precondition the v0.3.0 `tray` default masked). Caught only by running the host binary bare: unit tests and `gui --smoke` never exercise empty-argv dispatch.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D16",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D16 — Adapter bonding via per-adapter engines + Xray `sendThrough` (S8, 2026-11-18)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D16"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User report: \"There is no menu to select the network adapters that are being bonded for the vless connection.\" Root cause: the merge aggregator, policies and probers existed, but `EngineLinkFactory` built exactly ONE unbound engine — bonding had no adapter surface at all. S8 rules: 1. Enumeration lives in mt-platform (`adapters` module): Windows `GetAdaptersAddresses` FFI (windows-sys, AF_INET, loopback excluded, buffer-retry, 16 MiB cap, fail-open to an empty vec); non-Windows is a pure-std /proc+/sys dev path (IPv4 attribution documented-limited). `NetAdapter.id` = the stable machine id (Windows ANSI AdapterName GUID / Linux ifname) — settings persist IDS, never display names. 2. Binding model: ONE `ManagedEngine` per selected adapter, its Xray config carrying `\"sendThrough\": <adapter IPv4>` (top-level outbound field; Windows source-address binding selects the egress interface). Engine tags embed the adapter name (`\"profile [Wi-Fi]\"`, deduplicated) so config/log files never collide; each engine keeps its own ephemeral loopback SOCKS port. Mux stays OFF — the aggregator spreads individual TCP connections across the per-adapter links (net-merge model). 3. Selection is id-validated (`set_bonded_adapters` rejects unknown ids), persisted in `settings.json` (`SettingsView.bonded_adapters`, `#[serde(default)]` so v0.3 files load), and applied on the NEXT connect; a live session is restarted immediately on Apply. Unknown ids or IPv4-less adapters at connect time are SKIPPED with a warning (fail-open — an unplugged USB modem must not black-hole the tunnel). 4.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D17",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D17 — Stream bonding protocol (S9, 2026-11-18): mt-bond framing over N REALITY carriers",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D17"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User want: one logical connection, bytes split across the bonded adapters, re-merged at the server; reverse symmetric. Design: 1. TRANSPORT: each adapter keeps its per-adapter engine (D16); a CARRIER is one long-lived connection dialed through one engine whose VLESS target is `127.0.0.1:<merge_port>` ON THE SERVER — server Xray (freedom) pipes it to the `mt-merge-server` daemon. REALITY/vision unchanged per carrier. 2. FRAMING: fixed 24-byte little-endian header (magic 0x4D54, version 1, kind, bond_id u32, session u32, seq u64, len u32) + payload; kinds HELLO/OPEN/DATA/CLOSE/ACK/PING/PONG; DATA ≤ 16 KiB. Carriers are plain byte streams — framing is end-to-end between client bond engine and the daemon, invisible to Xray. 3. RELIABILITY: per-session cumulative ACKs; sender keeps unacked frames; carrier death (write err / EOF / pong timeout) replays unacked frames on live carriers; receiver reorders (drop dupes, buffer gaps, stall-close at 10 s). Backpressure is TCP-native: bounded demux channels → reader blocks → carrier socket buffers fill → sender stalls (no windowing protocol). 4. SCHEDULING: round-robin across live carriers (predictable even split — exactly what the user asked); per-carrier PING RTT EWMA powers health + the Status rows; weighted scheduling is future work. 5. FALLBACK: `bond_mode=stream` with <2 usable carriers → per-connection mode + LogLine (never black-hole). 6. DAEMON: loopback-only (127.0.0.1) — authentication is REALITY+UUID at the Xray edge; no extra secret in v0.5, documented.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D18",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D18 — Exit probe: plain HTTP inside the tunnel (S9, 2026-11-18)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D18"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "`exit_probe()` rides the LIVE session: SOCKS CONNECT (through the local listener) to `ip-api.com:80` + hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 GET, parse {query,country,city,isp,as}. Plain HTTP is deliberate: the client→server leg is REALITY-encrypted, and the last hop carries only the echo payload — no TLS stack enters the tree (zero-dep rule). The Status card compares the measured exit against the profile endpoint and calls out mismatches (the GCP-VM-VPN-egress case: exit ISP ≠ Google → server-side egress explanation, NOT a hidden MultiTunnel hop).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D19",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D19 — Status tab becomes a live dashboard (S9, 2026-11-18)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D19"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "1. Bandwidth graph = iced canvas, 120 s ring of (up_bps, down_bps) 1 s samples from ProxyEvent::Tick; Fill-sized (grows with the window, Task Manager style); auto-scaled axes; theme-aware; down=primary, up=tertiary. 2. Server picker = pick_list over profile tags; changing it while connected = set_active + automatic reconnect. 3. Status screen leaves the global scrollable (fixed state card + graph Fill + links scrollable) so the graph can scale with the window.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D2",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D2 — Cross-compilation via zig + cargo-zigbuild",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D2"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "No root in the sandbox (sudo needs a password) → apt gcc-mingw-w64 impossible. Chosen: zig 0.17.x as linker driver via cargo-zigbuild, target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, toolchains rooted under /home/z/my-project/tools/. CI (release.yml) builds MSVC natively on windows-latest for official releases; local zigbuild is the sandbox fallback and cross-check. REINSTALL RECIPE (used twice already — keep for next recycle): 1. curl rustup-init from static.rust-lang.org (direct binary, NOT curl|sh), run with RUSTUP_HOME=/home/z/my-project/tools/rustup CARGO_HOME=/home/z/my-project/tools/cargo -y --profile minimal --default-toolchain stable --no-modify-path 2. rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu 3. zig tarball from ziglang.org/download/index.json (pick newest stable, key containing 'linux' and 'x86_64') → extract to tools/zig 4. cargo install -q cargo-zigbuild 5. write tools/env.sh exporting RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, PATH(+zig)",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D20",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D20 — v0.5.1: visibility fixes driven by the first real two-adapter run (S9.1, 2026-11-18)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D20"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User report on v0.5.0 with Ethernet+Wi-Fi ticked: (1) all traffic rode Ethernet only; (2) the Status graph never appeared; (3) wanted one combined color-coded graph + per-interface graphs under an arrow.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "1. GRAPH COORDINATES: iced 0.13's Canvas draws through `renderer.with_translation(bounds.x, bounds.y)` — a Program's frame is in LOCAL space. v0.5.0's RateGraph computed every point from `bounds.x/y`, double-offsetting the plot outside the card (invisible, \"graph does not load\"). Fix: draw into `Rectangle::new(ORIGIN, bounds.size())`; regression test pins points inside the local rect for a realistically-offset widget rect. Unit tests never caught it because they used origin bounds. LESSON: a canvas program's helpers should never see widget-space coordinates at all. 2. MERGE POLICY DEFAULT: v0.5.0 shipped `merge_policy = \"failover\"`, and Failover always picks the FIRST healthy link — with Ethernet enumerated first, Wi-Fi stayed idle until Ethernet died. Users read that as broken bonding (it is failover semantics). v0.5.1: default round-robin (connections alternate), unknown-string fallback also round-robin, and a `settings_version` field (default 0 = v0.5.0 file) migrates the STOCK failover value to round-robin on load (best-effort persist). An explicit failover on a version>=1 file is respected verbatim — the migration is once, ever. 3. CARRIER VISIBILITY: ensure_carriers now returns a CarrierReport {live, lines} — one human line per link (\"live\" / \"down (reason)\") — and connect_flow emits them as ServiceEvent::LogLine so the GUI log shows per-carrier verdicts; <all-live emits a WARN with the share semantics. Skipped bonded adapters (absent / no IPv4 at connect) also LogLine (were tracing-only).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D21",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D21 — S10: rendering fixes as vendored iced patches + exclusions import",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D21"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User report: graphs occasionally out of frame / not loading; exclusions import like v2rayN; better-than-round-robin scheduling; \"Check exit IP\" panics on a non-total comparator.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "1. VENDORED ICED PATCHES over an iced upgrade: iced_graphics and iced_tiny_skia are at their TERMINAL 0.13.0 releases (no 0.13.x patch line exists), and 0.14/1.0 is a breaking migration. The three defects (local-vs-absolute clip space in damage + render mask; INFINITY marker bounds on canvas text → NaN damage; non-total sort comparator) are fixed as minimal vendored patches under vendor/ with [patch.crates-io], inline comments, per-patch READMEs and regression tests inside the vendored crates (`cargo test -p iced_graphics -p iced_tiny_skia`). LESSON: before upgrading iced wholesale, diff the canvas/damage paths — these fixes must be re-based or dropped deliberately when the dependency moves. 2. CANVAS TEXT BOUNDS are now MEASURED (one no-wrap cosmic-text layout per label per frame, ~µs) instead of INFINITY markers. The anchor stays the alignment position and the size is the measured line — both consumers (visible_bounds for damage, draw_cached for rendering) apply the same alignment arithmetic to the same rectangle. A first attempt that reused the frame clip as conservative bounds BROKE the draw anchor (draw_cached re-anchors via `..bounds`), pushing the right-aligned rate label to the window edge — caught by the Xvfb rig and fixed by measuring instead. 3. EXCLUSIONS SEMANTICS: every plain-list entry imports as action `direct`; v2rayN JSON keeps its own outbound tags where they map (direct/freedom, proxy, block/blackhole).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D23",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D23 — S11: even byte spreading (Balanced) + adapter priority order (Priority), v0.7.0",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D23"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User report: with 3+ bonded adapters, one carries most traffic, the second less, the third rarely any. Root cause: round-robin evens CONNECTION COUNT, not BYTES — a single fat flow dominates its adapter. (D22 was the S10.1 HiDPI fix — recorded in the ledger, no separate section here.)",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "1. BALANCED (new stock default) is load-aware spreading: each new connection goes to the link with the least live pressure (`rate_bps + active_conns × 128 KiB/s`). The per-connection reserve exists specifically so a burst of connections inside one 1 s counter tick spreads instead of stacking on the one link whose byte counters have not ticked yet. Ties rotate via the shared cursor, so an idle table degrades to exactly round-robin. Settings migration v2 moves the stock round-robin to balanced ONCE (D20 precedent: a version<2 file carrying the stock value is indistinguishable from an explicit choice; an explicit re-choice persists). 2. SATURATION IS A PLATEAU, NOT A LEVEL. The learned capacity rises to meet any new rate, so \"rate ≈ capacity\" is true during a ramp too — a naive threshold would mark a link saturated on its first fat flow. Priority therefore requires the capacity to have STOPPED rising (≥2%/tick resets the streak; the rate EWMA damps jitter below that) for 3+ ticks AND rate ≥ 0.85×capacity AND capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s. Consequences: a still-climbing link is never saturated (priority keeps feeding #1 while it ramps); a pinned link saturates within seconds of plateauing; when demand drops below the band the link un-saturates immediately (priority returns traffic to #1 long before the capacity decays). 3. PRIORITY ORDER = the bonded_adapters LIST ORDER (ids persisted in order since S8; links and stream carriers are built in that order, so link index IS priority).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "decision:D24",
-++      "type": "decision",
-++      "title": "D24 — S13: Status tab = one connection frame + one page scrollable (2026-11-19)",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "immutable"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
-++          "anchor": "D24"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "User report (v0.7.0): the Status scrollbars only scrolled the adapter list, so long adapter lists were effectively unusable; wide dead horizontal gap between the connect switch and the server dropdown; the combined graph should use that free space.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "1. STRUCTURE: ONE fixed connection frame at the top — tunnel state text, the connect toggler and the server pick_list STACKED in a fixed-width left column (STATUS_FRAME_LEFT_WIDTH 296) — and the combined bandwidth graph in a fixed-height panel (STATUS_GRAPH_HEIGHT 240, D22's stable-container rule intact) that Fill-scales into ALL remaining frame width. Below the frame: ONE page scrollable owning everything (exit card + the Links/Adapters card). The wheel therefore scrolls the whole page; the frame never moves. 2. WHY the graph may Fill WIDTH inside the frame but keep FIXED height: nothing that can grow lives in the frame any more (the exit-probe result, links and adapter rows all scroll below) — the D22 reflow triggers are gone by construction. 3. MOCK FIDELITY: seed_adapters now carries EIGHT adapters (the 3-NIC bond + Bluetooth, vEthernet (WSL), Tailscale, Loopback, VirtualBox — a realistic Windows enumeration); only the 3 wired ones are bonded. This is what exposed the stale test idiom: the toggle test's apply step used to send ALL row ids to set_bonded_adapters (the real AdaptersApply filters to selected rows; the all-bonded 3-seed made the two indistinguishable). Test now mirrors production. 4. RIG PROOF (pixel-verified): frame anchors byte-stable across scrolls at sf=1.0 AND sf=1.5; all 8 adapter rows render in priority order and the last row is visible at max scroll; per-adapter expansion, the exit-probe verdict card and the resize round-trip all still work; 0 panics.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {

-++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | S10 OPENED per user v0.5.1 report: (a) graphs occasionally show up but out of frame; (b) want exclusions import from file (v2rayN-style direct bypass); (c) is there something more efficient than round-robin / can both connections be used simultaneously; (d) \"Check exit IP\" panics with \"user-provided comparison function does not correctly implement a total order\" (smallsort.rs:854). Sandbox had recycled AGAIN (S2-era tree); fresh clone from origin (37d1d99). Toolchain rebuilt: rustup 1.100.0 stable + win-gnu target, zig 0.14.1 (pip wheel reused from tools/pypkgs), cargo-zigbuild 0.24.1; libxkbcommon-x11 + libxcb-xkb extracted from Debian debs into /tmp/xkblibs for the Xvfb GUI rig.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | REPRO RIG BUILT (the decisive tool): scripts/gui_drive.py — one-shot process tree (sandbox kills daemons between tool calls): Xvfb :99 → app under test (LD_LIBRARY_PATH=xkblibs) → scripted XTEST clicks/types (python-xlib; keymap-level SHIFT handling; explicit SetInputFocus because NO WM runs under Xvfb — keyboard focus is never granted otherwise) → ffmpeg x11grab screenshots; analysis via VLM on coordinate-grid crops (VLM coordinates are unreliable — always pixel-cluster verify). REPRODUCED ALL THREE RENDERING BUGS deterministically: (1) connected 12 s → ZERO series pixels anywhere (labels painted, series/grid never did) until a resize round-trip forced a full redraw; (2) the exit-IP click aborted with the user's EXACT panic (smallsort total-order, iced_graphics::damage::group in the stack); (3) with a first-attempt clip fix, the right-aligned rate label rendered at x≈30 (window edge) — the \"out of frame\" shape.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | ROOT CAUSES (all in the terminal iced 0.13 releases — 0.13.0 is the LAST of the 0.13 line for iced_graphics/iced_tiny_skia/iced_winit, no patch release to bump to): (a) iced_tiny_skia Layer::damage intersected ABSOLUTE primitive bounds with the group's UNTRANSFORMED LOCAL clip (a canvas Frame clips to (0,0,w,h)) → every canvas off the window origin produced ZERO damage → series/grid never repainted (text groups are not clip-intersected, which is why labels painted — the tell). Same local/absolute confusion in the render loop's group clip mask (→ masked to the ORIGIN = out-of-frame) and in Cached-geometry damage. (b) Frame::fill_text pushed Text::Cached with (position, INFINITY, INFINITY) marker bounds + INFINITY clip; right-alignment arithmetic (x -= width → -inf) then center() (-inf + inf/2) produced NaN damage rects; damage::group's partial_cmp().unwrap_or(Equal) comparator answered Equal for NaN-vs-anything → driftsort aborted the process (intermittent — sort-pattern dependent, matching \"occasionally\"). Caught in the act with a temporary diagnostic: rects like {x:-inf, w:+inf} and {x:156, y:588, w:NaN, h:NaN}. FIXES (vendored under vendor/ + [patch.crates-io], each with inline comments + regression tests): total_cmp in damage::group; clip mapped through the group transformation in damage (Group + Cached) and in the render mask; fill_text now MEASURES the line (same no-wrap cosmic layout as the glyph-outline branch) and stores honest anchor+size bounds so the damage and draw paths finally agree.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | TWO MORE LATENT BUGS FOUND WHILE WIRING THE IMPORT: (1) the Routing editor was BROKEN against the real backend since v0.5.0 — the GUI's RULE_KINDS were kebab-case (\"domain-suffix\") while real_service's rule_from_view only accepts camelCase (\"domainSuffix\"), so every GUI save errored \"unknown rule kind\" and loaded rules showed blank kind dropdowns (the smoke test missed it: MockService is permissive and never runs rule_from_view). Unified on camelCase. (2) merge_policy_from_str only accepted the UN-hyphenated serde names — the GUI's own \"lowest-latency\" pick fell into the unknown-value fallback and silently behaved as round-robin. Both hyphenated and un-hyphenated forms now parse (regression tests for each).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | FEATURES: (1) exclusions import — mt-service::parse_exclusion_list (pure, 6 tests): plain lists (domain/IP/CIDR per line, # comments full-line AND inline, bare IP → /32 or /128) and v2rayN routing-rules JSON ({\"routing\":{\"rules\"}} | {\"rules\"} | bare []; domain:/full:/plain → domainSuffix — full: WIDENED to subdomains, documented; outboundTag direct|freedom→direct, proxy→proxy, block|blackhole→reject; geosite:/geoip:/regexp: skipped with per-entry reasons, geoip:private noted as already-enforced); GUI: Routing tab import card (path field + Import + hint) → entries join the DRAFT (Apply activates) with skipped lines as WARN LogLines + status summary; CLI: multitunnel routing list | routing import <file> (appends + persists immediately). End-to-end verified in the Xvfb rig: typed path (cwd-relative to dodge the Shift-layer XTEST gap), Import → 4 rules joined the draft + status line, geosite:cn skipped. (2) SCHEDULING ANSWER + UX: lowest-latency (EWMA) already existed in mt-net but was unreachable from the GUI (bug 2 above) — now real; Advanced card gained the full per-connection vs stream explainer (\"stream: the BYTES of every connection split across ALL ticked adapters at once … one download uses both NICs\"), Network card's policy explainer now names EWMA and points at stream mode. (3) v0.6.0: README (Exclusions/Scheduling/Rendering-fix sections, CLI list), QUICKSTART Step 7, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES vendored-iced section.",

-++          "text": "2026-11-19T07:15Z | S10.1 OPENED per user v0.6.0 report: (a) graph axes jump to upper-left, out of bounds; (b) 'Check exit IP' output renders on the same line as the graph — graph needs a fixed container; (c) per-adapter graphs reachable by pressing the adapter NAME in the Status tab. Working tree was mode-changes only (sandbox recycle artifact); tree == 1da6de6 (s10-post-release).",
-++          "kind": "body"

-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T07:55Z | ROOT CAUSE FOUND + REPRODUCED (rig, WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1.5, 1920x1440 Xvfb screen — the sf=1.5 window needs the bigger screen or iced's 1024x768-logical default clamps and the graph card collapses to 0): the vendored (UPSTREAM iced_tiny_skia 0.13.0, inherited) render loop composes canvas group transforms as group.transformation() * scale(sf) — glam (A*B applies B first) makes that scale-FIRST-then-translate: physical = local*sf + OFFSET(unscaled). Correct is (local+offset)*sf. At sf=1.5 the status graph content lands ~offset*0.5 px up-left of its card, clipped by the (correct) clip mask to a ~20px sliver at the card top — pixel-verified: series strip y 613..632 inside card 612..935. This ALSO explains 'exit-IP output on the same line as the graph' on taller windows (shifted canvas overlaps the exit card). S10's rig ran sf=1.0 where both orders coincide — never caught. Fix: swap to scale(sf) * group.transformation() in BOTH primitives and text group draw paths; clip mapping (rect*t*scale, left-to-right) was already correct.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T08:10Z | IMPLEMENTED (D22): (1) HiDPI transform fix in vendor/iced_tiny_skia/src/lib.rs — group_transform(scale, group) helper composes scale AFTER the group offset for BOTH the primitive and the text group draw paths (upstream order was scale-first + unscaled offset); 3 regression tests pin the mapping ((local+offset)*sf), its sf=1 identity, and agreement with the clip mapping (rect*group*scale was already correct — only the draw transform was wrong). (2) Status graph moved to a FIXED-height container (STATUS_GRAPH_HEIGHT=240) — the exit-probe result appearing can no longer re-flow the graph (series bbox byte-identical across the probe in the rig). (3) Per-adapter graphs on the Status tab: bottom card now hosts Links + Adapters sections in ONE scrollable owning all remaining space; each adapter row's NAME is a text button (arrow + name, primary color) toggling Message::AdapterExpanded — same shared AdapterRow state as the Adapters tab; rows show up/down + not-bonded + live ↑/↓ rate chips (adapter_rates newest sample); expansion reveals the 110px mini graph + contextual hint (connected/bonded/idle/traffic). (4) Mock fidelity: seed links renamed to the REAL engine's \"profile [adapter]\" shape (\"synthetic-reality [Wi-Fi]/[Ethernet]\") and mock default bonds BOTH wired adapters (matches the round-robin default demo setup; adapters_screen_toggle_apply_revert test updated for the new seed). Adapters-tab explainer cross-references the Status shortcut.",

-++          "text": "2026-11-19T08:10Z | VERIFIED IN THE RIG (Xvfb, WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1.5, 2080x1750 screen — an sf=1.5 window needs a screen >= its 1536x1152 physical default or iced clamps it and the graph card collapses to 0): BEFORE fix the chart was a ~20px clipped sliver at the card top (user's exact report); AFTER fix the chart body fills its card (VLM: card y 470..875, content 615..820, labels inside; series pixels 9x before). -++          "text": "2026-11-19T09:47Z | S11 OPENED per field report: \"Per connection bonding mode works, but stream bonding mode does not.\" (v0.6.1). -++          "text": "2026-11-19T09:47Z | THE FIELD BUG (server-side, not our code): Xray 26.x freedom outbound has a DEFAULT SAFETY POLICY — traffic from VLESS/VMess/Trojan/SS inbounds targeting private/loopback IPs is BLACKHOLED (\"proxy/freedom: target blocked by a finalrule: tcp:127.0.0.1:7443, blackholing connection\"); stream bonding's merge target IS 127.0.0.1:<merge port>, so the server Xray blackholes every carrier while per-connection (public targets) works. Aggravated client-side: Xray's SOCKS inbound replies \"connected\" BEFORE the upstream dial resolves → carriers attach PHANTOM-LIVE → bonded traffic vanishes with no error until timeouts. Reproduced end-to-end in the rig exactly as reported.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },

-++          "text": "2026-11-19T09:47Z | mt-bond honest carriers (phantom-live killed): Carrier.verified flag — client attach_carrier queues a verify PING right after HELLO (seq tracked in pending_verify); the carrier becomes SCHEDULABLE (usable() = alive && verified) only when ITS pong returns (matched by seq wherever the daemon schedules the reply); server marks carriers verified at attach (freedom hands it the stream). ensure_carriers now waits ≤VERIFY_PONG_TIMEOUT (5s) and reports per-carrier verdicts honestly (\"no pong from the merge daemon …\" with the fix hint), respawns demand the pong too (abandon_unverified on timeout), live_carriers/all_carriers_dead/carrier_snapshot all report usable. Fallback WARN in real_service now names both likely causes + the exact VM commands. Daemon (mt-merge-server) UNCHANGED — no VM daemon upgrade needed beyond the scripts.",

-++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | S12 OPENED per user report (after v0.6.2): with 3+ bonded adapters \"most traffic goes through one adapter, the second a little less, the third rarely any\" — want (a) more even distribution, (b) a mode where adapters fill in a user-chosen ORDER (first adapter takes traffic until its bandwidth is saturated, then the next), and (c) UI to order adapters first/second/third. Root-cause read: the stock round-robin spreads CONNECTION COUNT evenly, not BYTES — one fat flow (video/download) dominates whichever adapter it landed on, which is exactly the reported shape. Sandbox had recycled again (fresh rootfs, no rustup); toolchain rebuilt per the STATE recipe (rustup 1.100.0 stable + win-gnu target, ziglang 0.14.1 wheel, cargo-zigbuild 0.24.1, python-xlib + xkb debs for the rig).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | IMPLEMENTED (D23) — SCHEDULING: two new MergePolicy variants in mt-net. `Balanced` (new stock default, settings_version 2 migration of the stock round-robin, D20-precedent): pick() ranks candidates by live PRESSURE = rate_bps + active_conns×CONN_RESERVE_BPS (128 KiB/s reserve stops same-second bursts stacking on one link before the 1 s counter ticks); ties rotate via the shared cursor (an idle table behaves exactly like round-robin). `Priority`: walk links in USER ORDER (link order == bonded_adapters order); first candidate NOT saturated wins; all saturated → least RELATIVE load (rate/capacity, unknown capacity = most headroom). Saturation is a PLATEAU, not a level: the capacity estimate rises to meet any new rate, so \"rate ≈ capacity\" is true mid-ramp too — saturation additionally requires the (EWMA-tracked) capacity to have stopped rising for ≥3 ticks (CAPACITY_RISE_RESET 2%/tick; the EWMA damps jitter below that) plus rate ≥ 0.85×capacity with capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s floor (background chatter never saturates). Load plumbing: LinkHealth gained active_conns/rate_bps/capacity_bps/plateau_ticks/saturated; the server's tunnel() bumps a per-link AtomicU64 (send path via establish→link_idx→pumps), establish/close maintain active_conns, and the 1 s tick_loop calls aggregator.tick_loads(dt) (pure update_load per link, unit-tested ramp→plateau→recovery). set_settings now validates the policy name (fail loud) and treats a policy change as dataplane-changing (live reconnect).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | IMPLEMENTED (D23) — STREAM MODE: the mt-bond carrier scheduler (D17 round-robin) is now policy-aware. Carrier gained a queued-bytes AtomicU64 (send_bytes fetch_add; writer_task fetch_sub after the socket write; writer-gone resets to 0 — a respawned carrier starts clean). pick_carrier snapshots live carriers (idx, queued, rtt_ms) into a PURE pick_carrier_index(): Failover=first, RoundRobin=cursor, LowestLatency=best sampled RTT (known beats unknown), Balanced=least queued with rotating ties (a fast NIC drains its queue quicker and naturally takes more frames — capacity-proportional even spreading), Priority=first carrier under PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER (512 KiB ≈ 8 max frames; a healthy carrier hovers near zero, a bottlenecked one grows) else least queued. BondOutbound::with_policy wires the GUI policy through Endpoint::client_with_policy; the daemon side keeps round-robin (priority order is a client concern). connect_flow log line now names the policy; settings.json default + mock default = \"balanced\".",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | IMPLEMENTED (D23) — UI: the Adapters tab is now the priority-ordering surface. Rows render selected-block-first in the SAVED bonded order (pure sort_adapter_rows; unselected rows keep enumeration order below); selected rows carry #1/#2/#3 position chips (primary container) and ↑/↓ buttons (on_press_maybe; disabled at block edges, no-ops for unselected rows); AdapterToggled maintains the block invariant (ticking ON appends at the END = lowest priority; OFF sinks below the block); AdapterMoved swaps with the previous/next SELECTED row; Apply persists the ordered id list (set_bonded_adapters already preserved order); dirty now includes ORDER changes (adapters_dirty compares draft ids vs saved ids restricted to present rows); AdaptersSaved chains load_settings → load_adapters → refresh_status so the sort key is fresh; SettingsLoaded re-sorts only when no draft is in flight. Status-tab adapter rows gained the same #n chips (priority_position_of). Two hard compiler lessons recorded: (1) async fn cycle in opaque-type computation (carrier_died→respawn→attach→writer→carrier_died) — Box<dyn Future> erasure did NOT break it because the coercion itself needed Send of the witness; broke it STRUCTURALLY with an unbounded death-notification channel consumed by the sweeper; (2) std lock guards across await inside spawned tasks — collect-then-await everywhere.",

-++          "text": "2026-11-18T10:10Z | PROTOCOL BUG found by integration tests (exactly what they exist for): CLOSE was fire-and-forget and could overtake in-flight DATA scheduled on ANOTHER carrier (round-robin), and full-close killed the reverse path — a 1 MiB echo came back 753664 bytes. Fix: flush-then-CLOSE (wait for cumulative ACKs of the session's unacked frames, ≤3 s bound) + asymmetric close semantics (client CLOSE(Eof) = WRITE half-close, session stays; daemon's CLOSE = final). -++          "text": "2026-11-18T16:22Z | CORRECTION of the OPS-RECOVERY entry above (honesty over convenience): attempt 1 was NOT a 24h zombie. Real timeline in UTC: run created 14:41:43Z, cancelled 16:0xZ = ~1h35m elapsed in cargo-test — exactly the DOCUMENTED cold-cache compile pattern (recorded for v0.5.0's release leg and ci 44316450330's ubuntu leg). The misjudgment came from comparing the 18 Nov publish date against an assumed current date of 19 Nov UTC, when the sandbox clock read 2026-11-18T16:21Z UTC (= 2026-11-19 00:21 Beijing / 22:51 Yangon — the UTC+8/UTC+6:30 headers had already rolled the calendar date). Cancelling attempt 1 was therefore precautionary, not forced; it cut a compiling job mid-flight (harmless — rerun attempt 2 green in ~13min on a warm cache and attached the zip) and ci 44316450330's slow-compiling ubuntu leg was likewise cancelled while merely cold-compiling (also harmless: its successor run 44336498456 is fully green on the same commit). LESSON (the real one): before declaring any run stuck, compute elapsed = now - started_at IN UTC and compare against the documented cold-compile window (~2h) AND the 6h hosted-runner limit; local/UTC calendar-date confusion fabricates phantom 24h outages. Secondary: a cancel+rerun gamble often lands on the cache the first attempt was still warming — but never cancel inside the documented cold window on elapsed-time grounds alone.",

-++      "id": "pm:architecture",

-++      "title": "Tech Stack & Architecture Rules",

-++        "durable"

-++          "file": "PROJECT_MEMORY.md",
-++          "anchor": "Tech Stack & Architecture Rules"
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "- **What**: MultiTunnel — Rust rewrite of BondTunnel; zero-dependency all-in-one (v2rayN import + net-merge), Material You GUI. Repo: github.com/maniesh-NR/MultiTunnel. - **Data path**: Windows client → local SOCKS/HTTP → ProxyServer → BondOutbound → N carriers (one per bonded NIC, VLESS+REALITY via Xray `sendThrough`, engine self-provisioned D14) → VM Xray (public 8443) → freedom → mt-merge-server (127.0.0.1:7443) → real target. Reverse symmetric. Auth at the Xray edge. - **Two bond modes**: per-connection (default) and stream bonding (D17 framing, needs the VM merge daemon; carriers verified by PING/PONG before schedulable). - **Scheduling (D23, v0.7.0)**: five merge policies in mt-net — round-robin, failover, lowest-latency (EWMA), **balanced** (stock default; pressure = rate_bps + active_conns × 128 KiB/s reserve), **priority** (user order; #1 fills until bandwidth plateaus (ramp detector, ≥3 flat ticks + rate ≥ 0.85 × capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s), then spills). Stream-mode frame scheduler is policy-aware too (least writer backpressure / 512 KiB queue high-water). Adapter priority == saved `bonded_adapters` ORDER; Adapters tab = ordering UI (selected rows first, #n chips, ↑/↓). - **Crates**: mt-net (proxy servers, merge, policy), mt-bond (stream framing, carrier scheduling, daemon), mt-engine (ManagedEngine lifecycle), mt-links (vless:// + subscriptions), mt-platform (Win32 adapter FFI), mt-service (service trait + real_service), mt-m3 + mt-app (Material You GUI, iced). Root crate = CLI binaries (multitunnel, tray, mt-app).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {

-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "Every change closes only after ALL of these (CI runs them too):",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "1. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean. 2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean, host AND windows-gnu (use cargo/zig-cc shims in `cargo/`). 3. `cargo test --workspace` — 0 failed (current baseline: 396 tests; E2E rig `tests/e2e_real_xray.rs` gated by `MT_E2E_XRAY=1`). 4. Vendored iced tests: 6/0 green. 5. `cargo zigbuild --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --workspace` — PE32+ ×4 (multitunnel, tray, mt-app, mt-merge-server) + linux ELF. 6. GUI: `mt-app --smoke` exit 0; visual changes verified in the Xvfb rig (`scripts/gui_drive.py`, pixel-verified, sf=1.0 AND sf=1.5). 7. GUI-affecting bugs: reproduce FIRST in the rig, fix, re-verify (no symptom patches); user-reported crashes get a regression test. 8. Release: tag `v*` → release.yml; verify assets by download+unzip; record in LEDGER.md; push via `./harness/backup.sh <label>`.",

-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "MultiTunnel: Rust rewrite of BondTunnel; zero-dependency all-in-one (v2rayN import + net-merge), Material You GUI. Repo: github.com/maniesh-NR/MultiTunnel. Windows client → local SOCKS/HTTP → ProxyServer → BondOutbound → N carriers (one per bonded NIC, VLESS+REALITY via Xray sendThrough, engine self-provisioned D14) → VM Xray (public 8443) → freedom → mt-merge-server (127.0.0.1:7443) → real target. Reverse symmetric. Auth at the Xray edge.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Two bond modes: per-connection (default) and stream bonding (D17 framing, needs the VM merge daemon; carriers verified by PING/PONG before schedulable). Scheduling (D23, v0.7.0): five merge policies in mt-net — round-robin, failover, lowest-latency (EWMA), balanced (stock default), priority (user order; fills #1 until bandwidth plateaus then spills). Stream-mode frame scheduler is policy-aware too. Adapter priority == saved bonded_adapters ORDER; Adapters tab = ordering UI.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Hard rules: config schema camelCase + versioned migrations (D8); no secrets in repo (D9) — token lives in ../upload/, backup.sh reads it; fail-open routing (D5); GUI never dies invisibly (D15); vendored iced under vendor/ + [patch.crates-io] (D21); CI timestamps UTC; rustc 1.100.0 + zig 0.14.1 + cargo-zigbuild (D2), windows target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "protocol:memory-graph",
-++      "type": "protocol",
-++      "title": "Agentic memory graph + RAG retrieval (S14) — typed nodes/edges store, BM25 + graph expansion, all-agent accessible",
-++      "tags": [
-++        "protocol",
-++        "s14",
-++        "done"
-++      ],
-++      "sources": [
-++        {
-++          "file": "harness/memory/build_graph.py",
-++          "anchor": ""
-++        }
-++      ],
-++      "passages": [
-++        {
-++          "text": "The agentic memory is a typed graph store: harness/memory/store/memory_graph.json (schema v1). Nodes (whitelisted types: project, architecture, playbook, contract, state, decision, ledger, release, commit, task, bug, component, protocol, report, consensus, fact) carry retrieval passages; edges carry typed relations with evidence. Sources: PROJECT_MEMORY.md durable sections, STATE.md, DECISIONS.md, LEDGER.md (grouped per stage tag), agent-reports/, consensus/, git tags + full log, curated/.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "RAG retrieval (BM25 k1=1.5 b=0.75, title boost 1.5, plus graph-neighborhood expansion with 0.5^hop score decay): query from repo root with `python3 query_memory.py \"<topic>\"` (flags: -k N, --expand HOPS, --json, --prompt). --prompt emits a paste-ready context pack with induced subgraph links — the RAG input for any consuming agent (session start, subagent delegation, or future session).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Agent WRITE path: `python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py --node id=... type=... title=... passage=...` or `--edge src=... dst=... rel=... evidence=...` — appends/updates harness/memory/curated/{nodes,edges}.json (merged last at build, wins on id collision) and rebuilds the store. update_memory.py rebuilds the store on every run. Rebuilds are deterministic (byte-identical while HEAD and sources are unchanged; no wall-clock in the store). Tests: python3 harness/memory/test_graph.py.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },

Session ritual: git fetch && git rebase origin/main, then python3 update_memory.py, then read the Active Playbook section of PROJECT_MEMORY.md. Durable sections of PROJECT_MEMORY.md are maintained BY HAND; the recent-activity section is maintained BY SCRIPT. Long-form history lives in harness/memory/ (LEDGER.md append-only, STATE.md rewritten per stage, DECISIONS.md immutable).",

-++          "text": "- Stage: S2 adversarial review (round 1), Reviewer-B - Repo: /home/z/my-project/MultiTunnel, branch main, HEAD 59d7bba (working tree clean — verified `git status --short` empty, `git rev-parse HEAD` = 59d7bba751e99707bb08bcb32288808a3d4a69be) - Date: 2026-11-13 - Scope reviewed: src/core_proc.rs, src/supervisor.rs, src/sysproxy.rs, src/elevate.rs, src/main.rs, src/bin/tray.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml (+ S1 modules read as context for cross-module issues) - No files modified except this report.",

-++          "text": "## 1. Verification log (all commands run by me, nothing trusted)",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `. tools/env.sh; cargo test` | **52/52 ok, 0 failed, finished 5.64 s** (lib 52; bin/tray/doc-test harnesses 0) | | `cargo test` ×3 more (back-to-back) | 52/52 ×3, no flakes | | `cargo test` under full 2-core CPU load (2 busy-loops) | 52/52 ok, 6.17 s | | `cargo test --lib -- supervisor:: core_proc:: --test-threads=1` ×5 | 13/13 ×5 (~6.2 s each) — the timing-sensitive tests repeated single-threaded | | `touch src/**/*.rs; cargo clippy --all-targets` | clean, no warnings (\"Checking multitunnel v0.1.0 … Finished\") — rebuild forced, not a cached pass | | `cargo fmt --check` | clean (exit 0, no diff) | | `touch src/**/*.rs; cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | green, crate genuinely recompiled for the target (\"Compiling multitunnel v0.1.0\") | | `file /tmp/mt-target/x86_64-pc-windows-gnu/debug/*.exe` | `multitunnel.exe`: **PE32+ executable for MS Windows 6.00 (console), x86-64**; `multitunnel-tray.exe`: **PE32+ … (GUI), x86-64** — both exes link, subsystems correct | | `objdump -p multitunnel.exe` (import table) | imports **ShellExecuteW** (shell32), **InternetSetOptionW** (wininet), **OpenProcessToken / GetTokenInformation** (advapi32), **RegOpenKeyExW / RegQueryValueExW / RegSetValueExW** (advapi32, winreg) → definitive proof the cfg(windows) code in elevate.rs/sysproxy.rs compiled **and linked** for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (not a skipped rebuild) | | Test inventory (`cargo test -- --list`) | config 9, core_proc 5, elevate 3, netmerge 16, supervisor 8, sysproxy 6, xrayconf 5 = **52** |",

-++        {
-++          "text": "## 2. Findings by severity",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P0 — none",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Cross-build is green and proven (imports above); windows-sys feature list covers every referenced API; no license contamination; both CI workflows are functional.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P1 — 3",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P1-1. A `v*` tag releases without any test run.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2-4` triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and PRs — a tag push does **not** trigger ci.yml. `.github/workflows/release.yml:9-14` goes straight to `cargo build --release` with no test/lint step. So the official release artifact can be built from code that never ran the suite (e.g. a tag pushed ahead of a green main commit). Fix: add a `cargo test` step to build-windows (and ideally ubuntu too) in release.yml, or make the release job depend on the ci workflow.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P1-2. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is referenced by LICENSE and release.yml but does not exist in the tree.** `LICENSE:23-25` states \"Third-party components … (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in releases)\"; `release.yml:21-23` lists it in the copy loop behind a `Test-Path` guard. The file is absent, so the guard silently drops it and every release zip ships without the notices the project's own LICENSE promises (MIT attribution for winreg, serde/regex/windows-sys dual-license choice, MPL-2.0 statement for the non-redistributed Xray-core). Not contamination (see §3.5), but it should be authored before the first `v*` tag.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P1-3. `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized — concurrent call can leave a half-up tunnel with `State::Failed`/`Connected` mismatch (S3 landmine).** `supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect). If `disconnect()` runs while `connect_sequence()` is in flight (state `Connecting`), the loop handle is still `None` (spawn_loop runs at the *end* of connect), so disconnect joins nothing and immediately restores the proxy / stops the core; connect_sequence then continues through steps 4–5 **after** the disconnect: `net-merge on` and `sysproxy::set` re-run, and either the state ends `Connected` with a live loop that undoes the user's disconnect (spawn_loop resets the stop flag at `:386`), or (restartMax=0) `Failed` with net-merge left on and the proxy restored by the campaign but no owner. Also, the loop's `wait_for_port`/`socks_probe` (up to 15 s each) are not stop-flag-aware, so disconnect can block a calling thread ~15 s. Unreachable from the S2 CLI (main.rs: `connect()?` then sleep-forever, single thread), but the module contract (`supervisor.rs:29-31`) explicitly hands the S3 tray an `Arc<Supervisor>` callable \"from menu handlers on any thread\" — a quick connect→disconnect click sequence is exactly that. Fix before S3: one cycle mutex / in-flight guard around connect+disconnect, and make the loop's port-wait/probe stoppable.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P2 — 7",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-1. Unused windows-sys feature.** `Cargo.toml:27` enables `Win32_System_LibraryLoader`, but no code references `GetModuleHandle`/`LoadLibrary` (grep over src: zero hits). Harmless (declaration-only crate) but it is dead dependency surface — drop it.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-2. CI never enforces the project's own fmt/clippy gates.** `ci.yml` runs only `cargo test` + zigbuild. The harness treats \"clippy clean / fmt clean\" as gate criteria; a regression in either lands silently. Add a lint job (`cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-3. `core_proc.rs` test stub still uses the blocking-accept pattern that caused the supervisor hang.** `core_proc.rs:421-444` (`stub_socks`: blocking `listener.accept().expect(...)`, `:454` join). It is provably unhangable here — the probe always connects before anything can fail (addr comes from the bound listener) and the stub thread ends right after writing its reply, independent of the probe — but supervisor's stub was hardened (nonblocking accept + quit flag, `supervisor.rs:705-754`) precisely because this *class* of bug hung the suite once. Apply the same pattern for defense-in-depth.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-4. Narrow `spawn_loop` race after a give-up.** `supervisor.rs:377-392` vs `:497`. If `connect()` reaches `spawn_loop` in the few-instruction window between the old loop's `break` (GaveUp, `:468`) and `loop_running.store(false)` (`:497`), the `loop_running` guard early-returns and the new cycle gets **no poll loop** (Connected, unsupervised). Practically unreachable (connect_sequence takes ≥ms; the window is instructions), but the guard could join-wait instead of returning.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-5. Tray stub `eprintln!` from a GUI-subsystem process.** `src/bin/tray.rs:5-6`: with `windows_subsystem = \"windows\"` and no console (double-click launch), the stderr handle is invalid and `eprintln!` panics (\"failed printing to stderr\") → exit 101 instead of the intended 2. Stub-only (real tray is S3); trivial to make robust (ignore the write error / drop the line).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-6. Cross-module note for S3: net-merge spawns lack CREATE_NO_WINDOW.** `netmerge.rs:134-138` (`run_full` — used by the supervisor poll loop every 5 s, `supervisor.rs:474`) sets no creation flags, unlike `core_proc.rs:149-154` for xray. Invisible from the S2 console binary (children share its console), but the S3 tray is GUI-subsystem: spawning `net-merge status` every 5 s will flash a console window. Either add the flag in netmerge or have the tray spawn through a helper that does.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "**P2-7. Metadata/hygiene nits.** `Cargo.toml` has no `repository` and no `rust-version` (lock is v4 → needs cargo ≥1.78; `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` is a moving target — pinning `rust-version` documents the floor). `release.yml:29-32` could set `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` so a path typo can't silently produce an asset-less release. No CI caching (optional; suite is fast).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },

-++          "text": "### 3.1 Timing margins on a loaded 2-core box (this sandbox IS 2-core) - **Drip test [350, 900) ms vs 500 ms budget**: measured 0.50–0.51 s across 15 runs including 5 under full CPU contention — the failure is produced by the kernel SO_RCVTIMEO deadline, not by user-space polling, so it is load-insensitive. Sound. - **Op-lock test (300 ms block window)**: the assertion is an *invariant*, not a race outcome — while the main thread holds op_lock, the connect thread cannot have moved state regardless of scheduling, so it cannot flake slow; after release, 10 s budget for a ~50 ms refused-probe connect. Sound. - **Start-twice <1 s**: second start() checks the child slot *first* (the REV-C P0-1 fix) and errors in microseconds; measured ~0 ms; 1000× margin. Concurrent start/stop on CoreProc remains impossible because op_lock serializes supervisor ops and the loop thread is joined before disconnect's core.stop(). No issue.",

-++          "text": "**P1-A. Winsock accepted-socket blocking-mode ambiguity in the Windows-CI-exposed test stub (core_proc.rs `stub_socks`).** `stub_socks` now sets the listener nonblocking (my P2-3 fix) and then does `set_read_timeout(5s)` + `read_exact` on the **accepted** socket. On Linux, accept() never propagates O_NONBLOCK (all local runs green). On Windows the tests `socks_probe_success` / `socks_probe_refusal_names_status` (NOT cfg-gated) run on windows-latest in **both** ci.yml and the new release.yml test step. Microsoft's accept() docs say the accepted socket \"has the same properties as socket s, **including the asynchronous events registered with WSAAsyncSelect or WSAEventSelect**\" — event registration is documented as inherited (and those APIs force nonblocking), but the docs are **silent on FIONBIO** (which is what std's set_nonblocking uses); community folklore claims Windows accepted sockets inherit the nonblocking mode, while wine's bug-compatible accept creates a fresh default-(blocking-)state socket and copies nothing. If inheritance is real, the stub's first `read_exact` loses the race with the probe's greeting write → WSAEWOULDBLOCK → stub thread panics → red windows-latest leg (and a release-blocking `cargo test`). Nobody in this project can execute the Windows leg before merge. I could not demonstrate breakage from this sandbox, so this is P1, not P0. **Fix is one line and correct under both semantics**: after accept, `let _ = s.set_nonblocking(false);` (same for the supervisor `spawn_stub` for symmetry, though its tests are unix-gated).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },

-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `. tools/env.sh; cargo test` | **52/52 passed, 0 failed, 5.64 s** (run twice, both green) | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` | **clean** — 0 warnings / 0 errors | | `cargo fmt --check` | **clean** (exit 0) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **success** — `multitunnel.exe` (26.7 MB) + `multitunnel-tray.exe` (4.9 MB), both PE32+ |",

-++          "text": "**Adversarial demos** (standalone crate in `/tmp/mt-revc-demo` against the repo as a path dependency; the repo itself was not modified — verified `git status` clean after):",
-++          "kind": "body"

-++        {
-++          "text": "- `start-hang`: `CoreProc::start()` called while a child is running — **blocked past 2 s** until the child was killed externally; on unblock it returned `Ok(())` and spawned a *second* core generation. The documented `Err(\"core already running\")` never materialized. → finding **P0-1**. - `disc-race`: `disconnect()` issued while a `connect()` sequence was in flight — **returned `Ok` in 44 ms**; the connect then completed and left `state == Connected` with `loop_running() == true`. → finding **P0-2**.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },

-++          "text": "---",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "## P0 — must fix before close",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` hangs (and then double-starts) when a child is already running **`src/core_proc.rs:108-116`** (doc claim at `:104`, module doc `:10-11`)",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "`start()` joins the previous waiter thread **before** checking the child slot:",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "The waiter (`waiter_loop`, :333-367) only exits when the child dies, the slot empties, or the stop flag is set. So while a child is live, `join()` blocks **indefinitely**; the `is_some()` error branch is dead code on that path. When the child eventually dies, the join returns, the (now empty) slot passes the check, and `start()` spawns a *new* child and returns `Ok(())` — a silent double-generation restart the caller never asked for. This violates the method's own contract (\"Returns an error if a child is already running\") and is an unbounded block in a public lib API that stage S3 (tray) is specified to call from menu threads.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Reachability inside the supervisor today is via P0-2's corrupted states (e.g. `State::Failed` with a live core → next `connect()` → `connect_sequence` step 2 → `core.start()` → wedged forever); it is also directly reachable by any external API user. **Fix (trivial):** check `lock(&self.child).is_some()` and return the error *before* joining the leftover waiter (the leftover join is only safe when the previous cycle's child is gone).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P0-2 — `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized as whole operations; disconnect can be silently ineffective **`src/supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect)**",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Only the tiny state-check windows hold `inner`. `connect_sequence` performs seconds of work (config write, core spawn, up-to-15 s port wait, up-to-20 s probe, up-to-15 s bonding wait) holding **no lock and no joinable loop handle** — `spawn_loop` runs only *after* it succeeds. A concurrent `disconnect()` sees `state != Disconnected`, sets the stop flag, joins a **`None`** loop handle (`:402` — the loop doesn't exist yet), restores proxy, stops whatever core exists, sets `Disconnected`, and returns `Ok` — while `connect_sequence` keeps running. Demonstrated (44 ms disconnect during an in-flight probe): final state `Connected`, poll loop alive; with `restart_max > 0` the loop even resurrects the core the disconnect killed, and step 5 sets the **system proxy after the user disconnected**, which in the kill-window black-holes all WinINET traffic through a dead proxy.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "This is exactly the usage the module docs advertise for S3 (\"wrap the `Supervisor` in an `Arc` and call from menu handlers on any thread\", :29-31). It also compounds with P0-1: the interleaving `connect A → disconnect B (completes early) → connect C` can leave `State::Failed`/`Disconnected` with a live core, after which the next `connect()` blocks forever in `start()`'s waiter join. **Fix:** one operation-level `Mutex<()>` (or making the state transition a token) held for the whole of `connect()`/`disconnect()`; all methods are already `&self`, so this is local and cheap.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "---",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "## P1 — should fix",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P1-1 — `socks_probe` has per-read timeouts but no total deadline **`src/core_proc.rs:259-268, 390-393`**",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "`set_read_timeout(timeout)` bounds each `read_exact`, but a proxy that drips one byte just inside every timeout window keeps each read alive forever — the probe never returns. The contract (\"a probe against a malicious/half-open proxy must never hang\", module doc :14-16) is satisfied per-read, not per-call. Consequences: `connect()` blocks unboundedly at step 3; the poll loop stalls mid-probe (no tick, no stop-flag observation), and since `disconnect()` joins the loop thread, a tray disconnect wedges with it. Practical exposure is low (the probed proxy is our own spawned xray on loopback), hence P1 not P0. **Fix:** compute a call deadline and re-set `read_timeout` to the remaining budget before each read.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P1-2 — `elevate::join_args` does not escape quotes / backslash-before-quote (argument injection into the elevated relaunch) **`src/elevate.rs:17-28`** (used at `src/main.rs:314` via `relaunch_elevated`)",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "Arguments containing whitespace are wrapped in quotes but embedded `\"` is never escaped. An argument like `a\" --evil` becomes `\"a\" --evil\"`, which `CommandLineToArgvW` parses as **two** arguments (`a`, `--evil\"`) — a single crafted argv entry splits into multiple arguments in the UAC-elevated child. Similarly a path argument ending in `\\` (e.g. `-config C:\\`) corrupts: `\"C:\\\"` parses as `C:\"`. Today's exposure is same-user self-injection (the user launches the CLI), but `main.rs` forwards arbitrary `std::env::args()` verbatim, so any future caller that passes semi-trusted arguments turns this into a real elevation-boundary injection. **Fix:** proper `CommandLineToArgvW`-compatible escaping (`\"` → `\\\"`, doubling trailing backslashes before a closing quote).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "### P1-3 — cross-module: `local.listen` is never validated to be loopback (contract #2) **`src/config.rs:234-263` (validate), `src/xrayconf.rs:20,27` (binds verbatim), `src/supervisor.rs:609-616` (socks_addr/http_addr)**",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "`Config::validate` checks server fields and port collision only. A config with `\"listen\": \"0.0.0.0\"` passes validation, is bound verbatim by **both** xray inbounds — the SOCKS inbound is `\"auth\": \"noauth\"` (`xrayconf.rs:23`) — exposing an unauthenticated SOCKS+HTTP proxy to the LAN, and becomes the WinINET `ProxyServer` value. This directly violates the lib.rs architecture contract #2 (\"the core exposes loopback-only SOCKS/HTTP inbounds\"). Defaults are safe (`127.0.0.1`) and `doctor` only checks parseability (`main.rs:237`), so it is a config-reachable footgun rather than an exploit — but the S2 supervisor is the natural enforcement point (fail `connect_sequence` if `socks_addr`/`http_addr` is not loopback), or add the check to `Config::validate` in a follow-up. Flagged as a cross-module contract violation per stage instructions (config.rs is S1-closed).",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "---",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "## P2 — nits / robustness",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        }
-++      ]
-++    },
-++    {
-++      "id": "report:s2-rev-c-round2",

-++      "title": "S2 Review — Reviewer-C Round 2 (Correctness & Security)",

-++        {
-++          "text": "# S2 Review — Reviewer-C Round 2 (Correctness & Security)",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C (adversarial round 2; round-1 verdict was BLOCK: P0-1, P0-2, P1-1, P1-2, P1-3) - **Date:** 2026-11-13 (repo HEAD `eb1235a`, branch main, clean tree — reviewed as-is, no files modified) - **Scope:** verification of the claimed fixes on top of `59d7bba`, adversarial re-review of all changed code (`core_proc.rs`, `supervisor.rs`, `elevate.rs`, `netmerge.rs`, `bin/tray.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, workflows, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), plus regression thinking around the new designs.",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "## Verification log (run myself, trusted nothing)",
-++          "kind": "title"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `git log --oneline -6` | `eb1235a` ← `9fafc6c` (s2-fix-round-1) ← `59d7bba` (round-1 tree) — history as claimed | | `git diff 59d7bba..HEAD --stat` | 12 files: src/{core_proc,supervisor,elevate,netmerge,bin/tray}.rs, Cargo.toml, 2 workflows, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, LEDGER, 2 agent reports. config/sysproxy/main/xrayconf/error/lib **untouched** (consistent with S1-closed + my P1-3 being fixed at the supervisor) | | `cargo test` | **57/57 passed, 0 failed** in 6.04 s — run **4× total**, all green (6.04/5.99/6.05 s), incl. all 5 new tests | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` | **clean** — 0 warnings / 0 errors | | `cargo fmt --check` | **clean** (exit 0) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **success** (both binaries, current sources) |",
-++          "kind": "body"

-++          "text": "**Round-1 adversarial demos re-run against the fixed tree** (same `/tmp/mt-revc-demo` crate, path-dep rebuilt at `eb1235a`; repo untouched):",
-++          "kind": "body"
-++        },
-++        {
-++          "text": "- `start-hang` (was: >2 s hang, then silent double-start): second `start()` now returns **`Err(\"core already running: …\")` promptly** → **P0-1 fixed, empirically**. - `disc-race` (was: disconnect Ok in 44 ms, tunnel left Connected + loop alive): disconnect now **blocks on op_lock for the in-flight connect (3.66 s), then completes the teardown** — final `state == Disconnected`, `loop_running == false` → **P0-2 fixed, empirically** (semantics correctly changed from \"lost teardown\" to \"serialized teardown\").",
