+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## 2. Findings by severity",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P0 — none",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "Cross-build is green and proven (imports above); windows-sys feature list covers every referenced API; no license contamination; both CI workflows are functional.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1 — 3",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P1-1. A `v*` tag releases without any test run.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2-4` triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and PRs — a tag push does **not** trigger ci.yml. `.github/workflows/release.yml:9-14` goes straight to `cargo build --release` with no test/lint step. So the official release artifact can be built from code that never ran the suite (e.g. a tag pushed ahead of a green main commit). Fix: add a `cargo test` step to build-windows (and ideally ubuntu too) in release.yml, or make the release job depend on the ci workflow.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P1-2. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is referenced by LICENSE and release.yml but does not exist in the tree.** `LICENSE:23-25` states \"Third-party components … (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in releases)\"; `release.yml:21-23` lists it in the copy loop behind a `Test-Path` guard. The file is absent, so the guard silently drops it and every release zip ships without the notices the project's own LICENSE promises (MIT attribution for winreg, serde/regex/windows-sys dual-license choice, MPL-2.0 statement for the non-redistributed Xray-core). Not contamination (see §3.5), but it should be authored before the first `v*` tag.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P1-3. `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized — concurrent call can leave a half-up tunnel with `State::Failed`/`Connected` mismatch (S3 landmine).** `supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect). If `disconnect()` runs while `connect_sequence()` is in flight (state `Connecting`), the loop handle is still `None` (spawn_loop runs at the *end* of connect), so disconnect joins nothing and immediately restores the proxy / stops the core; connect_sequence then continues through steps 4–5 **after** the disconnect: `net-merge on` and `sysproxy::set` re-run, and either the state ends `Connected` with a live loop that undoes the user's disconnect (spawn_loop resets the stop flag at `:386`), or (restartMax=0) `Failed` with net-merge left on and the proxy restored by the campaign but no owner. Also, the loop's `wait_for_port`/`socks_probe` (up to 15 s each) are not stop-flag-aware, so disconnect can block a calling thread ~15 s. Unreachable from the S2 CLI (main.rs: `connect()?` then sleep-forever, single thread), but the module contract (`supervisor.rs:29-31`) explicitly hands the S3 tray an `Arc<Supervisor>` callable \"from menu handlers on any thread\" — a quick connect→disconnect click sequence is exactly that. Fix before S3: one cycle mutex / in-flight guard around connect+disconnect, and make the loop's port-wait/probe stoppable.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P2 — 7",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-1. Unused windows-sys feature.** `Cargo.toml:27` enables `Win32_System_LibraryLoader`, but no code references `GetModuleHandle`/`LoadLibrary` (grep over src: zero hits). Harmless (declaration-only crate) but it is dead dependency surface — drop it.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-2. CI never enforces the project's own fmt/clippy gates.** `ci.yml` runs only `cargo test` + zigbuild. The harness treats \"clippy clean / fmt clean\" as gate criteria; a regression in either lands silently. Add a lint job (`cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-3. `core_proc.rs` test stub still uses the blocking-accept pattern that caused the supervisor hang.** `core_proc.rs:421-444` (`stub_socks`: blocking `listener.accept().expect(...)`, `:454` join). It is provably unhangable here — the probe always connects before anything can fail (addr comes from the bound listener) and the stub thread ends right after writing its reply, independent of the probe — but supervisor's stub was hardened (nonblocking accept + quit flag, `supervisor.rs:705-754`) precisely because this *class* of bug hung the suite once. Apply the same pattern for defense-in-depth.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-4. Narrow `spawn_loop` race after a give-up.** `supervisor.rs:377-392` vs `:497`. If `connect()` reaches `spawn_loop` in the few-instruction window between the old loop's `break` (GaveUp, `:468`) and `loop_running.store(false)` (`:497`), the `loop_running` guard early-returns and the new cycle gets **no poll loop** (Connected, unsupervised). Practically unreachable (connect_sequence takes ≥ms; the window is instructions), but the guard could join-wait instead of returning.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-5. Tray stub `eprintln!` from a GUI-subsystem process.** `src/bin/tray.rs:5-6`: with `windows_subsystem = \"windows\"` and no console (double-click launch), the stderr handle is invalid and `eprintln!` panics (\"failed printing to stderr\") → exit 101 instead of the intended 2. Stub-only (real tray is S3); trivial to make robust (ignore the write error / drop the line).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-6. Cross-module note for S3: net-merge spawns lack CREATE_NO_WINDOW.** `netmerge.rs:134-138` (`run_full` — used by the supervisor poll loop every 5 s, `supervisor.rs:474`) sets no creation flags, unlike `core_proc.rs:149-154` for xray. Invisible from the S2 console binary (children share its console), but the S3 tray is GUI-subsystem: spawning `net-merge status` every 5 s will flash a console window. Either add the flag in netmerge or have the tray spawn through a helper that does.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-7. Metadata/hygiene nits.** `Cargo.toml` has no `repository` and no `rust-version` (lock is v4 → needs cargo ≥1.78; `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` is a moving target — pinning `rust-version` documents the floor). `release.yml:29-32` could set `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` so a path typo can't silently produce an asset-less release. No CI caching (optional; suite is fast).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## 3. Scrutiny items — detailed results",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.1 cfg gating (both host and windows-gnu compile) Audited every `#[cfg(...)]` in src (39 occurrences, grep log in session): - Windows-only API code all behind `#[cfg(windows)]`: `core_proc.rs:149-154` (CREATE_NO_WINDOW via `std::os::windows::process::CommandExt`), `sysproxy.rs:141-221` + `:225-243`/`:253-274` (winreg + WinInet, with `#[cfg(not(windows))]` no-op bodies), `elevate.rs:38-72`/`:79-110` (with non-windows stubs at `:74-77`/`:112-116`), `main.rs:311-319` (UAC relaunch), `netmerge.rs:238-244` (DETACHED_PROCESS tray launch). No POSIX-only traits inside windows blocks anywhere. - Unix-only code all behind `#[cfg(unix)]`: `OpenOptionsExt` 0600 writes (`sysproxy.rs:94-98`, `supervisor.rs:621-633`, `main.rs:107-118` — each with a `cfg(not(unix))` fallback), fake-xray shell script + all process tests (`supervisor.rs:681-1065`, `netmerge.rs:433-510`). - The `#[cfg(any(windows, test))]` trick (sysproxy/elevate pure helpers) is correct: pure helpers compile on the host for tests, real registry/UAC code only on windows; the two windows-only mapping tests (`sysproxy.rs:416-449`) are `#[cfg(windows)]`-gated and run on the Windows CI leg. - Verified BOTH sides compile: host via cargo test/clippy (all `any(windows,test)` items exercised), target via zigbuild forced rebuild + PE import table proof (§1).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.2 windows-sys 0.61 features vs referenced APIs APIs referenced (grep): `Foundation::{CloseHandle, HANDLE}`, `Security::{GetTokenInformation, TokenElevation, TOKEN_ELEVATION, TOKEN_QUERY}`, `System::Threading::{GetCurrentProcess, OpenProcessToken}`, `UI::Shell::ShellExecuteW`, `UI::WindowsAndMessaging::SW_SHOWNORMAL`, `Networking::WinInet::{InternetSetOptionW, INTERNET_OPTION_REFRESH, INTERNET_OPTION_SETTINGS_CHANGED}`. Cargo.toml features: Win32_Foundation, Win32_Security, Win32_System_Threading, Win32_System_LibraryLoader (unused — P2-1), Win32_UI_Shell, Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging, Win32_Networking_WinInet. **Complete**: every referenced module is covered; a missing feature would have failed the target compile, and the zigbuild rebuild + objdump imports (§1) prove the windows paths genuinely compiled and linked, not skipped.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.3 Tray / console subsystems `file` output (§1): `multitunnel-tray.exe` = PE32+ **GUI** (`#![cfg_attr(target_os = \"windows\", windows_subsystem = \"windows\")]` at `tray.rs:2`), `multitunnel.exe` = PE32+ **console**. Both link. Stub behavior nit = P2-5.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.4 Dependency hygiene Lock: 18 packages, **all** `registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index` — no git deps, no path deps, no wildcard requirements (`serde = \"1\"`, `regex = \"1\"` are caret reqs; lock pins exact: serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.154, regex 1.13.1, windows-sys 0.61.2, winreg 0.56.0). Transitive set is the minimum expected: regex → aho-corasick/memchr/regex-automata/regex-syntax; serde_derive → syn/quote/proc-macro2/unicode-ident; serde_json → itoa/memchr/zmij; windows-sys → windows-link; winreg → cfg-if/windows-sys. No baggage. winreg/windows-sys correctly under `[target.\"cfg(windows)\".dependencies]` so the Linux host build pulls neither. Lock committed → reproducible CI. Only nit: unused LibraryLoader feature (P2-1), metadata (P2-7).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.5 Licensing Per-package: aho-corasick / memchr — MIT OR Unlicense; cfg-if, itoa, proc-macro2, quote, syn, unicode-ident, regex*, serde*, serde_json, zmij, windows-link, windows-sys — MIT OR Apache-2.0; winreg — MIT. **No copyleft anywhere in the build graph.** Xray-core (MPL-2.0) and net-merge run as separate processes and are not redistributed (LICENSE:23-25) — no contamination. Cargo.toml: `license = \"MIT\"`, `publish = false` ✓, LICENSE file is proper MIT ✓. Open obligation: the promised THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md doesn't exist yet (P1-2).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        }
+-++      ]
+-++    },

Windows-leg caveat: new P1-A below. | | P1-2 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md missing | **FIXED** (2 nits → new P2-A) | File exists (62 lines), licenses table checked against Cargo.lock — accurate for 18/19 crates; copied unconditionally in release.yml (Test-Path guard removed only for the notices file, still present for README/QUICKSTART which don't exist — fine). | | P1-3 connect/disconnect not serialized | **FIXED** (+ my P2-4) | `op_lock: Mutex<()>` held for the whole of connect() and disconnect() (supervisor.rs:247-248, :413-414); serialization covered by new test (3c). `spawn_loop` now joins the exiting handle instead of early-returning (P2-4 fixed). +-++          "text": "## 3. Adversarial re-review of the CHANGED code (my lens)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.1 Timing margins on a loaded 2-core box (this sandbox IS 2-core) - **Drip test [350, 900) ms vs 500 ms budget**: measured 0.50–0.51 s across 15 runs including 5 under full CPU contention — the failure is produced by the kernel SO_RCVTIMEO deadline, not by user-space polling, so it is load-insensitive. Lower bound safe (no early-error path exists: connection stays open, budget is the only failure mode); upper bound has ~400 ms headroom. Sound. - **Op-lock test (300 ms block window)**: the assertion is an *invariant*, not a race outcome — while the main thread holds op_lock, the connect thread cannot have moved state regardless of scheduling, so it cannot flake slow; after release, 10 s budget for a ~50 ms refused-probe connect. Sound. - **Start-twice <1 s**: second start() checks the child slot *first* (the REV-C P0-1 fix) and errors in microseconds; measured ~0 ms; 1000× margin. Sound. - Full suite 3× green, focused subset 3× green, 30/30 individual timing-test runs green. No flakiness observed.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.2 core_proc start() reorder (REV-C P0-1 fix, cross-checked) New order (slot check → join leftover → re-check under slot lock) is correct: the waiter only outlives an *empty* slot, so the join is bounded; the unreachable second check is harmless. Concurrent start/stop on CoreProc remains impossible because op_lock serializes supervisor ops and the loop thread is joined before disconnect's core.stop(). No issue.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.3 socks_probe deadline rewrite (REV-C P1-1, cross-checked) `refresh_socket_budget` re-arms read+write timeouts before **every underlying `s.read`** (the LEDGER-documented first attempt re-armed only per read_exact — per-syscall io timeouts are what a drip defeats; the shipped loop is the correct shape). `checked_add` deadline, zero-remaining guarded (set_read_timeout(Some(0)) is an error on some platforms — guarded), write budget re-armed before CONNECT. Total probe bounded by `timeout` + ε. Verified by the drip test. No issue for my lens.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.4 elevate.rs argv quoting (REV-C P1-2, cross-checked) `quote_windows_arg` implements the canonical CommandLineToArgvW rules exactly: quote iff empty/whitespace/`\"`; n backslashes before a quote → 2n+1; trailing backslashes doubled only when quoted; unquoted args pass through untouched (unquoted trailing backslash is correct). Round-trips with the child's Rust `std::env::args` (CommandLineToArgvW). Tests cover the attack shape (`a\" --evil`) and backslash edges. Correct.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.5 CI/workflows - lint job: right components, right commands, passes on the current tree (verified with `-D warnings` locally). Caveat: it lints only the Linux cfg surface — cfg(windows) blocks are compiled by the windows-latest test job and zigbuild but never *linted* (P2-D). - release.yml: test step green locally; packaging copies both exes + config.example.json + LICENSE + THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; zip + artifact + release attach with fail_on_unmatched_files. Works on GitHub runners modulo P1-A.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.6 Licensing (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md vs Cargo.lock) All 20 lockfile packages are permissive (MIT / MIT OR Apache-2.0 / MIT OR Unlicense) — **no copyleft**; Xray-core (MPL-2.0) and net-merge are declared non-redistributed process spawns — accurate. Two accuracy nits (P2-A): `serde_core 1.0.229` (a real lockfile crate) is missing from the table, and the embedded \"MIT License\" text is truncated (ends at \"…portions of the Software.\", omitting the warranty paragraphs) while the file says \"text also embedded below\".",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3.7 Premature-push incident (LEDGER 06:19Z) 9fafc6c was pushed with 2 failing tests (the per-read_exact deadline re-arm was insufficient). Verified: current origin/main == eb1235a == the tree I verified green (57/57 ×3, clippy -D warnings clean, zigbuild green, both PEs). The red commit is superseded ~4 minutes later. Process recommendations (P2-E): (a) the orchestrator's gate chain must propagate failure — the `rg … || echo` pattern made GATE_PASSED unconditional; use `set -euo pipefail` and only run backup/push when the gate's exit code is 0; (b) make backup.sh itself run (or trust a pre-computed) gate result before pushing; (c) once CI is trusted, add required status checks on main and never cut a `v*` tag from a commit whose Actions run isn't green.",

+-++          "text": "### P1 — 1",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P1-A. Winsock accepted-socket blocking-mode ambiguity in the Windows-CI-exposed test stub (core_proc.rs `stub_socks`).** `stub_socks` now sets the listener nonblocking (my P2-3 fix) and then does `set_read_timeout(5s)` + `read_exact` on the **accepted** socket. On Linux, accept() never propagates O_NONBLOCK (all local runs green). On Windows the tests `socks_probe_success` / `socks_probe_refusal_names_status` (NOT cfg-gated) run on windows-latest in **both** ci.yml and the new release.yml test step. Microsoft's accept() docs say the accepted socket \"has the same properties as socket s, **including the asynchronous events registered with WSAAsyncSelect or WSAEventSelect**\" — event registration is documented as inherited (and those APIs force nonblocking), but the docs are **silent on FIONBIO** (which is what std's set_nonblocking uses); community folklore claims Windows accepted sockets inherit the nonblocking mode, while wine's bug-compatible accept creates a fresh default-(blocking-)state socket and copies nothing. If inheritance is real, the stub's first `read_exact` loses the race with the probe's greeting write → WSAEWOULDBLOCK → stub thread panics → red windows-latest leg (and a release-blocking `cargo test`). Nobody in this project can execute the Windows leg before merge. I could not demonstrate breakage from this sandbox, so this is P1, not P0. **Fix is one line and correct under both semantics**: after accept, `let _ = s.set_nonblocking(false);` (same for the supervisor `spawn_stub` for symmetry, though its tests are unix-gated).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P2 — 5",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-A. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md accuracy nits.** `serde_core 1.0.229` (own lockfile entry) missing from the table; the embedded MIT text is truncated before the warranty paragraphs despite \"text also embedded below\" — embed the full 5-paragraph text (per-crate copyright holder lines would be gold-plating; license identification + upstream links matches ecosystem norms).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-B. `generate`/`doctor` bypass the loopback guard.** `ensure_loopback_listen` is wired only into connect_sequence (supervisor.rs:280-282). `multitunnel generate` (main.rs, unchanged) writes a ready-to-run xray config binding the noauth SOCKS/HTTP inbounds on any configured `local.listen` (config.rs does not validate loopback either), and `doctor` never flags a non-loopback listen. Inert unless someone runs xray with the file, but it contradicts the guard's contract-#2 intent — call the helper from `generate`/`doctor` (or Config::validate).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-C. Residual of P1-3: disconnect can block ~15 s+ on op_lock** while a connect sequence is in flight (wait_for_port/probe are not stop-flag-aware; the module contract now documents this). S3 tray must call connect/disconnect from worker threads, or the loop's port-wait/probe should check the stop flag between attempts. Carry-forward note for S3.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-D. Lint job covers only the Linux cfg surface.** Add `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` to cross-check (needs only the target's std + the clippy driver) so cfg(windows) blocks are linted, not just compiled.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-E. Process: the 06:19Z premature push.** Gate-script pitfall (`rg||echo` unconditional success) pushed a red commit; recommendations in §3.7. Current remote state verified green/consistent.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        }
+-++      ]
+-++    },
+-++    {
+-++      "id": "report:s2-rev-c",
+-++      "type": "report",
+-++      "title": "S2 Review — Reviewer-C (Correctness & Security)",
+-++      "tags": [
+-++        "agent-reports"
+-++      ],

+-++        {
+-++          "text": "# S2 Review — Reviewer-C (Correctness & Security)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C (adversarial round, stage S2) - **Date:** 2026-11-13 (repo HEAD 59d7bba, branch main, clean tree — reviewed as-is) - **Scope:** `src/core_proc.rs`, `src/supervisor.rs`, `src/sysproxy.rs`, `src/elevate.rs`, `src/main.rs` (incl. embedded `#[cfg(test)]` modules); S1 modules (config/xrayconf/netmerge/error/lib) treated as stable context, cross-module contract violations flagged where seen. - **Lens:** races, deadlocks, panics, error paths, unsafe FFI, process lifecycle, contract conformance.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Verification log (run myself, trusted nothing)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `. tools/env.sh; cargo test` | **52/52 passed, 0 failed, 5.64 s** (run twice, both green) | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` | **clean** — 0 warnings / 0 errors | | `cargo fmt --check` | **clean** (exit 0) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **success** — `multitunnel.exe` (26.7 MB) + `multitunnel-tray.exe` (4.9 MB), both PE32+ |",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**Adversarial demos** (standalone crate in `/tmp/mt-revc-demo` against the repo as a path dependency; the repo itself was not modified — verified `git status` clean after):",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- `start-hang`: `CoreProc::start()` called while a child is running — **blocked past 2 s** until the child was killed externally; on unblock it returned `Ok(())` and spawned a *second* core generation. The documented `Err(\"core already running\")` never materialized. → finding **P0-1**. - `disc-race`: `disconnect()` issued while a `connect()` sequence was in flight — **returned `Ok` in 44 ms**; the connect then completed and left `state == Connected` with `loop_running() == true`. → finding **P0-2**.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "---",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## P0 — must fix before close",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` hangs (and then double-starts) when a child is already running **`src/core_proc.rs:108-116`** (doc claim at `:104`, module doc `:10-11`)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "`start()` joins the previous waiter thread **before** checking the child slot:",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "The waiter (`waiter_loop`, :333-367) only exits when the child dies, the slot empties, or the stop flag is set. So while a child is live, `join()` blocks **indefinitely**; the `is_some()` error branch is dead code on that path. When the child eventually dies, the join returns, the (now empty) slot passes the check, and `start()` spawns a *new* child and returns `Ok(())` — a silent double-generation restart the caller never asked for. This violates the method's own contract (\"Returns an error if a child is already running\") and is an unbounded block in a public lib API that stage S3 (tray) is specified to call from menu threads.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "Reachability inside the supervisor today is via P0-2's corrupted states (e.g. `State::Failed` with a live core → next `connect()` → `connect_sequence` step 2 → `core.start()` → wedged forever); it is also directly reachable by any external API user. **Fix (trivial):** check `lock(&self.child).is_some()` and return the error *before* joining the leftover waiter (the leftover join is only safe when the previous cycle's child is gone).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P0-2 — `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized as whole operations; disconnect can be silently ineffective **`src/supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect)**",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "Only the tiny state-check windows hold `inner`. `connect_sequence` performs seconds of work (config write, core spawn, up-to-15 s port wait, up-to-20 s probe, up-to-15 s bonding wait) holding **no lock and no joinable loop handle** — `spawn_loop` runs only *after* it succeeds. A concurrent `disconnect()` sees `state != Disconnected`, sets the stop flag, joins a **`None`** loop handle (`:402` — the loop doesn't exist yet), restores proxy, stops whatever core exists, sets `Disconnected`, and returns `Ok` — while `connect_sequence` keeps running. Demonstrated (44 ms disconnect during an in-flight probe): final state `Connected`, poll loop alive; with `restart_max > 0` the loop even resurrects the core the disconnect killed, and step 5 sets the **system proxy after the user disconnected**, which in the kill-window black-holes all WinINET traffic through a dead proxy.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "This is exactly the usage the module docs advertise for S3 (\"wrap the `Supervisor` in an `Arc` and call from menu handlers on any thread\", :29-31). It also compounds with P0-1: the interleaving `connect A → disconnect B (completes early) → connect C` can leave `State::Failed`/`Disconnected` with a live core, after which the next `connect()` blocks forever in `start()`'s waiter join. **Fix:** one operation-level `Mutex<()>` (or making the state transition a token) held for the whole of `connect()`/`disconnect()`; all methods are already `&self`, so this is local and cheap.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "---",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## P1 — should fix",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1-1 — `socks_probe` has per-read timeouts but no total deadline **`src/core_proc.rs:259-268, 390-393`**",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "`set_read_timeout(timeout)` bounds each `read_exact`, but a proxy that drips one byte just inside every timeout window keeps each read alive forever — the probe never returns. The contract (\"a probe against a malicious/half-open proxy must never hang\", module doc :14-16) is satisfied per-read, not per-call. Consequences: `connect()` blocks unboundedly at step 3; the poll loop stalls mid-probe (no tick, no stop-flag observation), and since `disconnect()` joins the loop thread, a tray disconnect wedges with it. Practical exposure is low (the probed proxy is our own spawned xray on loopback), hence P1 not P0. **Fix:** compute a call deadline and re-set `read_timeout` to the remaining budget before each read.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1-2 — `elevate::join_args` does not escape quotes / backslash-before-quote (argument injection into the elevated relaunch) **`src/elevate.rs:17-28`** (used at `src/main.rs:314` via `relaunch_elevated`)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "Arguments containing whitespace are wrapped in quotes but embedded `\"` is never escaped. An argument like `a\" --evil` becomes `\"a\" --evil\"`, which `CommandLineToArgvW` parses as **two** arguments (`a`, `--evil\"`) — a single crafted argv entry splits into multiple arguments in the UAC-elevated child. Similarly a path argument ending in `\\` (e.g. `-config C:\\`) corrupts: `\"C:\\\"` parses as `C:\"`. Today's exposure is same-user self-injection (the user launches the CLI), but `main.rs` forwards arbitrary `std::env::args()` verbatim, so any future caller that passes semi-trusted arguments turns this into a real elevation-boundary injection. **Fix:** proper `CommandLineToArgvW`-compatible escaping (`\"` → `\\\"`, doubling trailing backslashes before a closing quote).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1-3 — cross-module: `local.listen` is never validated to be loopback (contract #2) **`src/config.rs:234-263` (validate), `src/xrayconf.rs:20,27` (binds verbatim), `src/supervisor.rs:609-616` (socks_addr/http_addr)**",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "`Config::validate` checks server fields and port collision only. A config with `\"listen\": \"0.0.0.0\"` passes validation, is bound verbatim by **both** xray inbounds — the SOCKS inbound is `\"auth\": \"noauth\"` (`xrayconf.rs:23`) — exposing an unauthenticated SOCKS+HTTP proxy to the LAN, and becomes the WinINET `ProxyServer` value. This directly violates the lib.rs architecture contract #2 (\"the core exposes loopback-only SOCKS/HTTP inbounds\"). Defaults are safe (`127.0.0.1`) and `doctor` only checks parseability (`main.rs:237`), so it is a config-reachable footgun rather than an exploit — but the S2 supervisor is the natural enforcement point (fail `connect_sequence` if `socks_addr`/`http_addr` is not loopback), or add the check to `Config::validate` in a follow-up. Flagged as a cross-module contract violation per stage instructions (config.rs is S1-closed).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "---",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## P2 — nits / robustness",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        }
+-++      ]
+-++    },
+-++    {

+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C (adversarial round 2; round-1 verdict was BLOCK: P0-1, P0-2, P1-1, P1-2, P1-3) - **Date:** 2026-11-13 (repo HEAD `eb1235a`, branch main, clean tree — reviewed as-is, no files modified) - **Scope:** verification of the claimed fixes on top of `59d7bba`, adversarial re-review of all changed code (`core_proc.rs`, `supervisor.rs`, `elevate.rs`, `netmerge.rs`, `bin/tray.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, workflows, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), plus regression thinking around the new designs.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Verification log (run myself, trusted nothing)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `git log --oneline -6` | `eb1235a` ← `9fafc6c` (s2-fix-round-1) ← `59d7bba` (round-1 tree) — history as claimed | | `git diff 59d7bba..HEAD --stat` | 12 files: src/{core_proc,supervisor,elevate,netmerge,bin/tray}.rs, Cargo.toml, 2 workflows, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, LEDGER, 2 agent reports. config/sysproxy/main/xrayconf/error/lib **untouched** (consistent with S1-closed + my P1-3 being fixed at the supervisor) | | `cargo test` | **57/57 passed, 0 failed** in 6.04 s — run **4× total**, all green (6.04/5.99/6.05 s), incl. all 5 new tests | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` | **clean** — 0 warnings / 0 errors | | `cargo fmt --check` | **clean** (exit 0) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **success** (both binaries, current sources) |",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**Round-1 adversarial demos re-run against the fixed tree** (same `/tmp/mt-revc-demo` crate, path-dep rebuilt at `eb1235a`; repo untouched):",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- `start-hang` (was: >2 s hang, then silent double-start): second `start()` now returns **`Err(\"core already running: …\")` promptly** → **P0-1 fixed, empirically**. - `disc-race` (was: disconnect Ok in 44 ms, tunnel left Connected + loop alive): disconnect now **blocks on op_lock for the in-flight connect (3.66 s), then completes the teardown** — final `state == Disconnected`, `loop_running == false` → **P0-2 fixed, empirically** (semantics correctly changed from \"lost teardown\" to \"serialized teardown\").",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "---",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Fix-by-fix verification (my round-1 IDs)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` waiter-join hang — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/core_proc.rs:105-124`: the child-slot check is now FIRST (`:109-111`) and returns the documented `Err`; the leftover-waiter join (`:115-117`) runs only when the slot is empty; a re-check under the slot lock (`:119-124`) covers the join window. Verified:",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **Soundness of the join:** with the slot empty, the old waiter has either exited or will observe `None` within one 50 ms poll (`waiter_loop`, :346-380) — the join is bounded. The re-check under the slot lock closes the TOCTOU between first check and join completion. - **Concurrent `start()`×2:** the slot lock is held across the whole spawn+publish region (`:119-198`), so a loser blocks at its first check and then sees `Some` → Err. No double-spawn. - **The orchestrator's question (child dies between check and join):** if a child is alive at the first check → immediate Err (no join). If the slot is empty, the join cannot wait on a live child — the waiter's exit conditions don't depend on any child. ✓ - Empirical demo + new test `start_while_running_errors_promptly` (`<1 s` bound on an instant Err — µs in practice, huge margin). ✓ - **Residual (new P1-1 below):** a theoretical hang remains for *concurrent external* `start()` calls hitting the ~50 ms window where the old waiter hasn't exited yet and another `start()` publishes a fresh child the old waiter then adopts. Not reachable through `Supervisor` (see op_lock analysis), so P1 hardening, not P0.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P0-2 — connect/disconnect not serialized — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/supervisor.rs:178,209,247-248,413-414`: `Shared::op_lock: Mutex<()>` acquired for the **whole body** of `connect()` and `disconnect()`; poison-tolerant `lock()`; guard released by RAII on every path. Verified by demo (above) and by `connect_waits_for_op_lock_of_in_flight_operation` (a blocked connect cannot even set `Connecting`). **Deadlock analysis (the specific question):**",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- `op_lock` is taken **only** by `connect()`/`disconnect()` (grep: :248, :414 + test) — the poll loop, restart campaign, and all helpers never take it. `disconnect()` joining the loop while holding op_lock therefore cannot deadlock; worst case it waits out one bounded blocking call (see below). - Lock nesting is strictly one-way: op_lock → {inner, loop_thread, core locks}, never the reverse; every inner/loop_thread acquisition is a standalone short statement. No ABBA cycle. - `spawn_loop` (`:391-408`) drops the loop_thread guard **before** joining and re-acquires after — and both `spawn_loop` and `disconnect` (the only slot writers) run under op_lock, so the re-acquire window is race-free. The old `loop_running` early-return (REV-B P2-4) is gone; the join target is provably exited: the only paths leaving a handle in the slot are give-up (loop already returned — `loop_running=false` is its final statement) or a just-exiting give-up thread (ns window). A *live* loop implies state Connecting/Connected, for which `connect()` no-ops before `spawn_loop` — so joining a live loop is unreachable. - Loop-join blocking is bounded: ticks sleep in 100 ms stoppable slices, campaigns re-check the stop flag every iteration, `wait_for_port` ≤ 15 s, `socks_probe` now has a **total** deadline (P1-1 fix), netmerge calls have hard timeouts. So `disconnect()` holds op_lock at most ~15-30 s; a concurrent connect waits, then sees the settled state. Serialization latency, not a hang — and it is exactly what makes the round-1 race impossible.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1-1 — `socks_probe` total deadline — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/core_proc.rs:271-277, 402-440`. The design is correct this time and the reasoning in the fix note is right: socket timeouts are per-underlying-syscall, so the budget must be re-armed before **every** `read` call, not per logical read. Verified in detail:",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- `refresh_socket_budget` (:404-420): `checked_duration_since` (None → Err) + explicit `is_zero` guard, then sets BOTH read and write timeouts to the remaining budget. No panic; errors are `socks5:`-prefixed. - `socks_read_exact` (:427-…): manual fill loop — re-arms the budget before each `s.read`, `Ok(0)` → clean \"connection closed\" error, io errors (incl. `TimedOut`/`WouldBlock` from the shrunken window) propagate with context, `filled` arithmetic cannot exceed `buf.len()` (read contract), empty buffer → no-op Ok. **No panic surface.** - Every reply phase (greeting, head, ATYP length, drain) passes the same deadline; the CONNECT write is preceded by its own refresh (:304). Total probe time ≤ `timeout` + ε for any drip schedule: each read's timeout is the *remaining* budget, so the deadline is a hard ceiling. - The new test drips 12 valid SOCKS5 reply bytes at 80 ms intervals against a 500 ms budget and asserts Err in **[350, 900) ms**. Timing analysis on a loaded 2-core box: in *every* delivery schedule the probe errors at ~500 ms (a delayed drip merely moves the failing read to the deadline; an on-time drip completes the head at ~480 ms and the drain read then has ~20 ms left), so the window has ≥150 ms lower / ≥400 ms upper margin — the tightest test in the suite but sound; observed stable across my 4 runs. Without the fix the probe returns Ok at ~880 ms and the test fails on `expect_err` — it genuinely pins the bug.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1-2 — argv quoting — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/elevate.rs:35-77`: `quote_windows_arg` implements the full `CommandLineToArgvW` rules. Verified against the rules case by case: n backslashes before a quote → `2n+1` (parses back as n literal backslashes + non-toggling quote) ✓; backslashes before any other char → literal ✓; trailing backslashes doubled before the closing quote ✓; bare args (no whitespace/quote, non-empty) untouched — so bare `C:\\` round-trips without the trailing-backslash trap ✓; empty → `\"\"` ✓; quote-only arg `\"` → `\"\\\"\"` ✓. The round-1 injection case `a\" --evil` now produces `\"a\\\" --evil\"` → re-parses to the **single** original argument (tested). `join_args` keeps the space separator. Tests cover `a\" --evil`, `C:\\my dir\\`, bare `C:\\`, `a\\b\"c`, plain `a\\b`. Correct.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1-3 — loopback enforcement — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/supervisor.rs:279-281, 616-634`: `ensure_loopback_listen` runs at connect step 0.5 — after the stale-proxy self-heal, **before** any config write or core spawn, so a bad `listen` fails fast into `State::Failed` with a clear message. Correctness: `\"localhost\"` allowed (ASCII case-insensitive), IP parse → `IpAddr::is_loopback()` — which covers the whole `127.0.0.0/8` (`127.9.9.9` ✓) and `::1` ✓; `0.0.0.0`, `::`, private/link-local IPs, garbage and empty strings are all rejected with `local.listen`-named errors (tested exhaustively). Non-IP strings like `192.168.1.5:1080` (bad config shapes) are rejected rather than guessed ✓. Note: `restart_campaign` doesn't re-check, but the config is immutable per Supervisor and connect_sequence validated it before the loop can exist — sound. Config.rs untouched as agreed (S1-closed).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P2-1 — misleading \"~100 ms disconnect\" doc — **FIXED** `src/supervisor.rs:32-37`: now says \"honored within ~100 ms **while the loop is between blocking calls**; worst case one wait_for_port/probe window (~15 s) finishes first\" — accurate.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "---",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Other diffs — quick adversarial pass (nothing violating my lens)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **`src/bin/tray.rs`** (REV-B P2-5): GUI-subsystem stderr writes via `let _ = writeln!(…)` instead of `eprintln!` — correct; `eprintln!` panics on a failed stderr write (exit 101); now best-effort + intended exit 2. ✓ - **`src/netmerge.rs:139-145`** (REV-B P2-6): `CREATE_NO_WINDOW (0x0800_0000)` on `run_full` spawns — right constant, right place (the 5 s status polls from the future S3 GUI tray); `ensure_running`'s tray spawn keeps its own DETACHED_PROCESS flags. ✓ - **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: fmt + clippy `-D warnings` gate — good. **`release.yml`**: tests before release build, `fail_on_unmatched_files: true`, ships THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md — good. **`Cargo.toml`**: dropped unused `Win32_System_LibraryLoader` (zigbuild green confirms), +repository, +`rust-version = \"1.78\"` (all APIs used are ≤1.78: let-else 1.65, OnceLock 1.70, checked_duration_since 1.39, Duration::is_zero 1.53). ✓ - **`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`**: cross-checked against Cargo.lock — the serde_json deps listed (itoa, zmij) match the lock file in this environment; license table is accurate; the \"user runs separately\" section correctly separates Xray-core (MPL-2.0, not redistributed) from shipped crates. ✓ - **`LEDGER.md` / agent reports**: bookkeeping only. ✓",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## New findings this round",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1 1. **`src/core_proc.rs:112-117`** — residual hang in `start()`'s leftover-waiter join under *concurrent external* API use: if two threads call `CoreProc::start()` in the ~50 ms window after a child died but before its waiter exited, thread A can take and join the old waiter while thread B spawns and publishes a **new** child — the old waiter then sees `Some(new child)`, adopts it, and polls as long as it lives, so A's join blocks indefinitely. **Not reachable through `Supervisor`** (op_lock serializes every `core.start()` call site: connect_sequence under op_lock; restart_campaign only runs from a live poll loop, which implies state Connecting/Connected, for which connect() no-ops — I verified there is no state in which both can run), so this is pub-API hardening, not a shipped-path deadlock. Suggested one-liner: only join `is_finished()` handles, else drop (detach) them — the exiting waiter needs no join.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P2 (new this round) 1. `src/core_proc.rs:283-284, 304-306` — the two `write_all` legs re-arm the budget once per call, so a *theoretical* adversarial partial-write schedule could stretch a write leg past the deadline (multiple full `remaining` windows inside one `write_all`). Physically irrelevant here (3 / ≤262-byte writes, kernel-buffered), but a per-syscall write helper would make the bound airtight like the read side. 2. `src/core_proc.rs:262-266` — `socks_probe` method doc still describes only per-socket timeouts (\"nothing blocks forever\"); the actual guarantee is now the total deadline — one sentence would align doc and mechanism. 3. `src/supervisor.rs:246-256` — `connect()`'s Connecting/Connected no-op check happens *after* acquiring op_lock, so a redundant connect during a long in-flight operation (worst case ~50 s: 15 s port wait + 20 s probe + 15 s bond wait) blocks the caller instead of returning the no-op promptly. Correctness-first tradeoff is fine (and the simplest race-free form), but a fast-path pre-check would spare S3 tray threads the wait.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P2 (carried from round 1, unaddressed, non-blocking) 4. `core_proc.rs:384-400` — two detached pump threads append to `xray.log` concurrently; `write_all` may split → interleaved partial lines (log-only). 5. `sysproxy.rs:228-233` — registry snapshot reads use `.ok()`: type-mismatched values (REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_BINARY `ProxyServer`) snapshot as absent and restore then deletes them; mid-`set` failure leaves `ProxyEnable=1` half-applied until restore. 6. `supervisor.rs:634-653` / `main.rs:106-123` — `write_private` truncates in place (no temp+rename); crash mid-write leaves a partial `xray-client.json`. 7. `supervisor.rs:613-620` — `parse_probe_target` has no IPv6-literal support (brackets not stripped). 8. `main.rs:168` — `doctor` runs `xray version` with no timeout (hung binary hangs doctor). 9. `core_proc.rs:472-477` / `supervisor.rs:722-725` (test-only) — `free_loopback_port` released-port reuse race. 10. `config.rs:200-202` + `sysproxy.rs:239-241` — an empty `proxyOverride` silently becomes the default (can't be disabled via config); `set()` skips writing it when empty, leaving a previous override in force. 11. `main.rs:23` — `--config=path` equals-form unsupported (space-separated only, usage-documented).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {

+-++          "text": "# S3 Implementation — Tray (notification-area UI)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **Implementer:** S3 agent (implementation round, stage S3) - **Date:** 2026-11-13, repo base fe613ab (S2 closed), branch main - **Scope:** new `src/tray.rs` (+`pub mod tray;` in lib.rs), real GUI binary `src/bin/tray.rs`, new `assets/icon.ico` + `scripts/make_icon.py`. No frozen S1/S2 module was modified (lib.rs change is the additive module decl + one doc line; main.rs untouched).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## What was built",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 1. `src/tray.rs` (1353 lines: ~316 pure / ~602 win32 / ~376 tests / stub)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**Pure helpers** (`#[cfg(any(windows, test))]`, all host-tested — the sysproxy/elevate pattern):",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "| Helper | Purpose | |---|---| | `state_word` / `state_line` | lifecycle state → menu/tooltip wording | | `links_line` | `Links: N (merging)` / `Links: bonding off` / `Links: unavailable` | | `snippet` | first line of an error, capped, with ellipsis | | `tooltip_text` | state line + error/bond/probe snippets (blank errors skipped) | | `tip_array` | NIF_TIP-safe `[u16;128]`: ≤127 UTF-16 units + NUL, never splits a surrogate pair across units 126/127 | | `ico_entries` / `ico_image_bytes` | ICO directory parse + RT_ICON entry selection (exact → largest-fits → largest overall; empty/out-of-bounds rejected) | | `status_dump` / `status_dump_path` / `write_status_dump` | snapshot pretty-JSON + raw net-merge status → `state_dir/net-merge-status.txt` | | `Cmd` / `MenuEntry` / `menu_plan` / `id_for_cmd` / `cmd_from_id` | full menu as a pure plan; Connect/Disconnect enablement per state |",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**Windows implementation** (`mod win`, all FFI through windows-sys 0.61.2, **no new Cargo features** — only the already-enabled Win32_Foundation/Win32_UI_Shell/Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging):",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **Window**: `CreateWindowExW` with the predefined `\"STATIC\"` system class, `HWND_MESSAGE` parent, style 0 (message-only, never shown) — no RegisterClass. Subclassed with `SetWindowLongPtrW(GWLP_WNDPROC)`; unhandled messages → `DefWindowProcW` (the STATIC proc only matters during creation, before the subclass is installed). - **Tray icon**: `Shell_NotifyIconW` NIM_ADD with NIF_MESSAGE|NIF_ICON|NIF_TIP; callback = `WM_APP+1`; tooltip refreshed by `SetTimer` 1 s → WM_TIMER → NIM_MODIFY only when the text changed (redundant updates skipped). - **Menu**: rebuilt FRESH from `supervisor.snapshot()` at every open via `CreatePopupMenu`/`AppendMenuW`/`TrackPopupMenuEx(TPM_RIGHTBUTTON | TPM_BOTTOMALIGN)`/`DestroyMenu`; KB Q135788 pattern (SetForegroundWindow before, WM_NULL after) so the menu dismisses when clicking elsewhere. - **Icon embedding**: `include_bytes!(\"../assets/icon.ico\")` → `ico_image_bytes(.., 32)` (RT_ICON payload, NOT the directory) → `CreateIconFromResourceEx(.., 0x00030000, 32, 32, LR_DEFAULTCOLOR)`; fallback `LoadIconW(NULL, IDI_APPLICATION)` (shared, never destroyed — tracked by `icon_owned`). - **Handler state**: `thread_local RefCell<Option<&'static TrayCtx>>` with a `Box::leak`'d context — no GWLP_USERDATA pointer juggling; handlers copy the `&'static` out and drop the borrow guard immediately, so re-entrancy during the `TrackPopupMenuEx` modal loop is safe. - **Threading contract honored**: `connect`/`disconnect` ALWAYS run on `std::thread` workers (they hold the supervisor op_lock, up to ~15 s); nothing blocking ever runs in the window procedure.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2. `assets/icon.ico` + `scripts/make_icon.py` (142 lines, stdlib-only, deterministic)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "32×32 + 16×16 BMP-format ICO entries (BITMAPINFOHEADER with doubled biHeight, bottom-up 32-bpp BGRA XOR rows, 1-bpp AND mask with 4-byte row padding). Motif: dark-navy `#0D1B2A` rounded square with two parallel link bars `#4FC3F7` (sky) over `#4ADE80` (emerald) — bonded links, pure geometry, no text/emoji. Entry layout validated byte-by-byte (biSize=40, biWidth=n, biHeight=2n, comp=BI_RGB) and by a Rust unit test.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 3. `src/bin/tray.rs` (108 lines) — real GUI binary",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "`#![cfg_attr(target_os = \"windows\", windows_subsystem = \"windows\")]` kept. Elevation check first (Windows: `!is_elevated()` → `relaunch_elevated(args)` + exit 0, original args ride along so `--config` survives). Config: explicit `-config/--config` arg → beside the exe → cwd fallback; when nothing exists, template lands beside the exe plus a friendly `config-needed.txt` note (GUI-app equivalent of the console bin's message) and exit 2. Then `Arc<Supervisor>` + `tray::run`. Non-Windows: stub `run` returns Err → stderr line + exit 2, same as the pre-S3 stub.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Key FFI decisions (for the unsafe reviewer)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "1. **RT_ICON bytes, not the file**: `CreateIconFromResourceEx` requires the image bytes an ICONDIRENTRY points at; passing the whole ICO file is the classic mistake. `ico_image_bytes` extracts+bounds-checks the slice; a unit test pins the 32×32 entry's header (biSize=40/biWidth=32/biHeight=64). 2. **STATIC + GWLP_WNDPROC subclass** instead of RegisterClass (fewer moving parts, per the stage spec). The previous proc pointer is checked non-null; we intentionally call `DefWindowProcW` (not `CallWindowProcW` on the saved STATIC proc) for unhandled messages — a message-only window never uses static-control behavior after creation. 3. **No GWLP_USERDATA**: state flows through a thread-local `&'static` (single window, single message thread). Eliminates the classic create-then-SetWindowLongPtrW race and null-deref windows entirely. 4. **Re-entrancy**: `TrackPopupMenuEx` runs a modal loop that re-enters the window procedure (WM_TIMER during the menu, etc.) — no `RefCell` borrow guard is ever held across it (guards close inside `ctx()`/small blocks). 5. **Icon ownership**: `CreateIconFromResourceEx` HICON is destroyed in teardown; `LoadIconW` fallback is shared and never destroyed (`icon_owned` flag). 6. **`NOTIFYICONDATAW` init**: struct literal with `..Default::default()` (all-zero is the valid Win32 \"unused\" state); `cbSize` set from `size_of`. 7. Every one of the 32 `unsafe` blocks carries a `SAFETY:` comment; error paths use `std::io::Error::last_os_error()` (thread-safe errno) rather than raw `GetLastError`.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Test / gate results (all run in-session)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "| Gate | Result | |---|---| | `cargo fmt --check` | clean | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` (host) | 0 warnings | | `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | 0 warnings | | `cargo test` | **77/77 passed** (was 57; +20 tray tests, ~6 s) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | both bins link | | `file .../multitunnel-tray.exe` | **PE32+ GUI subsystem, x86-64** (console bin still PE32+ console) |",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "New tests: state labels (4 states), links line 3 modes, tooltip clean/snippets/first-line-cap/blank-skip, tip_array NUL/cap-127/surrogate pair (incl. boundary at unit 126), ICO embedded-asset parse + DIB header assertions, ICO preference order (exact → fits → largest), ICO rejection (bad magic/cursor type/reserved/truncated/len-0/out-of-bounds), status dump content/placeholder/overwrite, menu enablement per state, menu structure (11 rows, separators, labels), cmd id roundtrip. Host stub behavior of the binary verified manually (missing-config template + note beside exe + exit 2; cwd fallback config loads; Windows-only stub message + exit 2).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Deviations / notes",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- **Tooltip also surfaces the top-level `snapshot.error`** (in addition to the specified bond/probe snippets): a Failed state without it would show no reason at all. Same snippet/first-line/cap rules; documented in helper docs. - **`Links: unavailable`** = enabled + not merging (disconnected or bonding down) — matches the three-way spec wording; merging with zero parsed links renders `Links: 0 (merging)` (count is the truth, never invented). - Menu placement flags: `TPM_RIGHTBUTTON | TPM_BOTTOMALIGN` (bottom-align is standard tray behavior so the menu grows up from the cursor). - Left-click and right-click both open the menu (task says \"on the icon click\"; no separate double-click action specified). - `scripts/make_icon.py` committed alongside `assets/icon.ico` per task; output is deterministic (re-running reproduces byte-identical file). - Raw net-merge status in the dump comes from the supervisor snapshot's `raw_status` (last poll) rather than shelling out to `net-merge status` at click time — a 10 s CLI call would block the menu handler. - P2 backlog from S2 (config loopback check, temp+rename writes, etc.) untouched — out of S3 scope.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "---",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {

+-++        {
+-++          "text": "Base: 81c7e72 (reviews s3-rev-c.md / s3-rev-b.md on top of my 0fb81f0). All three P1s fixed; supervisor change is the ONE additive pub fn approved by the orchestrator — no frozen signature touched.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Fix 1 — Reviewer-C P1-1: Exit could orphan the tunnel",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "- `src/supervisor.rs`: additive `pub fn emergency_stop(&self)` (module-doc contract line added; full semantics in the method docs). Takes NO op_lock: (1) sets the poll-loop stop flag — `spawn_loop` resets it at the next cycle, so future connects are not poisoned; (2) `core.stop()` (kill+reap, CoreProc's own mutexes, idempotent); (3) `sysproxy::restore(state_dir)` best-effort; (4) snapshot → `State::Failed` with error \"emergency stop after exit timeout\", `merging`/`system_proxy` cleared. `netmerge::off` is deliberately NOT called (10 s CLI timeout would defeat the fast path; next `connect()` re-syncs via `ensure_running`) — reasoning in the doc comment. - `src/tray.rs` `exit_app`: NIM_DELETE → normal disconnect worker → `recv_timeout(EXIT_WAIT=2 s)`; **on timeout** → `emergency_stop()` on the message thread (kill+reap+registry restore only — pump-block bounded) → `recv_timeout(EMERGENCY_WAIT=1 s)` → `PostQuitMessage`. New const `EMERGENCY_WAIT`. - Test `supervisor::tests::emergency_stop_works_while_op_lock_is_held` (host-runnable, unix rig): connect against the working stub, HOLD op_lock directly (the serialization-test pattern), call `emergency_stop()` — asserts < 2 s elapsed (never blocks on op_lock), core killed+reaped (`core.running()==false`), state Failed, exact error string, merging + proxy flags cleared; then the rig's deterministic disconnect proves no stuck state remains (lands Disconnected). Suite 77 → 78; supervisor subset 11/11 ×3 single-threaded, test itself 0.06 s.",

+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## Fix 2 — Reviewer-C P1-2: TaskbarCreated not handled",

+-++          "text": "- Stage: S3 adversarial review, Reviewer-B (build/portability/dependency hygiene/licensing/test-quality lens) - Repo: /home/z/my-project/MultiTunnel, branch main, HEAD **81c7e72** (working tree clean; `git ls-remote` confirms origin/main == 81c7e72 — the pushed tree is the one verified below). S3 landed in 0fb81f0 on top of S2-close fe613ab. - Scope: src/tray.rs (1354 lines), src/bin/tray.rs, assets/icon.ico, scripts/make_icon.py, lib.rs (additive), Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock (expected unchanged), CI workflows, +20 tests (57→77). - No project files modified. Environment writes only: regenerated the icon to /tmp for byte-comparison (cleaned up), ran the host tray stub binary in /tmp (cleaned up), rust-src component already installed in S2 round 2.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## 1. Verification log (all run by me on 81c7e72)",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `git show 0fb81f0 --stat` | 6 files: assets/icon.ico (5430 B), s3-implementation.md, scripts/make_icon.py, src/bin/tray.rs, src/lib.rs (+2), src/tray.rs (1353) — **no frozen module touched, no workflow/Cargo change** | | `cargo test` (run 1) | **77/77 ok**, 5.96 s, 0 ignored | | `cargo test` (runs 2–3) | 77/77 ok, 6.05 s / 6.05 s | | `cargo test` under full 2-core load (2 busy-loops) | **77/77 ok**, 6.38 s | | `cargo test --lib -- supervisor:: core_proc:: tray:: --test-threads=1` (×3) | **37/37 ok ×3** (7.39/7.36/7.27 s) — timing-sensitive subset single-threaded | | `cargo test --lib -- tray:: --test-threads=1` (×5) | **20/20 ok ×5, 0.00 s each** — the new tests are pure/instant | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` (forced rebuild after touch) | clean, no warnings | | `cargo clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -- -D warnings` | **clean** — compiles the entire `mod win` FFI for the target with `-D warnings`; proves every import resolves against windows-sys 0.61.2's mapping | | `cargo fmt --check` | clean | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (after touch) | green, \"Compiling multitunnel v0.1.0\" | | `file …/*.exe` | `multitunnel-tray.exe` **PE32+ GUI**, x86-64; `multitunnel.exe` **PE32+ console** — subsystems correct | | `objdump -p multitunnel-tray.exe` | imports **Shell_NotifyIconW** (shell32), **CreateWindowExW / AppendMenuW / TrackPopupMenuEx / CreateIconFromResourceEx / SetWindowLongPtrW / GetMessageW** (user32) + wininet/advapi32 (lib sysproxy/elevate) — the tray FFI genuinely compiled and linked for the target ",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**Test stability: 13/13 green runs (5 full incl. 1 under full 2-core load; 3 subset single-threaded; 5 tray-only single-threaded), 0 flakes.**",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## 2. Scrutiny items — results",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.1 cfg gating & both-sides compilation Pure helpers are `#[cfg(any(windows, test))]` (the sysproxy/elevate pattern): host non-test builds compile only the non-Windows `run` stub; host test builds compile helpers + 20 tests; Windows builds compile everything incl. `mod win`. No POSIX-only trait inside windows code; no windows API leaks onto the host. `ICON_BYTES` (`include_bytes!`) is cfg'd `any(windows, test)` so even the asset embedding is absent from the host non-test build. Both sides verified by clippy clean on host AND on the windows-gnu target with `-D warnings`. The lib.rs change is purely additive (doc line + `pub mod tray;`).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.2 windows-sys feature list vs APIs used (item 8) mod win references: Foundation `{HWND, LPARAM, LRESULT, POINT, WPARAM}`; UI::Shell `{Shell_NotifyIconW, NOTIFYICONDATAW, NIF_*, NIM_*}`; UI::WindowsAndMessaging `{AppendMenuW, CreateIconFromResourceEx, CreatePopupMenu, CreateWindowExW, DefWindowProcW, DestroyIcon, DestroyMenu, DestroyWindow, DispatchMessageW, GetCursorPos, GetMessageW, KillTimer, LoadIconW, PostMessageW, PostQuitMessage, SetForegroundWindow, SetTimer, SetWindowLongPtrW, TrackPopupMenuEx, TranslateMessage, GWLP_WNDPROC, HICON, HMENU, HWND_MESSAGE, IDI_APPLICATION, LR_DEFAULTCOLOR, MF_*, MSG, TPM_*, WM_*}`. All inside the three already-enabled features (Win32_Foundation, Win32_UI_Shell, Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging) — **no new features needed, none added**. `CreateIconFromResourceEx`'s windows-sys 0.61.2 signature matches the call site (verified by the target clippy + link; the crate declares the same mapping for gnu and MSVC, so the windows-latest MSVC leg compiles identically — windows-sys has no target-specific declarations for these). `SetWindowLongPtrW` exists only on 64-bit targets — fine, the project targets x86_64 only. `HWND_MESSAGE`, `IDI_APPLICATION` (PCWSTR), `WM_APP` all resolve. The `-D warnings` cross clippy is the machine proof; the PE import list is the link proof.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.3 GUI-subsystem discipline (item 9) Grep over src: every `println!`/`eprintln!` lives in main.rs (the console binary) or in test code. The tray paths use only `let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr(), …)` (bin main + `log_err`) — the S2-verified non-panicking form. Error/first-run flows are file-based: template + `config-needed.txt` beside the exe (verified by running the host binary). `spawn_detached` targets GUI apps (notepad.exe, explorer.exe) so no console flash even from the GUI-subsystem process. Clean.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.4 Custom build tooling — icon (item 6) - **Deterministic**: stdlib-only (`os/struct/sys`), no RNG, no timestamps, no environment dependence; accepts an output path, so I regenerated to /tmp: `cmp` reports the committed 5430-byte `assets/icon.ico` **byte-identical** to regeneration. - **Format validity** (independent python parse + `file`): ICONDIR reserved=0/type=1/count=2; entries 32×32 (offset 38, 4264 B) and 16×16 (offset 4302, 1128 B); each payload is a BITMAPINFOHEADER with biSize=40, biWidth=n, biHeight=2n (XOR+AND doubled), planes=1, 32 bpp, BI_RGB, and biSizeImage == 40 + n²·4 + padded-AND — exactly the RT_ICON shape `CreateIconFromResourceEx` consumes; XOR rows bottom-up BGRA; corners fully transparent (AND bit set), center navy (42,27,13,255); file ends exactly at the last image (no trailing bytes). `file(1)`: \"MS Windows icon resource - 2 icons, 32x32, 32 bits/pixel, 16x16, 32 bits/pixel\". - **No emoji**: the only non-ASCII bytes in make_icon.py are em-dashes (U+2014) in comments — punctuation, consistent with repo style; the motif is pure geometry (navy rounded square + two link bars), no text/emoji. - The Rust side pins the 32×32 DIB header in a unit test (biSize=40/biWidth=32/biHeight=64).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.5 Licensing (item 7) Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock **byte-identical to S2-close** — zero new dependencies, so the S2 notices file remains accurate. The icon is original work generated by the project's own committed script (pure geometry, no third-party artwork) → covered by the project MIT license; scripts/make_icon.py is project source. No copyleft, no contamination. My S2 round-2 follow-ups (serde_core row + full MIT text, windows-target clippy in cross-check, `set_nonblocking(false)` in the core_proc stub) verified present at fe613ab.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.6 Test quality (item 10) 20 new tests, all host-runnable against the pure helpers: state labels (all 4 states), links line (3 modes + 0-link edge), tooltip (clean / error+bond+probe / first-line cap at 48 / blank-skip), tip_array (NUL termination, 127-unit cap with slot-127 reserved, surrogate-pair boundary at unit 126, intact pair), ICO (embedded asset parse + DIB header asserts, preference order exact→fits→largest, rejection: empty/truncated/cursor-type/reserved/count-mismatch/len-0/out-of-bounds), status dump (content, placeholder, create-dirs + overwrite semantics), menu (enablement matrix across 4 states, 11-row structure with separators and labels, links line per config), cmd id roundtrip incl. 0/999/0xFFFF. None `#[ignore]`d (run reports 0 ignored); none vacuous — every one asserts exact strings/indices/bytes. Deterministic: no sleeps, clocks, sockets, or processes; the file-based dump test uses the pid+counter unique-dir pattern. 5/5 single-threaded runs at 0.00 s. All Windows-leg-safe (temp dirs + file IO only). One hygiene nit → P2-1.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### 2.7 CI sanity - ci.yml test leg (windows-latest, MSVC) compiles the tray module: same windows-sys crate and feature set proven to compile on windows-gnu; no MSVC-vs-mingw declaration divergence for these APIs. - lint job (host clippy -D warnings) and cross-check (zigbuild + windows-gnu clippy -D warnings, added at S2-close) both cover the new module and pass locally on the exact commands. - release.yml already packages `multitunnel-tray.exe`; the icon is embedded via `include_bytes!`, so the release zip has no runtime asset dependency. No workflow changes needed for S3 — and none were made.",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## 3. Findings by severity",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P0 — none Cross-build green and machine-proven (target clippy -D warnings + zigbuild + PE imports); no new dependencies; no license change; CI workflows cover the new code on all three legs (host test, windows test, cross lint+build).",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P1 — 1",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P1-1. Menu-dismiss pattern on a message-only window is runtime-unverifiable from this sandbox (tray.rs `show_menu`, :839-886).** The KB Q135788 fix calls `SetForegroundWindow(hwnd)` before `TrackPopupMenuEx` (return value discarded) so the menu dismisses when the user clicks elsewhere. `hwnd` is a **message-only** window (child of `HWND_MESSAGE`, style 0, never shown). Activation is a top-level-window concept; if `SetForegroundWindow` is a no-op for a message-only child (plausible per its docs — the call activates the window and brings its thread to the foreground), the classic stuck-menu bug returns despite the pattern being present. Nobody has run this tray on real Windows yet, and it cannot be exercised from Linux. Not build/CI-breaking and not UB — but it should be smoke-tested on real Windows before the first release, or the window created as a **hidden top-level** window (no `HWND_MESSAGE` parent, never shown — the pattern .NET NotifyIcon and the tray-icon crate use), which also keeps `Shell_NotifyIconW` callbacks working. Cross-lens flag for the unsafe reviewer to confirm.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "### P2 — 4",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-1. Temp-dir leak in one new test.** `write_status_dump_creates_dirs_and_overwrites` (tray.rs:1249-1263) never `remove_dir_all`s its unique dir — the only test in the crate that doesn't clean up after itself (the S1/S2 review criterion). One line fixes it.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-2. Exit's 2 s disconnect bound gives up on a legitimate ~15 s teardown.** `exit_app` (EXIT_WAIT=2 s) races the supervisor op_lock/poll-loop join that can legally take up to ~15 s; on timeout the process exits mid-disconnect, potentially leaving the system proxy set and net-merge on until the next launch (step-0 self-heal covers it, and the bound is a deliberate anti-hang). Documented trade-off — consider a brief \"shutting down…\" tooltip update or a slightly larger bound; behavior is safe, just occasionally untidy.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-3. Embedded-asset test under-pins the icon.** `ico_embedded_asset_parses_with_32_entry` asserts the 32×32 DIB header only; a drifted or hand-edited icon.ico would still pass. Cheap hardening: also assert the 16×16 DIB header and the total file length (5430) so any divergence from make_icon.py's deterministic output is caught (a full byte-compare needs python and can't live in cargo test).",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**P2-4. `spawn_detached` silently drops spawn failures** (`let _ = Command::…spawn()`) for notepad/explorer — both are inbox Windows components, so this is a nit; a `log_err` on failure would make a missing-shell case diagnosable.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "## 4. Verdict",
+-++          "kind": "title"
+-++        },
+-++        {
+-++          "text": "**APPROVE** — 0 P0. All mandatory gates pass on my own runs (77/77 ×5 incl. full-load, 37/37 subset ×3 single-threaded, 20/20 tray ×5, host + windows-gnu clippy `-D warnings` clean, fmt clean, zigbuild green, both PEs with correct subsystems, tray FFI proven linked via import table). No new dependencies, no licensing change, deterministic committed tooling with a byte-identical regeneration, and 20 genuinely assertive host-runnable tests. The single P1 is a runtime smoke-test recommendation (message-only window + SetForegroundWindow) that should be resolved on real Windows before the first release — it does not affect the build, CI, or any host-verifiable behavior.",
+-++          "kind": "body"
+-++        }
+-++      ]
+-++    },

+-++          "text": "- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C, adversarial round, stage S3 - **Date:** 2026-11-13, repo HEAD `81c7e72` (S3 landed in `0fb81f0` on base `fe613ab`), branch main, clean tree — no files modified; only this report written. - **Scope:** line-by-line audit of every `unsafe` block in `src/tray.rs` (+ `src/bin/tray.rs`, `assets/icon.ico`, `scripts/make_icon.py`, lib.rs diff) against the special S3 mandate: FFI correctness, memory/pointer safety, wndproc re-entrancy, races, GDI/user-handle leaks, panic paths in message handlers, Supervisor-lifecycle interaction.",
