+++      "passages": [
+++        {
+++          "text": "User report: graphs occasionally out of frame / not loading; exclusions import like v2rayN; better-than-round-robin scheduling; \"Check exit IP\" panics on a non-total comparator.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "1. VENDORED ICED PATCHES over an iced upgrade: iced_graphics and iced_tiny_skia are at their TERMINAL 0.13.0 releases (no 0.13.x patch line exists), and 0.14/1.0 is a breaking migration. The three defects (local-vs-absolute clip space in damage + render mask; INFINITY marker bounds on canvas text → NaN damage; non-total sort comparator) are fixed as minimal vendored patches under vendor/ with [patch.crates-io], inline comments, per-patch READMEs and regression tests inside the vendored crates (`cargo test -p iced_graphics -p iced_tiny_skia`). LESSON: before upgrading iced wholesale, diff the canvas/damage paths — these fixes must be re-based or dropped deliberately when the dependency moves. 2. CANVAS TEXT BOUNDS are now MEASURED (one no-wrap cosmic-text layout per label per frame, ~µs) instead of INFINITY markers. The anchor stays the alignment position and the size is the measured line — both consumers (visible_bounds for damage, draw_cached for rendering) apply the same alignment arithmetic to the same rectangle. A first attempt that reused the frame clip as conservative bounds BROKE the draw anchor (draw_cached re-anchors via `..bounds`), pushing the right-aligned rate label to the window edge — caught by the Xvfb rig and fixed by measuring instead. 3. EXCLUSIONS SEMANTICS: every plain-list entry imports as action `direct`; v2rayN JSON keeps its own outbound tags where they map (direct/freedom, proxy, block/blackhole).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        }

+++      "id": "decision:D23",
+++      "type": "decision",
+++      "title": "D23 — S11: even byte spreading (Balanced) + adapter priority order (Priority), v0.7.0",
+++      "tags": [
+++        "immutable"
+++      ],
+++      "sources": [
+++        {
+++          "file": "harness/memory/DECISIONS.md",
+++          "anchor": "D23"
+++        }
+++      ],
+++      "passages": [
+++        {
+++          "text": "User report: with 3+ bonded adapters, one carries most traffic, the second less, the third rarely any. Root cause: round-robin evens CONNECTION COUNT, not BYTES — a single fat flow dominates its adapter. (D22 was the S10.1 HiDPI fix — recorded in the ledger, no separate section here.)",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "1. BALANCED (new stock default) is load-aware spreading: each new connection goes to the link with the least live pressure (`rate_bps + active_conns × 128 KiB/s`). The per-connection reserve exists specifically so a burst of connections inside one 1 s counter tick spreads instead of stacking on the one link whose byte counters have not ticked yet. Ties rotate via the shared cursor, so an idle table degrades to exactly round-robin. Settings migration v2 moves the stock round-robin to balanced ONCE (D20 precedent: a version<2 file carrying the stock value is indistinguishable from an explicit choice; an explicit re-choice persists). 2. SATURATION IS A PLATEAU, NOT A LEVEL. The learned capacity rises to meet any new rate, so \"rate ≈ capacity\" is true during a ramp too — a naive threshold would mark a link saturated on its first fat flow. Priority therefore requires the capacity to have STOPPED rising (≥2%/tick resets the streak; the rate EWMA damps jitter below that) for 3+ ticks AND rate ≥ 0.85×capacity AND capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s. Consequences: a still-climbing link is never saturated (priority keeps feeding #1 while it ramps); a pinned link saturates within seconds of plateauing; when demand drops below the band the link un-saturates immediately (priority returns traffic to #1 long before the capacity decays). 3. PRIORITY ORDER = the bonded_adapters LIST ORDER (ids persisted in order since S8; links and stream carriers are built in that order, so link index IS priority).",

+++        }

+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | S10 OPENED per user v0.5.1 report: (a) graphs occasionally show up but out of frame; (b) want exclusions import from file (v2rayN-style direct bypass); (c) is there something more efficient than round-robin / can both connections be used simultaneously; (d) \"Check exit IP\" panics with \"user-provided comparison function does not correctly implement a total order\" (smallsort.rs:854). Sandbox had recycled AGAIN (S2-era tree); fresh clone from origin (37d1d99). Toolchain rebuilt: rustup 1.100.0 stable + win-gnu target, zig 0.14.1 (pip wheel reused from tools/pypkgs), cargo-zigbuild 0.24.1; libxkbcommon-x11 + libxcb-xkb extracted from Debian debs into /tmp/xkblibs for the Xvfb GUI rig.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | REPRO RIG BUILT (the decisive tool): scripts/gui_drive.py — one-shot process tree (sandbox kills daemons between tool calls): Xvfb :99 → app under test (LD_LIBRARY_PATH=xkblibs) → scripted XTEST clicks/types (python-xlib; keymap-level SHIFT handling; explicit SetInputFocus because NO WM runs under Xvfb — keyboard focus is never granted otherwise) → ffmpeg x11grab screenshots; analysis via VLM on coordinate-grid crops (VLM coordinates are unreliable — always pixel-cluster verify). REPRODUCED ALL THREE RENDERING BUGS deterministically: (1) connected 12 s → ZERO series pixels anywhere (labels painted, series/grid never did) until a resize round-trip forced a full redraw; (2) the exit-IP click aborted with the user's EXACT panic (smallsort total-order, iced_graphics::damage::group in the stack); (3) with a first-attempt clip fix, the right-aligned rate label rendered at x≈30 (window edge) — the \"out of frame\" shape.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | ROOT CAUSES (all in the terminal iced 0.13 releases — 0.13.0 is the LAST of the 0.13 line for iced_graphics/iced_tiny_skia/iced_winit, no patch release to bump to): (a) iced_tiny_skia Layer::damage intersected ABSOLUTE primitive bounds with the group's UNTRANSFORMED LOCAL clip (a canvas Frame clips to (0,0,w,h)) → every canvas off the window origin produced ZERO damage → series/grid never repainted (text groups are not clip-intersected, which is why labels painted — the tell). Same local/absolute confusion in the render loop's group clip mask (→ masked to the ORIGIN = out-of-frame) and in Cached-geometry damage. (b) Frame::fill_text pushed Text::Cached with (position, INFINITY, INFINITY) marker bounds + INFINITY clip; right-alignment arithmetic (x -= width → -inf) then center() (-inf + inf/2) produced NaN damage rects; damage::group's partial_cmp().unwrap_or(Equal) comparator answered Equal for NaN-vs-anything → driftsort aborted the process (intermittent — sort-pattern dependent, matching \"occasionally\"). Caught in the act with a temporary diagnostic: rects like {x:-inf, w:+inf} and {x:156, y:588, w:NaN, h:NaN}. FIXES (vendored under vendor/ + [patch.crates-io], each with inline comments + regression tests): total_cmp in damage::group; clip mapped through the group transformation in damage (Group + Cached) and in the render mask; fill_text now MEASURES the line (same no-wrap cosmic layout as the glyph-outline branch) and stores honest anchor+size bounds so the damage and draw paths finally agree.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T06:29Z | TWO MORE LATENT BUGS FOUND WHILE WIRING THE IMPORT: (1) the Routing editor was BROKEN against the real backend since v0.5.0 — the GUI's RULE_KINDS were kebab-case (\"domain-suffix\") while real_service's rule_from_view only accepts camelCase (\"domainSuffix\"), so every GUI save errored \"unknown rule kind\" and loaded rules showed blank kind dropdowns (the smoke test missed it: MockService is permissive and never runs rule_from_view). Unified on camelCase. (2) merge_policy_from_str only accepted the UN-hyphenated serde names — the GUI's own \"lowest-latency\" pick fell into the unknown-value fallback and silently behaved as round-robin. Both hyphenated and un-hyphenated forms now parse (regression tests for each).",
+++          "kind": "body"

+++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | S12 OPENED per user report (after v0.6.2): with 3+ bonded adapters \"most traffic goes through one adapter, the second a little less, the third rarely any\" — want (a) more even distribution, (b) a mode where adapters fill in a user-chosen ORDER (first adapter takes traffic until its bandwidth is saturated, then the next), and (c) UI to order adapters first/second/third. Root-cause read: the stock round-robin spreads CONNECTION COUNT evenly, not BYTES — one fat flow (video/download) dominates whichever adapter it landed on, which is exactly the reported shape. Sandbox had recycled again (fresh rootfs, no rustup); toolchain rebuilt per the STATE recipe (rustup 1.100.0 stable + win-gnu target, ziglang 0.14.1 wheel, cargo-zigbuild 0.24.1, python-xlib + xkb debs for the rig).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | IMPLEMENTED (D23) — SCHEDULING: two new MergePolicy variants in mt-net. `Balanced` (new stock default, settings_version 2 migration of the stock round-robin, D20-precedent): pick() ranks candidates by live PRESSURE = rate_bps + active_conns×CONN_RESERVE_BPS (128 KiB/s reserve stops same-second bursts stacking on one link before the 1 s counter ticks); ties rotate via the shared cursor (an idle table behaves exactly like round-robin). `Priority`: walk links in USER ORDER (link order == bonded_adapters order); first candidate NOT saturated wins; all saturated → least RELATIVE load (rate/capacity, unknown capacity = most headroom). Saturation is a PLATEAU, not a level: the capacity estimate rises to meet any new rate, so \"rate ≈ capacity\" is true mid-ramp too — saturation additionally requires the (EWMA-tracked) capacity to have stopped rising for ≥3 ticks (CAPACITY_RISE_RESET 2%/tick; the EWMA damps jitter below that) plus rate ≥ 0.85×capacity with capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s floor (background chatter never saturates). Load plumbing: LinkHealth gained active_conns/rate_bps/capacity_bps/plateau_ticks/saturated; the server's tunnel() bumps a per-link AtomicU64 (send path via establish→link_idx→pumps), establish/close maintain active_conns, and the 1 s tick_loop calls aggregator.tick_loads(dt) (pure update_load per link, unit-tested ramp→plateau→recovery). set_settings now validates the policy name (fail loud) and treats a policy change as dataplane-changing (live reconnect).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | IMPLEMENTED (D23) — STREAM MODE: the mt-bond carrier scheduler (D17 round-robin) is now policy-aware. Carrier gained a queued-bytes AtomicU64 (send_bytes fetch_add; writer_task fetch_sub after the socket write; writer-gone resets to 0 — a respawned carrier starts clean). pick_carrier snapshots live carriers (idx, queued, rtt_ms) into a PURE pick_carrier_index(): Failover=first, RoundRobin=cursor, LowestLatency=best sampled RTT (known beats unknown), Balanced=least queued with rotating ties (a fast NIC drains its queue quicker and naturally takes more frames — capacity-proportional even spreading), Priority=first carrier under PRIORITY_QUEUE_HIGH_WATER (512 KiB ≈ 8 max frames; a healthy carrier hovers near zero, a bottlenecked one grows) else least queued. BondOutbound::with_policy wires the GUI policy through Endpoint::client_with_policy; the daemon side keeps round-robin (priority order is a client concern). connect_flow log line now names the policy; settings.json default + mock default = \"balanced\".",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2026-11-19T13:50Z | IMPLEMENTED (D23) — UI: the Adapters tab is now the priority-ordering surface. Rows render selected-block-first in the SAVED bonded order (pure sort_adapter_rows; unselected rows keep enumeration order below); selected rows carry #1/#2/#3 position chips (primary container) and ↑/↓ buttons (on_press_maybe; disabled at block edges, no-ops for unselected rows); AdapterToggled maintains the block invariant (ticking ON appends at the END = lowest priority; OFF sinks below the block); AdapterMoved swaps with the previous/next SELECTED row; Apply persists the ordered id list (set_bonded_adapters already preserved order); dirty now includes ORDER changes (adapters_dirty compares draft ids vs saved ids restricted to present rows); AdaptersSaved chains load_settings → load_adapters → refresh_status so the sort key is fresh; SettingsLoaded re-sorts only when no draft is in flight. Status-tab adapter rows gained the same #n chips (priority_position_of). +++          "text": "- **What**: MultiTunnel — Rust rewrite of BondTunnel; zero-dependency all-in-one (v2rayN import + net-merge), Material You GUI. Repo: github.com/maniesh-NR/MultiTunnel. - **Data path**: Windows client → local SOCKS/HTTP → ProxyServer → BondOutbound → N carriers (one per bonded NIC, VLESS+REALITY via Xray `sendThrough`, engine self-provisioned D14) → VM Xray (public 8443) → freedom → mt-merge-server (127.0.0.1:7443) → real target. Reverse symmetric. Auth at the Xray edge. - **Two bond modes**: per-connection (default) and stream bonding (D17 framing, needs the VM merge daemon; carriers verified by PING/PONG before schedulable). - **Scheduling (D23, v0.7.0)**: five merge policies in mt-net — round-robin, failover, lowest-latency (EWMA), **balanced** (stock default; pressure = rate_bps + active_conns × 128 KiB/s reserve), **priority** (user order; #1 fills until bandwidth plateaus (ramp detector, ≥3 flat ticks + rate ≥ 0.85 × capacity ≥ 256 KiB/s), then spills). Stream-mode frame scheduler is policy-aware too (least writer backpressure / 512 KiB queue high-water). Adapter priority == saved `bonded_adapters` ORDER; Adapters tab = ordering UI (selected rows first, #n chips, ↑/↓). - **Crates**: mt-net (proxy servers, merge, policy), mt-bond (stream framing, carrier scheduling, daemon), mt-engine (ManagedEngine lifecycle), mt-links (vless:// + subscriptions), mt-platform (Win32 adapter FFI), mt-service (service trait + real_service), mt-m3 + mt-app (Material You GUI, iced). Root crate = CLI binaries (multitunnel, tray, mt-app).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        }
+++      ]
+++    },

+++      "id": "protocol:memory-graph",
+++      "type": "protocol",
+++      "title": "Agentic memory graph + RAG retrieval (S14) — typed nodes/edges store, BM25 + graph expansion, all-agent accessible",
+++      "tags": [
+++        "protocol",
+++        "s14",
+++        "done"
+++      ],
+++      "sources": [
+++        {
+++          "file": "harness/memory/build_graph.py",
+++          "anchor": ""
+++        }
+++      ],
+++      "passages": [
+++        {
+++          "text": "The agentic memory is a typed graph store: harness/memory/store/memory_graph.json (schema v1). Nodes (whitelisted types: project, architecture, playbook, contract, state, decision, ledger, release, commit, task, bug, component, protocol, report, consensus, fact) carry retrieval passages; edges carry typed relations with evidence. Sources: PROJECT_MEMORY.md durable sections, STATE.md, DECISIONS.md, LEDGER.md (grouped per stage tag), agent-reports/, consensus/, git tags + full log, curated/.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "RAG retrieval (BM25 k1=1.5 b=0.75, title boost 1.5, plus graph-neighborhood expansion with 0.5^hop score decay): query from repo root with `python3 query_memory.py \"<topic>\"` (flags: -k N, --expand HOPS, --json, --prompt). --prompt emits a paste-ready context pack with induced subgraph links — the RAG input for any consuming agent (session start, subagent delegation, or future session).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "Agent WRITE path: `python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py --node id=... type=... title=... passage=...` or `--edge src=... dst=... rel=... evidence=...` — appends/updates harness/memory/curated/{nodes,edges}.json (merged last at build, wins on id collision) and rebuilds the store. update_memory.py rebuilds the store on every run. Rebuilds are deterministic (byte-identical while HEAD and sources are unchanged; no wall-clock in the store). Tests: python3 harness/memory/test_graph.py.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        }
+++      ]
+++    },

Durable sections of PROJECT_MEMORY.md are maintained BY HAND; the recent-activity section is maintained BY SCRIPT. +++        {
+++          "text": "- Stage: S2 adversarial review (round 1), Reviewer-B - Repo: /home/z/my-project/MultiTunnel, branch main, HEAD 59d7bba (working tree clean — verified `git status --short` empty, `git rev-parse HEAD` = 59d7bba751e99707bb08bcb32288808a3d4a69be) - Date: 2026-11-13 - Scope reviewed: src/core_proc.rs, src/supervisor.rs, src/sysproxy.rs, src/elevate.rs, src/main.rs, src/bin/tray.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml (+ S1 modules read as context for cross-module issues) - No files modified except this report.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## 1. Verification log (all commands run by me, nothing trusted)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `. tools/env.sh; cargo test` | **52/52 ok, 0 failed, finished 5.64 s** (lib 52; bin/tray/doc-test harnesses 0) | | `cargo test` ×3 more (back-to-back) | 52/52 ×3, no flakes | | `cargo test` under full 2-core CPU load (2 busy-loops) | 52/52 ok, 6.17 s | | `cargo test --lib -- supervisor:: core_proc:: --test-threads=1` ×5 | 13/13 ×5 (~6.2 s each) — the timing-sensitive tests repeated single-threaded | | `touch src/**/*.rs; cargo clippy --all-targets` | clean, no warnings (\"Checking multitunnel v0.1.0 … Finished\") — rebuild forced, not a cached pass | | `cargo fmt --check` | clean (exit 0, no diff) | | `touch src/**/*.rs; cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | green, crate genuinely recompiled for the target (\"Compiling multitunnel v0.1.0\") | | `file /tmp/mt-target/x86_64-pc-windows-gnu/debug/*.exe` | `multitunnel.exe`: **PE32+ executable for MS Windows 6.00 (console), x86-64**; `multitunnel-tray.exe`: **PE32+ … (GUI), x86-64** — both exes link, subsystems correct | | `objdump -p multitunnel.exe` (import table) | imports **ShellExecuteW** (shell32), **InternetSetOptionW** (wininet), **OpenProcessToken / GetTokenInformation** (advapi32), **RegOpenKeyExW / RegQueryValueExW / RegSetValueExW** (advapi32, winreg) → definitive proof the cfg(windows) code in elevate.rs/sysproxy.rs compiled **and linked** for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (not a skipped rebuild) | | Test inventory (`cargo test -- --list`) | config 9, core_proc 5, elevate 3, netmerge 16, supervisor 8, sysproxy 6, xrayconf 5 = **52** |",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## 2. Findings by severity",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P0 — none",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "Cross-build is green and proven (imports above); windows-sys feature list covers every referenced API; no license contamination; both CI workflows are functional.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1 — 3",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P1-1. A `v*` tag releases without any test run.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2-4` triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and PRs — a tag push does **not** trigger ci.yml. `.github/workflows/release.yml:9-14` goes straight to `cargo build --release` with no test/lint step. So the official release artifact can be built from code that never ran the suite (e.g. a tag pushed ahead of a green main commit). Fix: add a `cargo test` step to build-windows (and ideally ubuntu too) in release.yml, or make the release job depend on the ci workflow.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P1-2. `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is referenced by LICENSE and release.yml but does not exist in the tree.** `LICENSE:23-25` states \"Third-party components … (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in releases)\"; `release.yml:21-23` lists it in the copy loop behind a `Test-Path` guard. The file is absent, so the guard silently drops it and every release zip ships without the notices the project's own LICENSE promises (MIT attribution for winreg, serde/regex/windows-sys dual-license choice, MPL-2.0 statement for the non-redistributed Xray-core). Not contamination (see §3.5), but it should be authored before the first `v*` tag.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P1-3. `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized — concurrent call can leave a half-up tunnel with `State::Failed`/`Connected` mismatch (S3 landmine).** `supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect). If `disconnect()` runs while `connect_sequence()` is in flight (state `Connecting`), the loop handle is still `None` (spawn_loop runs at the *end* of connect), so disconnect joins nothing and immediately restores the proxy / stops the core; connect_sequence then continues through steps 4–5 **after** the disconnect: `net-merge on` and `sysproxy::set` re-run, and either the state ends `Connected` with a live loop that undoes the user's disconnect (spawn_loop resets the stop flag at `:386`), or (restartMax=0) `Failed` with net-merge left on and the proxy restored by the campaign but no owner. Also, the loop's `wait_for_port`/`socks_probe` (up to 15 s each) are not stop-flag-aware, so disconnect can block a calling thread ~15 s. Unreachable from the S2 CLI (main.rs: `connect()?` then sleep-forever, single thread), but the module contract (`supervisor.rs:29-31`) explicitly hands the S3 tray an `Arc<Supervisor>` callable \"from menu handlers on any thread\" — a quick connect→disconnect click sequence is exactly that. Fix before S3: one cycle mutex / in-flight guard around connect+disconnect, and make the loop's port-wait/probe stoppable.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 — 7",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-1. Unused windows-sys feature.** `Cargo.toml:27` enables `Win32_System_LibraryLoader`, but no code references `GetModuleHandle`/`LoadLibrary` (grep over src: zero hits). Harmless (declaration-only crate) but it is dead dependency surface — drop it.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-2. CI never enforces the project's own fmt/clippy gates.** `ci.yml` runs only `cargo test` + zigbuild. The harness treats \"clippy clean / fmt clean\" as gate criteria; a regression in either lands silently. Add a lint job (`cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-3. `core_proc.rs` test stub still uses the blocking-accept pattern that caused the supervisor hang.** `core_proc.rs:421-444` (`stub_socks`: blocking `listener.accept().expect(...)`, `:454` join). It is provably unhangable here — the probe always connects before anything can fail (addr comes from the bound listener) and the stub thread ends right after writing its reply, independent of the probe — but supervisor's stub was hardened (nonblocking accept + quit flag, `supervisor.rs:705-754`) precisely because this *class* of bug hung the suite once. Apply the same pattern for defense-in-depth.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-4. Narrow `spawn_loop` race after a give-up.** `supervisor.rs:377-392` vs `:497`. If `connect()` reaches `spawn_loop` in the few-instruction window between the old loop's `break` (GaveUp, `:468`) and `loop_running.store(false)` (`:497`), the `loop_running` guard early-returns and the new cycle gets **no poll loop** (Connected, unsupervised). Practically unreachable (connect_sequence takes ≥ms; the window is instructions), but the guard could join-wait instead of returning.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-5. Tray stub `eprintln!` from a GUI-subsystem process.** `src/bin/tray.rs:5-6`: with `windows_subsystem = \"windows\"` and no console (double-click launch), the stderr handle is invalid and `eprintln!` panics (\"failed printing to stderr\") → exit 101 instead of the intended 2. Stub-only (real tray is S3); trivial to make robust (ignore the write error / drop the line).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-6. Cross-module note for S3: net-merge spawns lack CREATE_NO_WINDOW.** `netmerge.rs:134-138` (`run_full` — used by the supervisor poll loop every 5 s, `supervisor.rs:474`) sets no creation flags, unlike `core_proc.rs:149-154` for xray. Invisible from the S2 console binary (children share its console), but the S3 tray is GUI-subsystem: spawning `net-merge status` every 5 s will flash a console window. Either add the flag in netmerge or have the tray spawn through a helper that does.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-7. Metadata/hygiene nits.** `Cargo.toml` has no `repository` and no `rust-version` (lock is v4 → needs cargo ≥1.78; `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` is a moving target — pinning `rust-version` documents the floor). `release.yml:29-32` could set `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` so a path typo can't silently produce an asset-less release. No CI caching (optional; suite is fast).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## 3. Scrutiny items — detailed results",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 3.1 cfg gating (both host and windows-gnu compile) Audited every `#[cfg(...)]` in src (39 occurrences, grep log in session): - Windows-only API code all behind `#[cfg(windows)]`: `core_proc.rs:149-154` (CREATE_NO_WINDOW via `std::os::windows::process::CommandExt`), `sysproxy.rs:141-221` + `:225-243`/`:253-274` (winreg + WinInet, with `#[cfg(not(windows))]` no-op bodies), `elevate.rs:38-72`/`:79-110` (with non-windows stubs at `:74-77`/`:112-116`), `main.rs:311-319` (UAC relaunch), `netmerge.rs:238-244` (DETACHED_PROCESS tray launch). +++          "text": "**P1-A. Winsock accepted-socket blocking-mode ambiguity in the Windows-CI-exposed test stub (core_proc.rs `stub_socks`).** `stub_socks` now sets the listener nonblocking (my P2-3 fix) and then does `set_read_timeout(5s)` + `read_exact` on the **accepted** socket. On Linux, accept() never propagates O_NONBLOCK (all local runs green). On Windows the tests `socks_probe_success` / `socks_probe_refusal_names_status` (NOT cfg-gated) run on windows-latest in **both** ci.yml and the new release.yml test step. Microsoft's accept() docs say the accepted socket \"has the same properties as socket s, **including the asynchronous events registered with WSAAsyncSelect or WSAEventSelect**\" — event registration is documented as inherited (and those APIs force nonblocking), but the docs are **silent on FIONBIO** (which is what std's set_nonblocking uses); community folklore claims Windows accepted sockets inherit the nonblocking mode, while wine's bug-compatible accept creates a fresh default-(blocking-)state socket and copies nothing. If inheritance is real, the stub's first `read_exact` loses the race with the probe's greeting write → WSAEWOULDBLOCK → stub thread panics → red windows-latest leg (and a release-blocking `cargo test`). Nobody in this project can execute the Windows leg before merge. I could not demonstrate breakage from this sandbox, so this is P1, not P0. **Fix is one line and correct under both semantics**: after accept, `let _ = s.set_nonblocking(false);` (same for the supervisor `spawn_stub` for symmetry, though its tests are unix-gated).",

+++          "text": "# S2 Review — Reviewer-C (Correctness & Security)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "- **Reviewer:** Reviewer-C (adversarial round, stage S2) - **Date:** 2026-11-13 (repo HEAD 59d7bba, branch main, clean tree — reviewed as-is) - **Scope:** `src/core_proc.rs`, `src/supervisor.rs`, `src/sysproxy.rs`, `src/elevate.rs`, `src/main.rs` (incl. embedded `#[cfg(test)]` modules); S1 modules (config/xrayconf/netmerge/error/lib) treated as stable context, cross-module contract violations flagged where seen. - **Lens:** races, deadlocks, panics, error paths, unsafe FFI, process lifecycle, contract conformance.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },

+++          "text": "## Verification log (run myself, trusted nothing)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "| Command | Result | |---|---| | `. tools/env.sh; cargo test` | **52/52 passed, 0 failed, 5.64 s** (run twice, both green) | | `cargo clippy --all-targets` | **clean** — 0 warnings / 0 errors | | `cargo fmt --check` | **clean** (exit 0) | | `cargo zigbuild --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | **success** — `multitunnel.exe` (26.7 MB) + `multitunnel-tray.exe` (4.9 MB), both PE32+ |",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Adversarial demos** (standalone crate in `/tmp/mt-revc-demo` against the repo as a path dependency; the repo itself was not modified — verified `git status` clean after):",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "- `start-hang`: `CoreProc::start()` called while a child is running — **blocked past 2 s** until the child was killed externally; on unblock it returned `Ok(())` and spawned a *second* core generation. The documented `Err(\"core already running\")` never materialized. → finding **P0-1**. - `disc-race`: `disconnect()` issued while a `connect()` sequence was in flight — **returned `Ok` in 44 ms**; the connect then completed and left `state == Connected` with `loop_running() == true`. → finding **P0-2**.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "---",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## P0 — must fix before close",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` hangs (and then double-starts) when a child is already running **`src/core_proc.rs:108-116`** (doc claim at `:104`, module doc `:10-11`)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "`start()` joins the previous waiter thread **before** checking the child slot:",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "The waiter (`waiter_loop`, :333-367) only exits when the child dies, the slot empties, or the stop flag is set. So while a child is live, `join()` blocks **indefinitely**; the `is_some()` error branch is dead code on that path. When the child eventually dies, the join returns, the (now empty) slot passes the check, and `start()` spawns a *new* child and returns `Ok(())` — a silent double-generation restart the caller never asked for. This violates the method's own contract (\"Returns an error if a child is already running\") and is an unbounded block in a public lib API that stage S3 (tray) is specified to call from menu threads.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "Reachability inside the supervisor today is via P0-2's corrupted states (e.g. `State::Failed` with a live core → next `connect()` → `connect_sequence` step 2 → `core.start()` → wedged forever); it is also directly reachable by any external API user. **Fix (trivial):** check `lock(&self.child).is_some()` and return the error *before* joining the leftover waiter (the leftover join is only safe when the previous cycle's child is gone).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P0-2 — `connect()` and `disconnect()` are not serialized as whole operations; disconnect can be silently ineffective **`src/supervisor.rs:238-260` (connect), `:264-341` (connect_sequence), `:396-433` (disconnect)**",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "Only the tiny state-check windows hold `inner`. `connect_sequence` performs seconds of work (config write, core spawn, up-to-15 s port wait, up-to-20 s probe, up-to-15 s bonding wait) holding **no lock and no joinable loop handle** — `spawn_loop` runs only *after* it succeeds. A concurrent `disconnect()` sees `state != Disconnected`, sets the stop flag, joins a **`None`** loop handle (`:402` — the loop doesn't exist yet), restores proxy, stops whatever core exists, sets `Disconnected`, and returns `Ok` — while `connect_sequence` keeps running. Demonstrated (44 ms disconnect during an in-flight probe): final state `Connected`, poll loop alive; with `restart_max > 0` the loop even resurrects the core the disconnect killed, and step 5 sets the **system proxy after the user disconnected**, which in the kill-window black-holes all WinINET traffic through a dead proxy.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "This is exactly the usage the module docs advertise for S3 (\"wrap the `Supervisor` in an `Arc` and call from menu handlers on any thread\", :29-31). It also compounds with P0-1: the interleaving `connect A → disconnect B (completes early) → connect C` can leave `State::Failed`/`Disconnected` with a live core, after which the next `connect()` blocks forever in `start()`'s waiter join. **Fix:** one operation-level `Mutex<()>` (or making the state transition a token) held for the whole of `connect()`/`disconnect()`; all methods are already `&self`, so this is local and cheap.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "---",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## P1 — should fix",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1-1 — `socks_probe` has per-read timeouts but no total deadline **`src/core_proc.rs:259-268, 390-393`**",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "`set_read_timeout(timeout)` bounds each `read_exact`, but a proxy that drips one byte just inside every timeout window keeps each read alive forever — the probe never returns. The contract (\"a probe against a malicious/half-open proxy must never hang\", module doc :14-16) is satisfied per-read, not per-call. Consequences: `connect()` blocks unboundedly at step 3; the poll loop stalls mid-probe (no tick, no stop-flag observation), and since `disconnect()` joins the loop thread, a tray disconnect wedges with it. Practical exposure is low (the probed proxy is our own spawned xray on loopback), hence P1 not P0. **Fix:** compute a call deadline and re-set `read_timeout` to the remaining budget before each read.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1-2 — `elevate::join_args` does not escape quotes / backslash-before-quote (argument injection into the elevated relaunch) **`src/elevate.rs:17-28`** (used at `src/main.rs:314` via `relaunch_elevated`)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "Arguments containing whitespace are wrapped in quotes but embedded `\"` is never escaped. An argument like `a\" --evil` becomes `\"a\" --evil\"`, which `CommandLineToArgvW` parses as **two** arguments (`a`, `--evil\"`) — a single crafted argv entry splits into multiple arguments in the UAC-elevated child. Similarly a path argument ending in `\\` (e.g. `-config C:\\`) corrupts: `\"C:\\\"` parses as `C:\"`. Today's exposure is same-user self-injection (the user launches the CLI), but `main.rs` forwards arbitrary `std::env::args()` verbatim, so any future caller that passes semi-trusted arguments turns this into a real elevation-boundary injection. **Fix:** proper `CommandLineToArgvW`-compatible escaping (`\"` → `\\\"`, doubling trailing backslashes before a closing quote).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1-3 — cross-module: `local.listen` is never validated to be loopback (contract #2) **`src/config.rs:234-263` (validate), `src/xrayconf.rs:20,27` (binds verbatim), `src/supervisor.rs:609-616` (socks_addr/http_addr)**",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "`Config::validate` checks server fields and port collision only. A config with `\"listen\": \"0.0.0.0\"` passes validation, is bound verbatim by **both** xray inbounds — the SOCKS inbound is `\"auth\": \"noauth\"` (`xrayconf.rs:23`) — exposing an unauthenticated SOCKS+HTTP proxy to the LAN, and becomes the WinINET `ProxyServer` value. This directly violates the lib.rs architecture contract #2 (\"the core exposes loopback-only SOCKS/HTTP inbounds\"). Defaults are safe (`127.0.0.1`) and `doctor` only checks parseability (`main.rs:237`), so it is a config-reachable footgun rather than an exploit — but the S2 supervisor is the natural enforcement point (fail `connect_sequence` if `socks_addr`/`http_addr` is not loopback), or add the check to `Config::validate` in a follow-up. Flagged as a cross-module contract violation per stage instructions (config.rs is S1-closed).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "---",
+++          "kind": "body"

+++          "text": "### P0-1 — `CoreProc::start()` waiter-join hang — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/core_proc.rs:105-124`: the child-slot check is now FIRST (`:109-111`) and returns the documented `Err`; the leftover-waiter join (`:115-117`) runs only when the slot is empty; a re-check under the slot lock (`:119-124`) covers the join window. Verified:",

+++          "text": "- **Soundness of the join:** with the slot empty, the old waiter has either exited or will observe `None` within one 50 ms poll (`waiter_loop`, :346-380) — the join is bounded. The re-check under the slot lock closes the TOCTOU between first check and join completion. - **Concurrent `start()`×2:** the slot lock is held across the whole spawn+publish region (`:119-198`), so a loser blocks at its first check and then sees `Some` → Err. No double-spawn. - **The orchestrator's question (child dies between check and join):** if a child is alive at the first check → immediate Err (no join). If the slot is empty, the join cannot wait on a live child — the waiter's exit conditions don't depend on any child. ✓ - Empirical demo + new test `start_while_running_errors_promptly` (`<1 s` bound on an instant Err — µs in practice, huge margin). ✓ - **Residual (new P1-1 below):** a theoretical hang remains for *concurrent external* `start()` calls hitting the ~50 ms window where the old waiter hasn't exited yet and another `start()` publishes a fresh child the old waiter then adopts. +++          "text": "### P0-2 — connect/disconnect not serialized — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/supervisor.rs:178,209,247-248,413-414`: `Shared::op_lock: Mutex<()>` acquired for the **whole body** of `connect()` and `disconnect()`; poison-tolerant `lock()`; guard released by RAII on every path. Verified by demo (above) and by `connect_waits_for_op_lock_of_in_flight_operation` (a blocked connect cannot even set `Connecting`). **Deadlock analysis (the specific question):**",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "- `op_lock` is taken **only** by `connect()`/`disconnect()` (grep: :248, :414 + test) — the poll loop, restart campaign, and all helpers never take it. `disconnect()` joining the loop while holding op_lock therefore cannot deadlock; worst case it waits out one bounded blocking call (see below). - Lock nesting is strictly one-way: op_lock → {inner, loop_thread, core locks}, never the reverse; every inner/loop_thread acquisition is a standalone short statement. No ABBA cycle. - `spawn_loop` (`:391-408`) drops the loop_thread guard **before** joining and re-acquires after — and both `spawn_loop` and `disconnect` (the only slot writers) run under op_lock, so the re-acquire window is race-free. The old `loop_running` early-return (REV-B P2-4) is gone; the join target is provably exited: the only paths leaving a handle in the slot are give-up (loop already returned — `loop_running=false` is its final statement) or a just-exiting give-up thread (ns window). A *live* loop implies state Connecting/Connected, for which `connect()` no-ops before `spawn_loop` — so joining a live loop is unreachable. - Loop-join blocking is bounded: ticks sleep in 100 ms stoppable slices, campaigns re-check the stop flag every iteration, `wait_for_port` ≤ 15 s, `socks_probe` now has a **total** deadline (P1-1 fix), netmerge calls have hard timeouts. So `disconnect()` holds op_lock at most ~15-30 s; a concurrent connect waits, then sees the settled state. Serialization latency, not a hang — and it is exactly what makes the round-1 race impossible.",

+++          "text": "### P1-1 — `socks_probe` total deadline — **FIXED, CONFIRMED** `src/core_proc.rs:271-277, 402-440`. The design is correct this time and the reasoning in the fix note is right: socket timeouts are per-underlying-syscall, so the budget must be re-armed before **every** `read` call, not per logical read. Verified in detail:",

+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "- `refresh_socket_budget` (:404-420): `checked_duration_since` (None → Err) + explicit `is_zero` guard, then sets BOTH read and write timeouts to the remaining budget. No panic; errors are `socks5:`-prefixed. - `socks_read_exact` (:427-…): manual fill loop — re-arms the budget before each `s.read`, `Ok(0)` → clean \"connection closed\" error, io errors (incl. `TimedOut`/`WouldBlock` from the shrunken window) propagate with context, `filled` arithmetic cannot exceed `buf.len()` (read contract), empty buffer → no-op Ok. **No panic surface.** - Every reply phase (greeting, head, ATYP length, drain) passes the same deadline; the CONNECT write is preceded by its own refresh (:304). Total probe time ≤ `timeout` + ε for any drip schedule: each read's timeout is the *remaining* budget, so the deadline is a hard ceiling. - The new test drips 12 valid SOCKS5 reply bytes at 80 ms intervals against a 500 ms budget and asserts Err in **[350, 900) ms**. Timing analysis on a loaded 2-core box: in *every* delivery schedule the probe errors at ~500 ms (a delayed drip merely moves the failing read to the deadline; an on-time drip completes the head at ~480 ms and the drain read then has ~20 ms left), so the window has ≥150 ms lower / ≥400 ms upper margin — the tightest test in the suite but sound; observed stable across my 4 runs. Without the fix the probe returns Ok at ~880 ms and the test fails on `expect_err` — it genuinely pins the bug.",

+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1 1. **`src/core_proc.rs:112-117`** — residual hang in `start()`'s leftover-waiter join under *concurrent external* API use: if two threads call `CoreProc::start()` in the ~50 ms window after a child died but before its waiter exited, thread A can take and join the old waiter while thread B spawns and publishes a **new** child — the old waiter then sees `Some(new child)`, adopts it, and polls as long as it lives, so A's join blocks indefinitely. **Not reachable through `Supervisor`** (op_lock serializes every `core.start()` call site: connect_sequence under op_lock; restart_campaign only runs from a live poll loop, which implies state Connecting/Connected, for which connect() no-ops — I verified there is no state in which both can run), so this is pub-API hardening, not a shipped-path deadlock. Suggested one-liner: only join `is_finished()` handles, else drop (detach) them — the exiting waiter needs no join.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 (new this round) 1. `src/core_proc.rs:283-284, 304-306` — the two `write_all` legs re-arm the budget once per call, so a *theoretical* adversarial partial-write schedule could stretch a write leg past the deadline (multiple full `remaining` windows inside one `write_all`). Physically irrelevant here (3 / ≤262-byte writes, kernel-buffered), but a per-syscall write helper would make the bound airtight like the read side. 2. `src/core_proc.rs:262-266` — `socks_probe` method doc still describes only per-socket timeouts (\"nothing blocks forever\"); the actual guarantee is now the total deadline — one sentence would align doc and mechanism. 3. `src/supervisor.rs:246-256` — `connect()`'s Connecting/Connected no-op check happens *after* acquiring op_lock, so a redundant connect during a long in-flight operation (worst case ~50 s: 15 s port wait + 20 s probe + 15 s bond wait) blocks the caller instead of returning the no-op promptly. Correctness-first tradeoff is fine (and the simplest race-free form), but a fast-path pre-check would spare S3 tray threads the wait.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 (carried from round 1, unaddressed, non-blocking) 4. `core_proc.rs:384-400` — two detached pump threads append to `xray.log` concurrently; `write_all` may split → interleaved partial lines (log-only). 5. `sysproxy.rs:228-233` — registry snapshot reads use `.ok()`: type-mismatched values (REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_BINARY `ProxyServer`) snapshot as absent and restore then deletes them; mid-`set` failure leaves `ProxyEnable=1` half-applied until restore. 6. `supervisor.rs:634-653` / `main.rs:106-123` — `write_private` truncates in place (no temp+rename); crash mid-write leaves a partial `xray-client.json`. 7. `supervisor.rs:613-620` — `parse_probe_target` has no IPv6-literal support (brackets not stripped). 8. `main.rs:168` — `doctor` runs `xray version` with no timeout (hung binary hangs doctor). 9. `core_proc.rs:472-477` / `supervisor.rs:722-725` (test-only) — `free_loopback_port` released-port reuse race. 10. `config.rs:200-202` + `sysproxy.rs:239-241` — an empty `proxyOverride` silently becomes the default (can't be disabled via config); `set()` skips writing it when empty, leaving a previous override in force. 11. `main.rs:23` — `--config=path` equals-form unsupported (space-separated only, usage-documented).",

+++          "text": "### 1. `src/tray.rs` (1353 lines: ~316 pure / ~602 win32 / ~376 tests / stub)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Pure helpers** (`#[cfg(any(windows, test))]`, all host-tested — the sysproxy/elevate pattern):",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "| Helper | Purpose | |---|---| | `state_word` / `state_line` | lifecycle state → menu/tooltip wording | | `links_line` | `Links: N (merging)` / `Links: bonding off` / `Links: unavailable` | | `snippet` | first line of an error, capped, with ellipsis | | `tooltip_text` | state line + error/bond/probe snippets (blank errors skipped) | | `tip_array` | NIF_TIP-safe `[u16;128]`: ≤127 UTF-16 units + NUL, never splits a surrogate pair across units 126/127 | | `ico_entries` / `ico_image_bytes` | ICO directory parse + RT_ICON entry selection (exact → largest-fits → largest overall; empty/out-of-bounds rejected) | | `status_dump` / `status_dump_path` / `write_status_dump` | snapshot pretty-JSON + raw net-merge status → `state_dir/net-merge-status.txt` | | `Cmd` / `MenuEntry` / `menu_plan` / `id_for_cmd` / `cmd_from_id` | full menu as a pure plan; Connect/Disconnect enablement per state |",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Windows implementation** (`mod win`, all FFI through windows-sys 0.61.2, **no new Cargo features** — only the already-enabled Win32_Foundation/Win32_UI_Shell/Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging):",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "- **Window**: `CreateWindowExW` with the predefined `\"STATIC\"` system class, `HWND_MESSAGE` parent, style 0 (message-only, never shown) — no RegisterClass. Subclassed with `SetWindowLongPtrW(GWLP_WNDPROC)`; unhandled messages → `DefWindowProcW` (the STATIC proc only matters during creation, before the subclass is installed). - **Tray icon**: `Shell_NotifyIconW` NIM_ADD with NIF_MESSAGE|NIF_ICON|NIF_TIP; callback = `WM_APP+1`; tooltip refreshed by `SetTimer` 1 s → WM_TIMER → NIM_MODIFY only when the text changed (redundant updates skipped). - **Menu**: rebuilt FRESH from `supervisor.snapshot()` at every open via `CreatePopupMenu`/`AppendMenuW`/`TrackPopupMenuEx(TPM_RIGHTBUTTON | TPM_BOTTOMALIGN)`/`DestroyMenu`; KB Q135788 pattern (SetForegroundWindow before, WM_NULL after) so the menu dismisses when clicking elsewhere. - **Icon embedding**: `include_bytes!(\"../assets/icon.ico\")` → `ico_image_bytes(.., 32)` (RT_ICON payload, NOT the directory) → `CreateIconFromResourceEx(.., 0x00030000, 32, 32, LR_DEFAULTCOLOR)`; fallback `LoadIconW(NULL, IDI_APPLICATION)` (shared, never destroyed — tracked by `icon_owned`). - **Handler state**: `thread_local RefCell<Option<&'static TrayCtx>>` with a `Box::leak`'d context — no GWLP_USERDATA pointer juggling; handlers copy the `&'static` out and drop the borrow guard immediately, so re-entrancy during the `TrackPopupMenuEx` modal loop is safe. - **Threading contract honored**: `connect`/`disconnect` ALWAYS run on `std::thread` workers (they hold the supervisor op_lock, up to ~15 s); nothing blocking ever runs in the window procedure.",

Motif: dark-navy `#0D1B2A` rounded square with two parallel link bars `#4FC3F7` (sky) over `#4ADE80` (emerald) — bonded links, pure geometry, no text/emoji. Entry layout validated byte-by-byte (biSize=40, biWidth=n, biHeight=2n, comp=BI_RGB) and by a Rust unit test.",

+++          "text": "### 3. `src/bin/tray.rs` (108 lines) — real GUI binary",
+++          "kind": "title"

+++        {
+++          "text": "`#![cfg_attr(target_os = \"windows\", windows_subsystem = \"windows\")]` kept. Elevation check first (Windows: `!is_elevated()` → `relaunch_elevated(args)` + exit 0, original args ride along so `--config` survives). Config: explicit `-config/--config` arg → beside the exe → cwd fallback; when nothing exists, template lands beside the exe plus a friendly `config-needed.txt` note (GUI-app equivalent of the console bin's message) and exit 2. Then `Arc<Supervisor>` + `tray::run`. Non-Windows: stub `run` returns Err → stderr line + exit 2, same as the pre-S3 stub.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## Key FFI decisions (for the unsafe reviewer)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "1. **RT_ICON bytes, not the file**: `CreateIconFromResourceEx` requires the image bytes an ICONDIRENTRY points at; passing the whole ICO file is the classic mistake. `ico_image_bytes` extracts+bounds-checks the slice; a unit test pins the 32×32 entry's header (biSize=40/biWidth=32/biHeight=64). 2. **STATIC + GWLP_WNDPROC subclass** instead of RegisterClass (fewer moving parts, per the stage spec). The previous proc pointer is checked non-null; we intentionally call `DefWindowProcW` (not `CallWindowProcW` on the saved STATIC proc) for unhandled messages — a message-only window never uses static-control behavior after creation. 3. **No GWLP_USERDATA**: state flows through a thread-local `&'static` (single window, single message thread). Eliminates the classic create-then-SetWindowLongPtrW race and null-deref windows entirely. 4. **Re-entrancy**: `TrackPopupMenuEx` runs a modal loop that re-enters the window procedure (WM_TIMER during the menu, etc.) — no `RefCell` borrow guard is ever held across it (guards close inside `ctx()`/small blocks). 5. **Icon ownership**: `CreateIconFromResourceEx` HICON is destroyed in teardown; `LoadIconW` fallback is shared and never destroyed (`icon_owned` flag). 6. **`NOTIFYICONDATAW` init**: struct literal with `..Default::default()` (all-zero is the valid Win32 \"unused\" state); `cbSize` set from `size_of`. 7. Every one of the 32 `unsafe` blocks carries a `SAFETY:` comment; error paths use `std::io::Error::last_os_error()` (thread-safe errno) rather than raw `GetLastError`.",

+++          "text": "- `src/supervisor.rs`: additive `pub fn emergency_stop(&self)` (module-doc contract line added; full semantics in the method docs). +++          "text": "### P1 — 1",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P1-1. Menu-dismiss pattern on a message-only window is runtime-unverifiable from this sandbox (tray.rs `show_menu`, :839-886).** The KB Q135788 fix calls `SetForegroundWindow(hwnd)` before `TrackPopupMenuEx` (return value discarded) so the menu dismisses when the user clicks elsewhere. `hwnd` is a **message-only** window (child of `HWND_MESSAGE`, style 0, never shown). Activation is a top-level-window concept; if `SetForegroundWindow` is a no-op for a message-only child (plausible per its docs — the call activates the window and brings its thread to the foreground), the classic stuck-menu bug returns despite the pattern being present. Nobody has run this tray on real Windows yet, and it cannot be exercised from Linux. Not build/CI-breaking and not UB — but it should be smoke-tested on real Windows before the first release, or the window created as a **hidden top-level** window (no `HWND_MESSAGE` parent, never shown — the pattern .NET NotifyIcon and the tray-icon crate use), which also keeps `Shell_NotifyIconW` callbacks working. Cross-lens flag for the unsafe reviewer to confirm.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 — 4",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-1. Temp-dir leak in one new test.** `write_status_dump_creates_dirs_and_overwrites` (tray.rs:1249-1263) never `remove_dir_all`s its unique dir — the only test in the crate that doesn't clean up after itself (the S1/S2 review criterion). One line fixes it.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-2. Exit's 2 s disconnect bound gives up on a legitimate ~15 s teardown.** `exit_app` (EXIT_WAIT=2 s) races the supervisor op_lock/poll-loop join that can legally take up to ~15 s; on timeout the process exits mid-disconnect, potentially leaving the system proxy set and net-merge on until the next launch (step-0 self-heal covers it, and the bound is a deliberate anti-hang). Documented trade-off — consider a brief \"shutting down…\" tooltip update or a slightly larger bound; behavior is safe, just occasionally untidy.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-3. Embedded-asset test under-pins the icon.** `ico_embedded_asset_parses_with_32_entry` asserts the 32×32 DIB header only; a drifted or hand-edited icon.ico would still pass. Cheap hardening: also assert the 16×16 DIB header and the total file length (5430) so any divergence from make_icon.py's deterministic output is caught (a full byte-compare needs python and can't live in cargo test).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-4. `spawn_detached` silently drops spawn failures** (`let _ = Command::…spawn()`) for notepad/explorer — both are inbox Windows components, so this is a nit; a `log_err` on failure would make a missing-shell case diagnosable.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## 4. Verdict",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },

+++          "text": "**APPROVE** — 0 P0. No new dependencies, no licensing change, deterministic committed tooling with a byte-identical regeneration, and 20 genuinely assertive host-runnable tests. The single P1 is a runtime smoke-test recommendation (message-only window + SetForegroundWindow) that should be resolved on real Windows before the first release — it does not affect the build, CI, or any host-verifiable behavior.",

+++          "text": "| # | Line | API | Verdict & reasoning | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | :482 | `DestroyIcon` | OK — only when `icon_owned` (from `CreateIconFromResourceEx`) and non-null; nothing references it (no tray icon was added on this failure path) | | 2 | :493 | `DestroyWindow` | OK — window created by this thread on this path; no icon registered | | 3 | :496 | `DestroyIcon` | OK — same guard as #1 on the NIM_ADD-failure path | | 4 | :508 | `SetTimer` | OK — valid hwnd, fresh id 1, `None` TIMERPROC ⇒ WM_TIMER to the subclassed proc; failure (returns 0) is non-fatal and logged | | 5 | :523 | `GetMessageW` | OK — `&mut msg` is a valid aligned `MSG` out-slot; NULL hwnd filter; both i32 outcomes (0 = WM_QUIT, −1 = error → teardown + Err) handled | | 6 | :535 | `TranslateMessage` | OK — `msg` holds a message returned by #5 | | 7 | :537 | `DispatchMessageW` | OK — same; routes to our subclass; wndproc is panic-free (see below) | | 8 | :559 | `Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_DELETE)` (teardown) | OK — identity fields (cbSize/hWnd/uID) set via `nid_base`; guarded by `icon_added` (swap ⇒ idempotent with exit_app's delete); FALSE (already gone) ignored | | 9 | :564 | `KillTimer` | OK — our timer/hwnd; idempotent; ordered before DestroyWindow | | 10 | :566 | `DestroyWindow` (teardown) | OK — our message-only window; the defensive WM_DESTROY handler posts one extra (harmless, never-consumed) WM_QUIT | | 11 | :571 | `DestroyIcon` (teardown) | OK — only when owned; the `LoadIconW` fallback is a SHARED icon and is correctly never destroyed (`icon_owned=false`) — no GDI leak, no shared-icon UAF | | 12 | :587 | ",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Wndproc panic-freedom (panic across `extern \"system\"` = abort/UB):** `tray_wndproc` and everything it calls were walked exhaustively: no indexing, slicing, `unwrap`, `expect`, or arithmetic that hostile data can reach (grep-confirmed zero in `mod win`). The two remaining panic-capable constructs are both proven unreachable: (a) `ctx()`'s `RefCell::borrow` — the CTX cell is mutably borrowed exactly once, before the window exists and before any message dispatch, on the same thread; (b) `ui.borrow_mut()` in `on_timer`/`exit_app`/`teardown` — never held across any message-pumping call (`show_menu` never touches `ui`; the exit wait blocks rather than pumps). Supervisor `snapshot()`/locks use the poison-tolerant `lock()` and are contention-brief (workers hold `inner` only momentarily). Interior NULs in net-merge-sourced tooltip text merely truncate display (fixed-size NUL-terminated buffer), no memory-safety impact.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Threading / op_lock interaction (mandate item 2):** verified — `connect`/`disconnect` run ONLY via `spawn_supervisor_op` workers; nothing in the wndproc or `show_menu` ever calls a supervisor op synchronously. `exit_app`: NIM_DELETE → worker `disconnect()` → `recv_timeout(2 s)` → PostQuitMessage. No deadlock is possible: the message thread holds no lock the worker needs; op_lock holders never wait on the message thread (verified all op paths: spawn_loop/net-merge/registry/core — none send messages to the window). The orphaned-worker-at-exit scenario is bounded and implicitly documented — but its teardown-completion gap is P1-1 below.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**ICO byte-level bounds (mandate item 1):** `ico_entries`/`ico_image_bytes` re-audited line-by-line: `len < 6` reject, reserved/type magic check, per-entry `checked_add(16)` + `end > len` reject, `dim` from directory byte (0 ⇒ 256), `len == 0` reject, `offset.checked_add(len)` then `slice::get` (no panic on any malformed input; no unwrap). The committed asset itself parses byte-perfect (my independent Python walk). `include_bytes!` is a compile-time embed — no runtime path dependency, stable in release builds.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Supervisor integration (mandate item 5):** menu enablement matches the state machine exactly (Connect: Disconnected/Failed; Disconnect: Connecting/Connected — cancelling an in-flight connect via op_lock, per the S2 contract; snapshot-staleness between menu open and click is harmless because the supervisor state gate arbitrates). Tooltip surfacing `snapshot.error` (implementer's documented deviation) is correct and I endorse it — without it a Failed state would show no reason. The status dump contains no secrets (snapshot fields + net-merge text; no credentials in any supervisor error string — verified in S2). 1 s timer → `NIM_MODIFY` only on text change — no shell churn.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Bin cross-check (mandate item 6):** elevation flow forwards original args (`-config` survives; quoting hardened in S2); GUI-subsystem stderr writes are all best-effort `writeln!` with ignored errors — **no `eprintln!` panic-on-invalid-handle anywhere**; the missing-config path is file-based (template + `config-needed.txt` beside the exe — visible without a console); config search order (explicit → beside exe → cwd) and template placement logic verified correct.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "---",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## Findings",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P0 — none I could not construct any UB, handle leak, deadlock, or reachable panic in the shipped paths. The three highest-risk patterns (wndproc + RefCell + panic-across-FFI; SetWindowLongPtrW subclass; NOTIFYICONDATAW ABI) are all sound by construction and verified against the actual windows-sys 0.61.2 definitions.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1 — 2 1. **`src/tray.rs:807-832` (`exit_app`)** — the 2 s exit budget can be exceeded by a *healthy* disconnect: `disconnect()` joins the poll loop, which may legitimately sit inside `socks_probe` (15 s total budget), a restart campaign's `wait_for_port` (15 s), or `netmerge::off`'s CLI timeout (10 s) — or an in-flight `connect` worker may still hold the op_lock (up to ~50 s). When the 2 s expires, the process exits with teardown incomplete: the xray core is **orphaned** (Windows does not kill children on parent exit) and the system proxy stays set — the user believes the app (and tunnel) exited, while traffic keeps flowing through the VM, or browsing is silently routed through a half-dead proxy. Fix suggestion: on timeout, perform an op_lock-free emergency stop — `CoreProc::stop` (own mutexes, no op_lock) plus `sysproxy::restore(state_dir)` — both safe to call from the message thread; or escalate the wait with a visible \"disconnecting…\" state. At minimum the incomplete-teardown possibility must be documented as more than \"best-effort\". 2. **`src/tray.rs` (whole module — no `TaskbarCreated` handling)** — if explorer.exe restarts (shell crash, user-initiated restart — not rare), the tray icon is silently lost and never re-added: the process becomes an elevated, unreachable zombie holding the tunnel with no UI and no window (message-only ⇒ not findable); the only exit is Task Manager. Standard fix: `RegisterWindowMessageW(\"TaskbarCreated\")` handled in the wndproc → re-`NIM_ADD` (icon handle and window survive explorer restarts).",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 — 7 1. `src/bin/tray.rs:28,41` + `src/tray.rs:491` — GUI-subsystem errors are invisible: a declined UAC prompt, `NIM_ADD` failure, or any `tray::run` error goes to a best-effort stderr that usually doesn't exist — the user sees nothing happen. Safe (no panic) but a `MessageBoxW` (or writing an error file like the config-note pattern) would make failures diagnosable. 2. `src/tray.rs:797-799` — \"Edit config\"/\"Show raw status\" spawn **notepad running elevated**; an elevated editor is the classic admin-shell footgun (its file dialogs can launch arbitrary executables with admin rights). User-initiated and the whole app is elevated by requirement, but worth documenting or delegating to an unelevated broker in a future stage. 3. `src/tray.rs:776-794` — `show_raw_status`/`open_log_folder` do synchronous file writes + `create_dir_all` inside the wndproc (small, but a state dir on slow/network storage would stall the pump); the connect/disconnect worker pattern is the right home for these too. 4. `src/tray.rs:79-87` — `snippet(s, cap)` underflows (`cap - 1`) if ever called with `cap == 0`; unreachable today (sole call site uses 48) but it is a latent panic-in-wndproc if reused — guard or `debug_assert!(cap > 0)`. 5. `src/tray.rs:456` — the \"call exactly once\" contract for `run` is unenforced; a second call would leak another ctx and create a second window. A cheap `debug_assert`/atomic once-flag would pin the invariant. 6.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### Positive notes - The RT_ICON-not-the-file insight (#12), the surrogate-pair-safe `tip_array`, the no-GWLP_USERDATA thread-local design, the Q135788 dance, the `icon_owned` shared-vs-owned distinction, and the idempotent teardown with swap-guarded `icon_added` are all exactly right — this is a carefully done raw-FFI tray. - The pure-helper/test split (316 pure lines host-tested) is the same pattern that made S1/S2 reviewable, and the 20 new tests genuinely pin the helpers (tip boundary at unit 126, ICO preference order and rejections, menu enablement per state, id round-trip, dump overwrite). - The icon asset is byte-perfect and exactly the size the format dictates (5430 B); `make_icon.py` is deterministic and dev-only (not shipped).",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## Verdict",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**APPROVE.** No P0: all 32 unsafe blocks are correct with accurate SAFETY comments (signatures and struct layouts verified against the vendored windows-sys 0.61.2 source, not assumed); the wndproc is provably panic-free; no GDI/user-handle leaks on any path; no deadlock in the op_lock interaction; all four mandatory gates green. The two P1s (exit-teardown completeness, TaskbarCreated re-add) are production-readiness items that should be fixed before the S4 release but do not introduce UB, leaks, deadlocks, or reachable panics; P2-7 needs one on-hardware check during S4 smoke testing.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },

+++          "text": "## 2. Release-readiness audit",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 2.1 release.yml trace — tag `v0.1.0` pushed hypothetically NOW windows-latest → checkout (Cargo.lock committed → reproducible deps) → stable toolchain → **`cargo test`** (65 tests on MSVC, see 2.7) → `cargo build --release` (both bins at `target/release/`, default target dir on the runner — paths in the Copy-Item match) → package: unconditional copy of `multitunnel.exe`, `multitunnel-tray.exe`, `config.example.json`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (all exist — a missing one would fail the step loudly, which is the desired behavior), guarded copy of `README.md` + `QUICKSTART.md` (both exist → included) → `Compress-Archive` → `dist/multitunnel-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` → upload-artifact → softprops release attach with `fail_on_unmatched_files: true` (the glob will match). **No missing path, no silent-degradation path: the release would build, test, package and attach successfully.** One content gap → P1-3 (server script not in the zip).",

+++          "text": "### 2.2 ci.yml on the tag push — is release-only testing enough? ci.yml does not run on tags (`branches: [main]`); release.yml carries `cargo test`. fmt/clippy are NOT run on the tag. Judgment: **acceptable** — in this project's flow every main push is CI-green (test on both OSes + lint + cross-check incl. windows-target clippy), and tags are cut from main HEAD; the release job re-runs the full suite on the exact tag commit, so the artifact is always *tested*. The residual (a tag of a never-pushed commit ships unlinted code) is a lint-regression risk, not a functional one → P2-1 optional belt-and-braces.",

+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 2.3 The zip a Windows user downloads Contents: `multitunnel.exe`, `multitunnel-tray.exe`, `config.example.json`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `README.md`, `QUICKSTART.md`. +++          "text": "### 2.4 MSVC-vs-gnu parity (shipped = MSVC, local proof = gnu) Risk judged **low**: windows-sys 0.61.2 and winreg are the same crate versions with identical FFI declarations for both ABIs (win32 is a stable C ABI; windows-link import shims are toolchain-agnostic); the gnu side is proven by zigbuild (debug + release) + clippy `-D warnings` + PE import inspection; the MSVC side compiles and runs 65 tests in CI. Rust MSVC release binaries carry the CRT statically (no vcruntime DLL prerequisite). No printf/CRT-dependent behavior exists in the code paths. The genuinely untested-until-now part — the tray UI at runtime — is exactly what QUICKSTART step 6 turns into the documented first-run smoke test (with 7 checkpoints and a \"report it\" escape hatch). Acceptable for v0.1.0 with that backstop.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 2.5 Licensing chain for the release artifact - Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock byte-identical since S2-close → the S2-round-2-verified THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (all 19 dep crates, permissive MIT / MIT-OR-Apache-2.0 / MIT-OR-Unlicense; full MIT text) is still current. **Zero new dependencies in S3/S4.** - The zip redistributes only project code (MIT) + statically-linked permissive crates + docs. Xray-core (MPL-2.0) and net-merge (MIT) are downloaded by the user from their own upstreams (QUICKSTART links; server script downloads from XTLS releases) — never bundled → **no copyleft contamination**. The setup script similarly downloads rather than embeds. - The tray icon is original generated artwork (project's own committed script) → project MIT. No third-party assets. - SmartScreen/unsigned-binary warning: covered in README (Security notes) and QUICKSTART step 6.1. UAC/admin expectations documented in both.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 2.6 Docs build claims `cargo build --release` produces both binaries (proven locally in the release profile via zigbuild); the zigbuild cross instructions match the exact commands this harness runs; MSRV 1.78 matches Cargo.toml (verified exact in S2 r2: code max 1.70, deps ≤1.71, lockfile v4 ⇒ 1.78); \"Linux build compiles stubs\" is true; CI description matches the actual workflows (test matrix, lint, cross-check incl. windows-target clippy); harness pointer present. Version: Cargo.toml `0.1.0` ↔ planned tag `v0.1.0` ↔ zip name `multitunnel-v0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` — consistent. **Two doc-accuracy defects → P1-1 (restartMax semantics), P1-2 (stale S3 string vs README description).**",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 2.7 Windows-leg test count and safety Host runs 78. `#[cfg(unix)]`-gated tests (exhaustively enumerated by multiline grep): supervisor 6 (op-lock wait, emergency stop, 4 rig tests), core_proc 2 (start-twice, drip deadline), netmerge 7 (process tests) = **15 excluded**; `#[cfg(windows)]`-only sysproxy tests: 2 (mapping helpers). **Windows leg = 78 − 15 + 2 = 65.** Safety: all 65 are pure / temp-dir file IO / loopback binds; the two loopback-binding core_proc stub tests carry the S2-round-2 `set_nonblocking(false)` hardening; every timing-sensitive test (drip 350–900 ms window, op-lock 300 ms, start-twice <1 s, emergency-stop <2 s, core-death 15 s deadline, 20 s recv bounds) is unix-gated, so the Windows leg carries no timing risk. Windows runners handle temp dirs, loopback binds, and the file-IO dump tests without issue (same tests have been green on the windows-latest CI leg since S2). **Low risk of a Windows-leg failure at tag time.**",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### 2.8 Server script (portability/lens notes; deep security is REV-C's) `set -euo pipefail`; validation-before-root; no curl|bash (download → `unzip -t` → extract → smoke test → `install -D`); mktemp 0700 with EXIT trap; ETXTBSY handled (stop service before replacing binary); `xray run -test` gate on the generated config; both `xray x25519` output generations parsed; JSON built from charset-validated variables (no injection through DOMAIN/DEST/keys); GitHub-API rate-limit fallback to the `releases/latest` redirect (verified live: this sandbox's IP is currently rate-limited on api.github.com — the fallback path is real-world exercised); pipefail/SIGPIPE analyzed for every `sed | head` pipeline (each sed emits at most one line → no SIGPIPE-141 under `set -e`). GNU-isms (`sed s///I`, `install -D`) are unreachable on non-systemd hosts (earlier clean die \"targets Ubuntu/Debian\"). Config written 0644 root:root because `User=nobody` must read it → P2-2 (0640 root:nogroup would be tighter). systemd unit hardening (NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp) as documented in README.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## 3. Findings by severity",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },

+++          "text": "### P0 — none The tagged release would not fail: every workflow path exists, both exes build and test green on the exact commands CI uses (host + windows-gnu + release profile), licensing is clean, the zip is complete for the client side, and the Windows CI leg carries no identified failure risk.",

+++          "text": "### P1 — 3",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },

+++          "text": "**P1-1. README config table inverts `restartMax` semantics — ships in the zip.** README.md:153 — \"`behavior.restartMax` | 5 | core restart budget after failures **(0 = unlimited)**\". Actual behavior: `restart_campaign` (supervisor.rs) treats `max == 0` as *give up immediately — never restart* (the S2 contract: \"restart_max (0 = never)\"), and `apply_fallback_defaults` (config.rs:174-212) deliberately does NOT 0-fallback `restartMax`, so a JSON `0` reaches the supervisor as \"never\". Also the blanket claim at README.md:155-156 (\"numbers set to `0` fall back to these defaults on load\") is false for this one field. A user setting `restartMax: 0` expecting unlimited retries gets a fail-fast tunnel that disables the system proxy on the first core death. Fix the table line to \"0 = never restart (fail immediately)\" and scope the 0-fallback sentence.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P1-2. Stale stage-3 string in the shipped console binary contradicts the README.** `multitunnel` with no args prints `error: tray lands in stage S3 — build multitunnel-tray` and exits 1 (verified against the built binary). README.md:170 documents \"(none) print a pointer to multitunnel-tray (the tray app is the GUI binary)\". In v0.1.0, \"stage S3\" is meaningless jargon for an end user and the wording/behavior doesn't match the docs that ship next to it. One-string fix in `src/main.rs:49-51` (frozen file — the implementer flagged it for orchestrator arbitration; as release reviewer I escalate: fix before tagging).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P1-3. The release zip lacks `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` — QUICKSTART step 1's prerequisite.** release.yml:23 copies exes + config.example.json + LICENSE + notices (+ guarded README/QUICKSTART). QUICKSTART step 1 tells the user to \"copy `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` there (or fetch the repo)\" — a zip-only user has no script and no direct URL. One line (`Copy-Item server/setup-xray-reality.sh` after creating the dir, or adding `server/setup-xray-reality.sh` to the unconditional list) makes the zip self-sufficient for the whole 10-minute path; alternatively add the raw-GitHub URL to QUICKSTART step 1. Fix before tagging (re-tagging after the fact is worse than one more line now).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 — 3",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**P2-1. release.yml runs `cargo test` but no fmt/clippy on the tag.** Acceptable today (tags cut from CI-green main; the artifact is fully tested), but adding the two lint steps to the release job (~4 lines) closes the \"tag of an untested commit ships unlinted\" residual permanently.",

Note: `nobody`'s group is `nogroup` on Debian/Ubuntu — worth a quick verification on the target VM before switching.",
