+++          "text": "## Script audit (root-running software standard)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**`set -euo pipefail` discipline — holds.** Every expansion is double-quoted; all interpolations into heredocs are charset-validated before use (DOMAIN `[A-Za-z0-9.-]` with edge rules, PORT all-digits + range, DEST regex `host:port`/`[v6]:port` + port range, INSTALL_ROOT absolute + whitespace-free, keys `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`, shortId/uuid generator-produced) → **no JSON or ExecStart injection is possible** (re-proven with a `a\".evil` DOMAIN attempt). The three `cmd | head -n 1` pipelines either output ≤1 line (no SIGPIPE possible under pipefail) or are `|| true`-guarded (`xray version | head`); command-substitution failures land in `TAG`-empty → guarded die. `WORKDIR=\"$(mktemp -d)\"` + `chmod 0700` + `trap cleanup EXIT` → temp dir always removed.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**No curl|sh; download failure handled.** Zip → temp file → `-s` empty check → `unzip -t` integrity → extract exactly `xray geoip.dat geosite.dat` → per-file existence checks → `chmod 0755` → `xray version` smoke test (catches wrong architecture loudly) → `install -D` into `$INSTALL_ROOT`. `curl -fSL --retry 3 … || die` on the download. The GitHub-API rate-limit case degrades to the `releases/latest` redirect, and both paths terminate in the `^v[0-9]…` tag guard — re-proven above.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Credentials.** `xray uuid`; `xray x25519` parsed for BOTH output generations (re-proven above); `openssl rand -hex 8` shortId (64 bits — adequate for REALITY's anti-probe salt). The private key is never printed (client block carries `publicKey` only; the `log` line prints uuid/shortId which are client-side values anyway) and never leaves the VM.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**REALITY config validity.** Field set (`show:false, dest, xver:0, serverNames, privateKey, shortIds`) is the current documented shape; `dest` (not the legacy `target` spelling) is what current Xray accepts; VLESS `decryption:\"none\"` + client `flow:\"xtls-rprx-vision\"` correct; and the script hard-fails via `xray run -test` **before** touching the service if anything is wrong. Existing config + no FORCE → refusal with regeneration warning (no silent credential rotation). (Implementer's real-binary `-test` pass is credible; tooling no longer present here — noted, not re-run.)",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**systemd unit.** Sound for Ubuntu 22.04+: `User=nobody` + `Environment=XRAY_LOCATION_ASSET=$ASSET_DIR` (assets 0644 in 0755 dirs — readable), `ExecStart` path from whitespace-validated INSTALL_ROOT (systemd takes it verbatim — no shell, so no metachar risk), `Restart=always`+`RestartSec=3`, `NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp` (xray needs no writes outside stdout → journald). `daemon-reload` → `enable` (guarded) → `restart` → `sleep 2` → `is-active --quiet`; on failure dumps 30 journal lines and dies naming the state — a crash-looping service reads as not-active, so the check cannot pass a broken endpoint. A bind failure (e.g. port taken) exits xray → crash-loop → caught. Good.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Firewall guidance.** Non-destructive: `iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport $PORT -j ACCEPT` (insert, **no `-F` anywhere in the repo**) + `netfilter-persistent save`; explicit \"check existing rules first\" steps; the gcloud command is syntactically correct with a narrower-source-ranges suggestion. Print-only (script never touches the firewall itself) — correct choice.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Public IP.** GCP metadata (correct endpoint + `Metadata-Flavor` header, IPv4-validated) preferred over ipify with an explicit VPN-egress warning on the ipify path; placeholder + guidance when neither works. Sound; the metadata preference is the right call for a VM whose egress may be VPN-routed.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**Gaps found** → findings P1-1/P2-1/2/3 below (teardown-on-failure story, config mode, privileged-port validation).",

+++          "text": "## Docs cross-check (README/QUICKSTART vs code)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "Verified accurate: architecture diagram & design contracts (mux off, loopback-only, geoip:private direct, fail-open, op_lock + emergency_stop, stale-proxy self-heal, connect order, backoff 1→30 s) — all match lib.rs/supervisor.rs/xrayconf.rs; doctor check list & order (QUICKSTART step 5 = main.rs exactly, incl. \"all checks passed\"); `generate` 0600; `connect` UAC/elevation/summary/Ctrl+C semantics; tray menu items, `State:` wording, Links line variants, `state\\net-merge-status.txt` dump path, 1 s tooltip, TaskbarCreated re-registration and the emergency-teardown Exit — **both S3 P1 features exist in code** (`RegisterWindowMessageW` re-add, `Supervisor::emergency_stop` after the 2 s exit bound) so the QUICKSTART smoke-test checkpoints are truthful; release.yml description (test-first, zip contents, `fail_on_unmatched_files`); .gitignore really contains `config.json` (+ `xray-client.json`, `*.exe`, logs/state/bin); MSRV 1.78; **smoke-test warning present and prominent**; **no emoji** (programmatic scan); all 23 config-table defaults match `config.rs` **except the restartMax semantics and server.address fallback noted below**; geoip.dat/geosite.dat instruction in QUICKSTART step 3 is **genuinely required** (the generated client config's `geoip:private` routing rule fails xray startup without geoip.dat; xray finds assets next to its exe; the server script mirrors the same convention).",

+++          "text": "## Findings",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P0 — 0 The script is careful root-running software: injection-proof, download-verified, loudly-failing, secret-preserving; nothing that breaks a VM, installs a broken endpoint, or opens a security hole. (The `-test`-before-restart gate in particular means a bad generated config can never take the endpoint down.)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P1 — 4 1. **`README.md:153`** — \"`behavior.restartMax` … (0 = unlimited)\" is **factually wrong**: per the supervisor contract and `restart_campaign` (`if max == 0 || attempt > max` → give up), **0 = never restart** (immediate give-up, proxy restored, `Failed`). A user following the README to get \"unlimited\" resilience gets zero. One-word doc fix. 2. **`QUICKSTART.md:47`** — \"Make sure `net-merge` is on your PATH **or** sits next to `multitunnel.exe`\": with the default config (`\"netMerge\": \"net-merge\"`), `config.rs::resolve` joins the relative name onto the **executable's directory**, and a directory-qualified program is not PATH-searched — so a PATH-only install fails `doctor`/bonding (empirically re-proven: relative paths resolve against the exe dir in my doctor run). Only \"next to the exe\" (or an absolute `paths.netMerge`) works; the sentence's first disjunct misleads users into a broken step 2. 3. **`README.md:134` + `:155`** — the config table lists `server.address` with default `35.208.99.240`, and the conventions paragraph claims \"strings left empty … fall back to these defaults on load\". **False for `server.address`**: it has no load-time fallback (only `server.port` and the local/paths/behavior fields do); an empty address is rejected by `validate()` (empirically re-proven: `doctor -config` → \"incomplete config — missing: server.address\"). The 35.208.99.240 value is a template/example prefill; the table should mark address required like uuid/sni/publicKey, and the convention sentence should be scoped. 4.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 — 6 1. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh:214-337` — no failure-rollback: after `systemctl stop xray` (upgrade path), any failure before `systemctl restart` (install/credential/validation/unit error) leaves the old endpoint STOPPED with no restart attempt and only a raw `set -e` exit (`install`/`chmod`/`chown`/`systemctl restart` have no `|| die` diagnostics); the subsequent re-run then demands `FORCE=1`, which regenerates all credentials (killing the old client block) even though the old config is still valid. Suggest a failure trap that best-effort `systemctl start xray`, plus a \"config unchanged — `systemctl start xray` recovers\" hint. 2. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh:297` — config written `0644 root:root`; `chown root:nogroup` + `chmod 0640` would keep it readable by `User=nobody` (nobody's group is nogroup on Debian/Ubuntu) while hiding the REALITY private key from other local users; also create under `umask 077` to close the pre-chmod window. The implementer's \"local read = already on the box\" argument is acceptable for a dedicated VM — noted as defense-in-depth, not a blocker. 3. `server/setup-xray-reality.sh:95-100` — PORT < 1024 (e.g. `PORT=443`, or `PORT=08` → 8) passes validation but `User=nobody` cannot bind privileged ports → the service fails at start (caught loudly by is-active, but with a cryptic journal). Pre-validate `PORT ≥ 1024` or warn. 4. `README.md:170` — \"(none) print a pointer to multitunnel-tray\" describes intent; the actual no-arg behavior prints the stale S3-era string \"tray lands in stage S3 — build multitunnel-tray\" and exits FAILURE.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### Deviation judgments requested - **geoip/geosite in QUICKSTART**: justified — the generated client config's `geoip:private` routing rule hard-requires geoip.dat at xray startup; geosite.dat is not strictly needed (no geosite rules) but ships in the same zip and costs nothing to copy. The \"next to the executable\" location is where xray looks absent `XRAY_LOCATION_ASSET` (the supervisor sets none). - **Config 0644 root-owned**: acceptable for a single-user VM per the implementer's argument, with the 0640 root:nogroup improvement noted as P2-2. - **GCP-metadata-over-ipify**: correct deviation — on a VPN-egress VM, ipify reports the VPN exit IP and the client block would be wrong; metadata reports the true external IP; ipify remains the fallback with a warning. - **`xray run -test` verification**: not re-runnable here (tooling cleaned from /tmp); the script's built-in gate order (test config → die before touching the service) plus the implementer's real-binary validation record give adequate confidence.",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## Verdict",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "**APPROVE.** No P0: the installer is injection-proof, verifies everything it downloads and generates, fails loudly rather than half-working, never prints the private key, and cannot replace a working endpoint with a broken config (the `-test` gate). The four P1s are documentation/CI accuracy issues — three false claims in the new docs (restartMax=0 semantics, net-merge PATH resolution, server.address fallback) and one pre-existing-but-now-documented CI trigger corruption (`branches: ain]`) — all one-to-few-line fixes that should land before the v0.1.0 tag, but none breaks a user's VM, ships a broken endpoint, or opens a security hole.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        }
+++      ]

+++          "text": "Reviewer lens: BUILD / PORTABILITY (windows-gnu vs msvc) / DEPENDENCY+LICENSE HYGIENE / TEST QUALITY / CI+DOCS ACCURACY. Scope reviewed: `git diff 07ef5c5..40ee65c` (14 files, +1716/−255) plus the full current state of every touched source file, both workflows, the server script, the docs, and independent runs of every gate.",

+++          "text": "No P0. No P1. Eight P2s (doc/robustness nits, all fixable at close or carried). All 19 contract items verified implemented and tested; all gates reproduce green.",

+++          "text": "## Findings",
+++          "kind": "title"

+++          "text": "### P1 (should fix before release)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "None rose to P1. The closest candidate (snapshot downgrade gap, P2-1 below) was downgraded: the common-case snapshot round-trips both directions, the failure mode is non-destructive (v0.1.0 refuses to guess rather than deleting data) and recoverable by deleting `state/sysproxy.json`.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 (nits)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "1. **Snapshot downgrade direction undocumented** — `src/sysproxy.rs:52-56` (`SnapValue` doc: \"JSON shape (backward compatible with pre-S5 snapshots)\") and `src/sysproxy.rs:218-227`. The claim is true for the direction it states (v0.1.0 file → v0.2.0 binary; verified: the legacy test at `src/sysproxy.rs:611` pins the *actual* v0.1.0 on-disk shape — `proxyEnable` always a plain number, strings `null`/string, per `git show 07ef5c5:src/sysproxy.rs` — not a hand-invented format). The reverse direction is only partially compatible: a v0.2.0-written snapshot containing `\"proxyEnable\": null` (Absent — new shape; v0.1.0 always wrote a number) or any `{\"opaqueKind\": …}` marker fails v0.1.0's `u32`/`Option<String>` parse (`#[serde(default)]` does not rescue a present-but-wrong-typed field), so a downgraded v0.1.0 `load_snapshot` errs → `restore` errs → the stale snapshot persists and the proxy stays set until the file is deleted. Narrow (requires downgrade while a snapshot exists AND ProxyEnable absent/Opaque) and recoverable. Suggested fix: one doc sentence on `Snapshot` noting the downgrade caveat (\"v0.2.0 snapshots containing `null`/`opaqueKind` markers will not parse on v0.1.0 — delete state/sysproxy.json after downgrade\"); optionally serialize DWORD `Absent` as `0` (semantically identical: `EnableAction::Write(0)`) to keep even that corner downgrade-readable. No code change required for approval.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2. **rust-cache on the release tag is effectively a cold cache** — `.github/workflows/release.yml:17`. rust-cache's default key includes the workflow name (\"release\" ≠ \"ci\"), and GitHub cache scoping means caches saved on a tag ref are not restorable by later tags (only default-branch caches are). Harmless (perf only); the cache step still satisfies contract D2 as written (\"default key + the workflow name\"). Optional: `prefix-key` shared with ci.yml, or drop the step from release.yml.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "3. **cross-check cache not keyed on the zig version** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:51-56`. rust-cache@v2 stores `target/` (including `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` artifacts) keyed on Cargo.lock + rustc, not on the zig 0.17.1 pinned at ci.yml:53. Cargo fingerprints don't include the linker, so a future zig bump could in theory serve a stale *linked* exe from cache (rustc-produced rlibs are unaffected). rust-cache does NOT touch the zig toolchain itself (only cargo home + target — confirmed against the action's defaults), so the toolchain can't go stale. Suggested: prefix the job's cache key with the zig version or set `cache: false` on this job. Theoretical; the cross-check is a sanity leg, not the release artifact.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "4. **Packaging hard-required list omits two files the docs promise** — `.github/workflows/release.yml:34-49`: `README.md` and `QUICKSTART.md` are only best-effort copied (`if (Test-Path …)`), while QUICKSTART step 0 now states the zip's \"full contents\" includes both. They are tracked files, so every real tag build packages them; but if either were ever renamed, the zip would silently lack a doc that QUICKSTART promises (`fail_on_unmatched_files` can't catch it — it matches `dist/*.zip`). Suggested: add both to `$required`. (Pre-existing behavior; S5-D's doc change is what makes the promise explicit.)",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "5. **`join_reader` grace can silently drop captured output** — `src/main.rs:213-222` (`READER_GRACE` = 1 s): if a fast-exiting child produced output the reader threads haven't drained within 1 s, `run_bounded` returns the output it has (empty) and discards the rest. Correct and documented for the `xray version` use case (a few hundred bytes drain in ms); a trap if the helper is reused for a chatty child. Suggested: note the budget in the `run_bounded` doc, or make the grace apply only when a grandchild is suspected.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "6. **Slow-child test can orphan a bounded grandchild** — `src/main.rs:618-631`: `sh -c \"sleep 30\"` killed at 250 ms; on hosts where `sh` forks rather than execs the single command, the `sleep` survives ~30 s (a stray `sleep 30` was observed in the sandbox during my test run — other agents may also produce these). Self-terminating, no hang, no scratch files. Nit only.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "7. **THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md zmij row cites itoa's URL** — `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:28`: \"itoa, zmij | (serde_json deps) … https://crates.io/crates/itoa\" — zmij v1.0.23 is a real serde_json dep (Cargo.lock:176) and the MIT OR Apache-2.0 license claim is right, but the upstream link is itoa's. Pre-existing (file untouched by S5), license-hygiene lens nit.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "8. **Cargo.lock format silently downgraded v4 → v3** — `Cargo.lock:3`. The only lock changes in S5 are the multitunnel 0.1.0→0.2.0 bump and this format regression, i.e. the lock was regenerated/edited by something older than the sandbox cargo 1.100 (which preserves v4). Harmless — v3 is readable by every cargo ≥1.53 (and by the MSRV 1.78 claim), and `git status` stayed clean after test/clippy/zigbuild, proving the lock is in sync. No dependency additions/removals (diff verified). Informational.",

+++          "kind": "title"

+++        {
+++          "text": "1. **`sysproxy.rs:153-154, 418-421, 440-445` — Opaque tri-state leaves OUR values, not the user's, in place after a connect/disconnect cycle.** Two facets of one root gap (the contract's \"Opaque → leave untouched, that is the user's data\" ignores that `set()` overwrites those very values first): - **(a) Silent proxy-enable flip via type-mismatched `ProxyEnable`** — the exact scenario the review brief called out. With `ProxyEnable` present as a non-DWORD (e.g. REG_SZ `\"0\"`, written by some third-party proxy switchers): `set()` unconditionally writes DWORD 1 (`sysproxy.rs:418`); `snap_dword` records `Opaque` (`:344-348`); `restore` takes `EnableAction::Leave` (`:444`) and writes nothing. Result: after disconnect, `ProxyEnable` is still DWORD 1 pointing at the now-dead local HTTP inbound — every WinINET consumer is blackholed until the user manually disables the proxy. This is a *regression vs v0.1.0*, where the failed typed read snapshotted `0` and restore wrote 0 (disabled = fail-safe). Failure scenario is concrete; trigger is rare (Windows itself always writes DWORD there). - **(b) Exotic-typed REG_SZ values are destroyed by `set()` itself** — for a REG_EXPAND_SZ/REG_BINARY `ProxyServer`/`ProxyOverride`/`AutoConfigURL`, the unconditional `reg_set_string` loop (`:419-421`) replaces the user's value with our REG_SZ string before restore ever runs; `Opaque → Leave` then preserves *our* tunnel address, not the user's data. The S2-REV-C P2-5 goal is only half-achieved (restore no longer deletes — but `set` already clobbered).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },

+++          "text": "1. **`supervisor.rs:371,382` — residual check-then-act window in the exit-race fix.** The gates narrow the ~1 s re-set window to the gate→side-effect span, but a stop landing *after* the net-merge gate still lets `netmerge::on` complete up to `BOND_WAIT` = 15 s after an `emergency_stop` restored the proxy (and `sysproxy::set` for ~ms). Suggested: re-check `stop` *after* each side effect and best-effort undo (`sysproxy::restore` / `netmerge::off`). 2. **`sysproxy.rs:193-216` — `save_snapshot` is not atomic** (create_new + write_all, no fsync/rename). A crash mid-write leaves a truncated `sysproxy.json`; `load_snapshot` then errors and every caller drops the error (`let _ =` at `supervisor.rs:304,335,410,494,550,653`), so all future restores silently no-op — proxy stays enabled across reboots until the file is hand-deleted. Reuse the `fsutil` temp+fsync+rename pattern; log restore errors somewhere visible. 3. **`supervisor.rs:728` + `core_proc.rs:249,286` — `listen: \"localhost\"` passes `ensure_loopback_listen` (and now `Config::validate`) but `wait_for_port`/`socks_probe` parse `\"localhost:10808\"` as a `SocketAddr` → connect always fails at step 2 with \"invalid address\".** Pre-existing inconsistency (not an S5 regression); consider resolving localhost at load or rejecting with a precise message. 4. **`main.rs:213-222` — `join_reader` discards already-collected output when the 1 s grace expires** (grandchild inheriting the pipe), and the TimedOut path detaches readers entirely (documented). Bounded, no hang possible; doctor may show an empty version line.",

+++          "text": "1. **NEW — .github/workflows/release.yml:20-25 — release gate still scoped to the root package; the 7 new S6 crates are untested at tag time.** `cargo fmt --check` (no `--all`), `cargo clippy --all-targets` (no `--workspace`) and `cargo test` (no `--workspace`) cover only the root package = 148 of the 321 workspace tests; none of mt-links/mt-net/ mt-engine/mt-m3/mt-platform/mt-service/mt-app's own tests, lints or fmt run on a `v*` tag, and the workflow's own comments (S2-REV-B P1-1, \"a v* tag must never ship an untested build — tag pushes bypass ci.yml\") state exactly the guarantee that no longer holds — and all seven crates are *linked into* the shipped multitunnel.exe. ci.yml's test/lint/cross-check legs are all correctly `--workspace`, so the exposure is a tag cut from a commit whose main-push CI hasn't completed or was skipped; still a regression of a documented invariant. Fix: add `--workspace` / `--all` to the three gate lines (cheap, no downside on windows-latest).",

+++          "text": "2. **NEW — Cargo.toml:8 (echoed at README.md:218) — `rust-version = \"1.78\"` is now false; the effective MSRV is 1.97.** `material-colors 0.5.0` (mt-m3's color engine) declares `rust-version = \"1.97.0\"`; uuid 1.29.3 needs 1.89, tokio 1.54.1 needs 1.85, iced 0.13.1 needs 1.80. +++          "text": "### P1 (should fix before release)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "1. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:336` — leftover debug `eprintln!` in the production liveness path.** `child_addr_if_alive()` — called on EVERY engine connect/probe (i.e. per proxied connection) — contains `eprintln!(\"[dbg-eng] probe pid={pid:?} tw={tw:?}\")` in non-test code. Byte-verified with `od -An -c` (sandbox output-filter rule). This violates global contract rule 5 (\"tracing for diagnostics, no println! in libs\") and will spam stderr of `multitunnel gui` with one line per tunnel connection. It leaks no credentials (pid + try_wait result only) but is exactly the class of leftover that must not ship. One-line deletion.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "2. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:450-461` — the v0.2 kill-on-close Job Object was not ported; `xray.exe` is orphaned on abnormal GUI death.** The module doc claims \"the exact `core_proc` discipline\", but `src/core_proc.rs:583-618` (added by the 2026-11-17 v0.2-audit REV-C#2 backport, commit ff0abb4) puts the child in a Windows Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so the *kernel* guarantees \"the core cannot outlive this process\". `ManagedEngine` relies solely on `Drop::kill_current()`, which does not run on `TerminateProcess` (Task Manager kill), console Ctrl+C (the C-runtime exits without unwinding), power loss, or panic-abort — the precise scenarios the v0.2 audit fixed. Normal window close is safe (runtime drop cancels tasks → Arc chain → Drop → kill), so the orphan trigger is abnormal death; the orphan then runs an open REALITY tunnel with a loopback listener indefinitely. Restore the job-object wrapper (cfg(windows)) around the spawned child, or route spawns through `core_proc`.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "3. **`src/real_service.rs:919-949,688-714` + `crates/mt-app/src/app.rs:831-842` + `src/main.rs:605-625` — the GUI path loses the S2 supervisor's fail-open/self-heal contract for the system proxy (D5).** Three facets, one root cause (RealService has no supervision loop and no lifecycle hook): **(a)** closing the GUI window while Connected (or Ctrl+C on the console host) never calls `disconnect()`/`sysproxy::restore` — no `window::close` subscription, no exit hook in `cmd_gui`; the registry keeps pointing at the now-dead `127.0.0.1:10809`. **(b)** Nothing heals a stale snapshot at startup: v0.2 `connect` step 0 is \"sysproxy::restore() best-effort\" (supervisor.rs:25, contract line); `RealService::connect_flow` has no equivalent, and `disconnect()` in a fresh instance is a no-op (`sysproxy_set=false`), so a crashed run leaves browsing blackholed until the user manually fixes Windows settings or completes a full connect→disconnect cycle. **(c)** Engine give-up does not restore: after `ManagedEngine` exhausts its respawn budget the outbound errors permanently while `RealService` state stays `Connected` and the system proxy stays set — the v0.2 supervisor restored the proxy on restart exhaustion (supervisor.rs:20-22, D5). Keep-first `save_snapshot` (sysproxy.rs:219-223) does protect the user's original values from being overwritten, so this is recoverable-but-stuck, not data loss. Distinct from the parked \"no-snapshot-disable UX\" backlog item: v0.2 had all three recovery paths; v0.3's GUI has none.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "4. **`src/real_service.rs:696-699,587-588` — LAN/private traffic no longer bypasses the tunnel when the GUI system proxy is on (regression of a stated top-3 design principle).** `lib.rs:22` lists \"LAN/private traffic bypasses the tunnel\" as a project invariant, implemented in v0.2 twice over: the proxy override default is the full LAN bypass list `localhost;127.*;10.*;192.168.*;…;<local>` (config.rs:134-139) AND the generated Xray config routes `geoip:private → direct` (xrayconf.rs:66). The S6 RealService path writes a hard-coded `ProxyOverride=\"localhost\"` only, and the `Router` starts with an empty rule list whose default action is `Proxy` (SettingsFile default rules = `Vec::new()`). Net effect with `system_proxy=true`: requests to 192.168.x/10.x/172.16-31.x (router admin pages, printers, NAS) are sent through the VLESS tunnel to the remote server — breaking local access and leaking LAN hostnames/IPs to the tunnel operator. Fix: seed the default rules with a private-CIDR → direct rule (or route private IPs direct in `ProxyServer::establish`) and write the v0.2 LAN bypass override.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "5. **`crates/mt-platform/src/engine.rs:129-133` (via `crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:412`) — engine-download errors echo the full request URL, which can carry a credential (D9).** `ReqwestFetch::fetch` propagates `reqwest::Error` via `?`; its `Display` includes the full URL (\"error sending request for url (…)\"). The chain `ensure() → \"engine \\`{tag}\\`: binary download failed: {e}\" → connect error string → GUI LogLine + tracing` therefore prints whatever `$MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE_URL` contains — and user-set download-mirror URLs with embedded tokens (`https://host/xray.zip?token=…`) are a common pattern; the token then persists in GUI logs and any pasted bug report. mt-links solved exactly this with `reqwest::Error::without_url()` (subscription.rs:100-108) — mt-platform needs the same treatment in `fetch` (and `error_for_status` on the same line).",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "### P2 (notes)",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "1. **`src/real_service.rs:661,932-934` — stale `disconnect_requested` flag can spuriously abort one later connect.** A `disconnect()` landing in the window between the post-probe flag check (line 661) and session installation sets the flag but leaves the session Connected; the flag is consumed only by a later `connect_flow`, which then aborts itself right after its probe (one lost connect click, self-healing thereafter). Clear the flag at `begin_connect` or after session install. NEW. 2. **`crates/mt-app/src/app.rs:524-531` — the GUI cannot cancel a Connecting session.** `ConnectToggle(false)` only acts when `cur == Connected`; while Connecting the switch silently bounces back. The service already implements cancellation (`disconnect_requested` honored after the probe) — the GUI just never calls it in that state. NEW. 3. **`crates/mt-engine/src/engine.rs:316-324,428-430` + `src/real_service.rs:1015-1020` — two engines with the same profile tag race on shared files.** `test_latency` on the active profile while connected builds a second `ManagedEngine` with the same tag; both write `engine-<tag>.tmp` → `engine-<tag>.json` (one can truncate the other's in-flight temp; the fsutil single-writer assumption from S5-REV-C P2-6 is now reachable) and append to the same log handle. Worst case is a corrupt config → one failed spawn → retry; the misdirected port mostly self-corrects. Include the port or a nonce in the config/log filename, or serialize per-tag. NEW. 4.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {

+++        },

+++          "text": "- **D10/D9 redaction**: every link.rs/migrate.rs error carries lengths only; ignored query params log NAMES only (link.rs:246-248); subscription failures are numbered-line + redacted; `profiles` CLI never prints identity; engine errors carry tag/port/binary-path at most; no `tracing` site in the new code interpolates `identity`/`public_key`/`uuid` (grepped). The one gap is P1-5. The mt-links percent-decode policy (decode query values/userinfo, never authority; pbk/sid alphabet-validated after decode) deviates from v0.2's stricter \"no percent-decoding of stored fields\" but is the frozen S6 contract's \"parse liberally\", keeps `parse(render(p)) == p` a fixed point, and D10 strictness still gates the engine path (`endpoint_from_profile`: VLESS×Reality×Tcp×vision-or-absent, polite credential-free errors). - **mt-platform zip install**: zip-slip is closed by basename allowlist + `..`/`:`/leading-`/` rejection + flat extraction into a private staging dir; SHA256SUMS is verified at locate-time exactly per D14 (advisory warn by default, `MULTITUNNEL_ENGINE_STRICT=1` refuses — by design, not a bug); the staging→rename swap with backup+restore makes partial installs crash-safe; reqwest is `default-features = false` + `rustls-tls` (validation on, no `danger_accept_*` anywhere in the workspace). - **mt-net data plane**: socks5/http parsers are total-budget (10 s) and size-bounded (16 KiB head, wire-length-bounded ATYP reads), reject non-UTF-8/zero-length domains, answer BIND/UDP with REP 07 and unknown ATYP with REP 08; CONNECT authority forms incl.",
+++          "kind": "body"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "## Verdict rationale",
+++          "kind": "title"
+++        },
+++        {
+++          "text": "The S6 expert crates are individually solid: parsers are panic-free and credential-redacted, the data plane matches its frozen contract in every detail I could pin down, the zip installer's zip-slip and atomicity story is sound, and all six gates pass with a 321-test suite. What keeps this at five P1s rather than a BLOCK is that none of them is an exploitable hole, credential *value* leak to a remote party, data loss, or a reachable panic/deadlock — the closest to the P0 bar are the D5 fail-open regression (P1-3) and the LAN-bypass regression (P1-4), both of which require the user to enable the system-proxy feature and both recoverable by manual action. But they are real regressions against deliberately-fixed guarantees (the v0.2-audit Job Object, the S2 stale-heal/give-up contract, the \"LAN bypasses the tunnel\" invariant), and P1-1/P1-5 are trivial fixes, so all five should land before the v0.3 release ships. APPROVE per D6 (zero P0s), with the P1 list as the release blocker checklist.",

+++        }

+++          "text": "Task E core: user reported traffic still not split evenly — when one adapter reaches its maximum bandwidth, the remaining traffic does NOT split over to the remaining adapters. v0.7.0's balanced/priority (D23) spread per-connection load but stream-mode saturation spill was missing. +++(uses the real repo sources; builds throwaway stores under a temp dir,
+++plus one read-only check of the canonical store).

+++class RetrievalTests(unittest.TestCase):
+++    """RAG retrieval quality: BM25 ranking + graph expansion."""
+++
+++    @classmethod
+++    def setUpClass(cls):
+++        cls.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+++        cls.store = build_graph.build(Path(cls.tmp.name) / "g.json")
+++
+++    @classmethod
+++    def tearDownClass(cls):
+++        cls.tmp.cleanup()

+++    def _top_ids(self, query: str, k: int = 6, expand: int = 1) -> list[str]:
+++        res = graph_store.retrieve(self.store, query, k=k, expand=expand)
+++        self.assertTrue(res, f"no results for {query!r}")
+++        return [r["node"] for r in res]
+++
+++    def test_query_saturation(self):
+++        ids = self._top_ids("traffic split evenly adapter saturates maximum bandwidth")
+++        self.assertTrue(
+++            {"task:saturation-aware-split", "bug:uneven-traffic-split"} & set(ids),
+++            f"saturation query missed: {ids}")
+++
+++    def test_query_scroll_layout(self):
+++        ids = self._top_ids("status tab wheel scrolls connection frame graph fills")
+++        self.assertTrue(
+++            {"task:status-page-layout", "pm:playbook", "decision:D24"} & set(ids),
+++            f"scroll query missed: {ids}")
+++
+++    def test_query_tray(self):
+++        ids = self._top_ids("tray icon quick settings minimize close")
+++        self.assertTrue(
+++            {"task:e-ui-logo-titlebar-tray", "decision:D4"} & set(ids),
+++            f"tray query missed: {ids}")
+++
+++    def test_query_protocol(self):
+++        ids = self._top_ids("memory graph RAG agents retrieval")
+++        self.assertIn("protocol:memory-graph", ids,
+++                      f"protocol query missed: {ids}")
+++
+++    def test_query_release_history(self):
+++        ids = self._top_ids("v0.7.1 release verified assets")
+++        self.assertTrue(
+++            {"release:v0.7.1", "ledger:s13", "task:status-page-layout"} & set(ids),
+++            f"release query missed: {ids}")
+++
+++    def test_graph_expansion_adds_neighbors(self):
+++        res = graph_store.retrieve(
+++            self.store, "freedom loopback blackhole merge daemon", k=3, expand=1)
+++        hit_ids = {r["node"] for r in res if r["kind"] == "hit"}
+++        neighbor_ids = {r["node"] for r in res if r["kind"] == "neighbor"}
+++        self.assertTrue(neighbor_ids, "expansion returned no neighbors")
+++        # neighbors must be graph-adjacent to some hit
+++        adj = graph_store.adjacency(self.store)
+++        for nb in neighbor_ids:
+++            self.assertTrue(
+++                any(other in hit_ids for other, _, _ in adj.get(nb, [])),
+++                f"neighbor {nb} not adjacent to any hit")
+++
+++    def test_results_sorted_by_score(self):
+++        res = graph_store.retrieve(self.store, "carrier scheduler policy", k=6)
+++        scores = [r["score"] for r in res]
+++        self.assertEqual(scores, sorted(scores, reverse=True))
+++
+++    def test_empty_query(self):
+++        self.assertEqual(graph_store.retrieve(self.store, "zzzqqqxxx", k=3), [])
+++

+++#!/usr/bin/env python3
+++"""write_memory.py — the agent WRITE path into the MultiTunnel memory graph.
+++
+++Agents (main session, subagents, future sessions) append durable knowledge
+++without touching the builder. Writes land in harness/memory/curated/
+++(merged last at build time — curated wins on node-id collision) and the
+++store is rebuilt immediately. Validation is strict (whitelisted types/rels,
+++endpoints must exist); a failed rebuild rolls the curated change back.
+++
+++Usage (from repo root):
+++
+++    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py \\
+++        --node id=task:next-thing type=task title="Next thing" \\
+++        passage="What and why." tag=next source=harness/memory/LEDGER.md
+++
+++    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py \\
+++        --edge src=task:next-thing dst=project:multitunnel rel=part_of \\
+++        evidence="roadmap item"
+++
+++    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py --list          # curated ids
+++"""
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import argparse
+++import json
+++import shutil
+++import subprocess
+++import sys
+++import tempfile
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
+++import graph_store  # noqa: E402
+++from build_graph import DEFAULT_OUT, MEM, build  # noqa: E402
+++
+++CURATED = MEM / "curated"
+++
+++
+++def parse_kv(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+++    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+++    for it in items:
+++        if "=" not in it:
+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] expected KEY=VALUE, got: {it!r}")
+++        k, v = it.split("=", 1)
+++        out.setdefault(k, []).append(v)
+++    return out
+++
+++
+++def read_json(path: Path, default: dict) -> dict:
+++    if path.exists():
+++        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+++    return default
+++
+++
+++def write_json(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
+++    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+++    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
+++                    encoding="utf-8")
+++
+++
+++def do_node(kv: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
+++    need = ("id", "type", "title", "passage")
+++    for k in need:
+++        if k not in kv:
+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] --node requires {'/'.join(need)}=… (missing {k})")
+++    if kv["type"][0] not in graph_store.NODE_TYPES:
+++        raise SystemExit(f"[!] unknown node type {kv['type'][0]!r}; "
+++                         f"whitelist: {', '.join(graph_store.NODE_TYPES)}")
+++    node = {
+++        "id": kv["id"][0],
+++        "type": kv["type"][0],
+++        "title": kv["title"][0],
+++        "tags": kv.get("tag", []),
+++        "sources": [{"file": f, "anchor": ""}
+++                    for f in kv.get("source", ["harness/memory/curated/"])],
+++        "passages": [{"text": t, "kind": "body"} for t in kv["passage"]],
+++    }
+++    nodes = read_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", {"nodes": []})
+++    nodes["nodes"] = [n for n in nodes["nodes"] if n["id"] != node["id"]]
+++    nodes["nodes"].append(node)
+++    nodes["nodes"].sort(key=lambda n: n["id"])
+++    write_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", nodes)
+++    print(f"[✓] node upserted: {node['id']} ({len(nodes['nodes'])} curated)")
+++
+++
+++def do_edge(kv: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
+++    need = ("src", "dst", "rel")
+++    for k in need:
+++        if k not in kv:
+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] --edge requires {'/'.join(need)}=… (missing {k})")
+++    if kv["rel"][0] not in graph_store.EDGE_RELS:
+++        raise SystemExit(f"[!] unknown rel {kv['rel'][0]!r}; "
+++                         f"whitelist: {', '.join(graph_store.EDGE_RELS)}")
+++    edge = {
+++        "src": kv["src"][0],
+++        "dst": kv["dst"][0],
+++        "rel": kv["rel"][0],
+++        "evidence": kv.get("evidence", ["agent-curated"])[0],
+++    }
+++    edges = read_json(CURATED / "edges.json", {"edges": []})
+++    edges["edges"] = [e for e in edges["edges"]
+++                      if (e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"])
+++                      != (edge["src"], edge["dst"], edge["rel"])]
+++    edges["edges"].append(edge)
+++    edges["edges"].sort(key=lambda e: (e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"]))
+++    write_json(CURATED / "edges.json", edges)
+++    print(f"[✓] edge upserted: {edge['src']} --{edge['rel']}--> {edge['dst']}")
+++
+++
+++def rebuild_with_rollback(store_out: Path) -> None:
+++    """Rebuild; on any failure restore the curated files from a snapshot."""
+++    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+++        snap = Path(td)
+++        shutil.copytree(CURATED, snap / "curated")
+++        try:
+++            build(store_out, CURATED)
+++        except Exception as exc:  # rollback, then surface loudly
+++            shutil.rmtree(CURATED)
+++            shutil.copytree(snap / "curated", CURATED)
+++            try:
+++                build(store_out, CURATED)
+++            except Exception:
+++                pass
+++            raise SystemExit(f"[!] rebuild failed, curated change ROLLED BACK: {exc}")
+++    print(f"[✓] store rebuilt: {store_out}")
+++
+++
+++def main() -> int:
+++    global CURATED
+++    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+++    ap.add_argument("--node", nargs="+", metavar="KEY=VALUE",
+++                    help="node fields: id type title passage [tag source]")
+++    ap.add_argument("--edge", nargs="+", metavar="KEY=VALUE",
+++                    help="edge fields: src dst rel [evidence]")
+++    ap.add_argument("--list", action="store_true",
+++                    help="list curated node ids + edges")
+++    ap.add_argument("--no-rebuild", action="store_true",
+++                    help="skip the store rebuild (rarely wanted)")
+++    ap.add_argument("--curated", type=Path, default=CURATED,
+++                    help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # test hook: curated dir override
+++    ap.add_argument("--store-out", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT,
+++                    help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # test hook
+++    args = ap.parse_args()
+++
+++    CURATED = args.curated
+++
+++    if args.list:
+++        nodes = read_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", {"nodes": []})
+++        edges = read_json(CURATED / "edges.json", {"edges": []})
+++        for n in nodes["nodes"]:
+++            print(f"{n['type']:<12} {n['id']}")
+++        for e in edges["edges"]:
+++            print(f"edge         {e['src']} --{e['rel']}--> {e['dst']}")
+++        return 0
+++
+++    if not args.node and not args.edge:
+++        raise SystemExit("[!] nothing to do: pass --node or --edge (or --list)")
+++
+++    if args.node:
+++        do_node(parse_kv(args.node))
+++    if args.edge:
+++        do_edge(parse_kv(args.edge))
+++    if not args.no_rebuild:
+++        rebuild_with_rollback(args.store_out)
+++    return 0
+++
+++
+++if __name__ == "__main__":
+++    try:
+++        raise SystemExit(main())
+++    except BrokenPipeError:  # e.g. `write_memory.py --list | head`
+++        raise SystemExit(0)
++diff --git a/query_memory.py b/query_memory.py
++new file mode 100644
++index 0000000..d85190f
++--- /dev/null
+++++ b/query_memory.py
++@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+++#!/usr/bin/env python3
+++"""query_memory.py — RAG retrieval over the MultiTunnel agentic memory graph.
+++
+++Any agent (session start, subagent, future session) can pull relevant project
+++memory with one command from the repo root:
+++
+++    python3 query_memory.py "saturation aware traffic split"
+++    python3 query_memory.py "tray icon quick settings" --prompt
+++    python3 query_memory.py "verification gates" -k 8 --json
+++
+++Retrieval = BM25 (lexical, title-boosted) + graph-neighborhood expansion
+++(typed edges, 0.5^hop score decay). Modes:
+++    default   ranked human-readable passages with sources + graph links
+++    --json    structured results + induced subgraph (for programmatic agents)
+++    --prompt  paste-ready RAG context pack (inject into any agent prompt)
+++
+++The store is rebuilt automatically if missing. It lives at
+++harness/memory/store/memory_graph.json; rebuild it with
+++`python3 harness/memory/build_graph.py` (also run by update_memory.py).
+++"""
+++
+++from __future__ import annotations
+++
+++import argparse
+++import json
+++import subprocess
+++import sys
+++from pathlib import Path
+++
+++REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+++sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "harness" / "memory"))
+++
+++import graph_store  # noqa: E402
+++from build_graph import DEFAULT_OUT  # noqa: E402
+++
+++
+++def ensure_store(store_path: Path) -> dict:
+++    if not store_path.exists():
+++        print(f"[i] store missing — building {store_path}", file=sys.stderr)
+++        subprocess.run(
+++            [sys.executable, str(REPO / "harness" / "memory" / "build_graph.py")],
+++            check=True)
+++    return graph_store.load_store(store_path)
+++
+++
+++def main() -> int:
+++    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+++        description="RAG retrieval over the MultiTunnel memory graph")
+++    ap.add_argument("query", help="what to look for (natural language or keywords)")
+++    ap.add_argument("-k", type=int, default=5,
+++                    help="top hits (default 5; neighbors may add more)")
+++    ap.add_argument("--expand", type=int, default=1,
+++                    help="graph expansion hops (default 1; 0 = BM25 only)")
+++    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", dest="as_json",
+++                    help="structured JSON output")
+++    ap.add_argument("--prompt", action="store_true",
+++                    help="paste-ready RAG context pack for a consuming agent")
+++    ap.add_argument("--store", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT,
+++                    help="store path (default: %(default)s)")
+++    args = ap.parse_args()
+++
+++    store = ensure_store(args.store)
+++    results = graph_store.retrieve(store, args.query, k=args.k,
+++                                   expand=args.expand)
+++
+++    if args.as_json:
+++        ids = [r["node"] for r in results]
+++        print(json.dumps({
+++            "query": args.query,
+++            "k": args.k,
+++            "expand": args.expand,
+++            "as_of": store.get("as_of"),
+++            "results": results,
+++            "subgraph": graph_store.induced_subgraph(store, set(ids)),
+++        }, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
+++    elif args.prompt:
+++        print(graph_store.format_prompt(args.query, results, store))
+++    else:
+++        print(graph_store.format_human(args.query, results))
+++    return 0
+++
+++
+++if __name__ == "__main__":
+++    raise SystemExit(main())

+++++ b/update_memory.py

++@@ -64,5 +65,23 @@ def update_project_memory():

++     print(f"[✓] Successfully updated {MEMORY_FILE} with the last {NUM_COMMITS} commit diffs.")
+  
+- ## Blockers / open items
+- - None blocking. Watch item: disk headroom (release zigbuild needs ~5G;
+--  /tmp/mt-target/debug was cleaned before the release build; the rig
+--  rebuilds it). After a sandbox recycle the whole toolchain needs
+--  reinstalling (recipe below) — budget ~10 minutes — AND the clone may
+--  be a STALE snapshot: fetch origin/main FIRST and rebase before
+--  building on last session's tree (this stage's push was rejected for
+--  exactly that reason).
+-+  /tmp/mt-target/debug was cleaned before this release build and the
+-+  rig rebuilt it). After a sandbox recycle the toolchain needs
+-+  reinstalling (recipe below) AND the clone may be STALE: fetch
+-+  origin/main FIRST and rebase before building.
+++
+++def rebuild_memory_graph():
+++    """Rebuild the agentic memory graph store (S14 protocol). The store is
+++    the RAG source for `query_memory.py`; keeping it fresh on every ritual
+++    run means all agents always retrieve current state."""
+++    script = Path(__file__).parent / "harness" / "memory" / "build_graph.py"
+++    if not script.exists():

+++        assert_eq!(carrier_score(&idle), 0.0);
+++    }

+++        // The user's saturation complaint: adapter 0 (Wi-Fi) is at its

+++        // adapter 1 (Ethernet) has headroom (offered 0.2, delivers 2.0).
+++        // Capacity-aware Balanced must pick adapter 1 even though adapter
+++        // 0 has the SHALLOWER writer queue (queue depth alone is not a
+++        // saturation signal).
+++        let slots = [
+++            cap_slot(0, 10_000, 30, 1.6 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 1.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++            cap_slot(1, 900_000, 40, 0.2 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 2.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++        ];
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots), Some(1));
+++        // Equal relative load (both 0.5, above the probe floor) →
+++        // capacity-proportional tie via the cursor.
+++        let tied = [
+++            cap_slot(0, 0, 30, 1.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 2.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++            cap_slot(1, 0, 40, 0.5 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 1.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++        ];
+++        let mut cursor = 0u64;
+++        let seq: Vec<usize> = (0..2)
+++            .map(|_| pick_carrier_index(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &tied, &mut cursor).unwrap())
+++            .collect();
+++        assert_eq!(seq, vec![0, 1]);

+++    #[test]
+++    fn balanced_spreads_proportionally_to_reported_capacity() {
+++        // 10:1 capacity ratio. Greedy min-relative-load picking converges
+++        // on the equilibrium where every carrier's assign/deliver ratio is
+++        // equal — i.e. the fat path ends up carrying ~10x the thin one's
+++        // share. Assert the crossover points around that equilibrium.
+++        let fat = cap_slot(0, 0, 30, 0.0, 10_000_000.0);
+++        let thin = cap_slot(1, 0, 40, 3_000_000.0, 1_000_000.0);
+++        // fat score 0 < thin score 3.0 → fat wins; still winning at 0.4.
+++        let mut slots = [fat, thin];
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots), Some(0));
+++        slots[0].assign_bps = 4_000_000.0; // 0.4 < 3.0
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots), Some(0));
+++        // Near equilibrium (fat 0.99 vs thin 1.0) fat still wins…
+++        slots[0].assign_bps = 9_900_000.0; // 0.99
+++        slots[1].assign_bps = 1_000_000.0; // 1.0
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots), Some(0));
+++        // …and flips the moment its relative load exceeds thin's.
+++        slots[0].assign_bps = 10_100_000.0; // 1.01 > 1.0
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Balanced, &slots), Some(1));
+++    }

+++        // Adapter 0 is #1 in user order and its writer queue is EMPTY —
+++        // but the peer reports it only delivers 1 MiB/s while it is being
+++        // offered 1.2 MiB/s (score 1.2 ≥ PRIORITY_SPILL_RATIO) → spill to
+++        // adapter 1 even though its queue is deeper.
+++        let c0_ceiling = [
+++            cap_slot(0, 0, 30, 1.2 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 1.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++            cap_slot(1, 300_000, 40, 0.1 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 4.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++        ];
+++        assert_eq!(
+++            pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Priority, &c0_ceiling),
+++            Some(1),
+++            "queue-empty but over-reported #1 must spill"
+++        );
+++        // Just under the ratio (1.1 < 1.15) → #1 keeps filling.
+++        let c0_healthy = [
+++            cap_slot(0, 0, 30, 1.1 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 1.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++            cap_slot(1, 300_000, 40, 0.1 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 4.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++        ];
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Priority, &c0_healthy), Some(0));
+++        // Everything over-reported → the least RELATIVE load takes the
+++        // excess (0.9 beats 2.5), not the least-queued.
+++        let all_over = [
+++            cap_slot(
+++                0,
+++                1_000_000,

+++                0.9 * 1024.0 * 1024.0,

+++            cap_slot(1, 100_000, 40, 5.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0, 2.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0),
+++        ];
+++        assert_eq!(pick1(mt_net::MergePolicy::Priority, &all_over), Some(0));
+++    }

+++
+++    #[test]
+++    fn would_overflow_mirrors_the_insert_boundary() {
+++        // S14: the endpoint's backpressure path polls would_overflow BEFORE
+++        // inserting — it must agree exactly with insert's Overflow check.
+++        let mut rb = ReorderBuffer::new(16);
+++        assert!(rb.insert(5, vec![0u8; 10]).is_ok());
+++        assert!(!rb.would_overflow(6), "10 + 6 == cap 16 fits");
+++        assert!(rb.would_overflow(7), "10 + 7 > cap 16 overflows");
+++        // An insert that would_overflow rejects must be the same size that
+++        // insert() errors on — the pause loop's invariant.
+++        let probe = vec![0u8; 7];
+++        assert_eq!(rb.would_overflow(probe.len()), rb.insert(6, probe).is_err());
+++        assert_eq!(rb.buffered_bytes(), 10, "rejected insert left state intact");
+++        // Once the gap ahead of seq 5 drains (in-order 0..=4 flushes the
+++        // buffered 5), the previously-rejected frame fits — the backpressure
+++        // pause resolves instead of erroring.
+++        for seq in 0..5u64 {
+++            assert!(rb.insert(seq, vec![0u8; 4]).is_ok());
+++        }
+++        assert_eq!(rb.buffered_bytes(), 0, "seq 5 flushed by the 0..=4 run");
+++        assert!(!rb.would_overflow(7));
+++        assert!(rb.insert(6, vec![0u8; 7]).is_ok());
+++    }
++ }

-+class RetrievalTests(unittest.TestCase):

-+    @classmethod

-+            f"release query missed: {ids}")

-+    def test_graph_expansion_adds_neighbors(self):
-+        res = graph_store.retrieve(
-+            self.store, "freedom loopback blackhole merge daemon", k=3, expand=1)

-+        self.assertEqual(scores, sorted(scores, reverse=True))

-+    def test_empty_query(self):

-+#!/usr/bin/env python3
-+"""write_memory.py — the agent WRITE path into the MultiTunnel memory graph.
-+
-+Agents (main session, subagents, future sessions) append durable knowledge
-+without touching the builder. Writes land in harness/memory/curated/
-+(merged last at build time — curated wins on node-id collision) and the
-+store is rebuilt immediately. Validation is strict (whitelisted types/rels,
-+endpoints must exist); a failed rebuild rolls the curated change back.
-+
-+Usage (from repo root):
-+
-+    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py \\
-+        --node id=task:next-thing type=task title="Next thing" \\
-+        passage="What and why." tag=next source=harness/memory/LEDGER.md
-+
-+    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py \\
-+        --edge src=task:next-thing dst=project:multitunnel rel=part_of \\
-+        evidence="roadmap item"
-+
-+    python3 harness/memory/write_memory.py --list          # curated ids
-+"""
-+
-+from __future__ import annotations
-+
-+import argparse
-+import json
-+import shutil
-+import subprocess
-+import sys
-+import tempfile
-+from pathlib import Path
-+
-+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
-+import graph_store  # noqa: E402
-+from build_graph import DEFAULT_OUT, MEM, build  # noqa: E402
-+
-+CURATED = MEM / "curated"
-+
-+
-+def parse_kv(items: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
-+    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
-+    for it in items:
-+        if "=" not in it:
-+            raise SystemExit(f"[!] expected KEY=VALUE, got: {it!r}")
-+        k, v = it.split("=", 1)
-+        out.setdefault(k, []).append(v)
-+    return out
-+
-+
-+def read_json(path: Path, default: dict) -> dict:
-+    if path.exists():
-+        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
-+    return default
-+
-+
-+def write_json(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
-+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
-+    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
-+                    encoding="utf-8")
-+
-+
-+def do_node(kv: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
-+    need = ("id", "type", "title", "passage")
-+    for k in need:
-+        if k not in kv:
-+            raise SystemExit(f"[!] --node requires {'/'.join(need)}=… (missing {k})")
-+    if kv["type"][0] not in graph_store.NODE_TYPES:
-+        raise SystemExit(f"[!] unknown node type {kv['type'][0]!r}; "
-+                         f"whitelist: {', '.join(graph_store.NODE_TYPES)}")
-+    node = {
-+        "id": kv["id"][0],
-+        "type": kv["type"][0],
-+        "title": kv["title"][0],
-+        "tags": kv.get("tag", []),
-+        "sources": [{"file": f, "anchor": ""}
-+                    for f in kv.get("source", ["harness/memory/curated/"])],
-+        "passages": [{"text": t, "kind": "body"} for t in kv["passage"]],
-+    }
-+    nodes = read_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", {"nodes": []})
-+    nodes["nodes"] = [n for n in nodes["nodes"] if n["id"] != node["id"]]
-+    nodes["nodes"].append(node)
-+    nodes["nodes"].sort(key=lambda n: n["id"])
-+    write_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", nodes)
-+    print(f"[✓] node upserted: {node['id']} ({len(nodes['nodes'])} curated)")
-+
-+
-+def do_edge(kv: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
-+    need = ("src", "dst", "rel")
-+    for k in need:
-+        if k not in kv:
-+            raise SystemExit(f"[!] --edge requires {'/'.join(need)}=… (missing {k})")
-+    if kv["rel"][0] not in graph_store.EDGE_RELS:
-+        raise SystemExit(f"[!] unknown rel {kv['rel'][0]!r}; "
-+                         f"whitelist: {', '.join(graph_store.EDGE_RELS)}")
-+    edge = {
-+        "src": kv["src"][0],
-+        "dst": kv["dst"][0],
-+        "rel": kv["rel"][0],
-+        "evidence": kv.get("evidence", ["agent-curated"])[0],
-+    }
-+    edges = read_json(CURATED / "edges.json", {"edges": []})
-+    edges["edges"] = [e for e in edges["edges"]
-+                      if (e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"])
-+                      != (edge["src"], edge["dst"], edge["rel"])]
-+    edges["edges"].append(edge)
-+    edges["edges"].sort(key=lambda e: (e["src"], e["dst"], e["rel"]))
-+    write_json(CURATED / "edges.json", edges)
-+    print(f"[✓] edge upserted: {edge['src']} --{edge['rel']}--> {edge['dst']}")
-+
-+
-+def rebuild_with_rollback(store_out: Path) -> None:
-+    """Rebuild; on any failure restore the curated files from a snapshot."""
-+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
-+        snap = Path(td)
-+        shutil.copytree(CURATED, snap / "curated")
-+        try:
-+            build(store_out, CURATED)
-+        except Exception as exc:  # rollback, then surface loudly
-+            shutil.rmtree(CURATED)
-+            shutil.copytree(snap / "curated", CURATED)
-+            try:
-+                build(store_out, CURATED)
-+            except Exception:
-+                pass
-+            raise SystemExit(f"[!] rebuild failed, curated change ROLLED BACK: {exc}")
-+    print(f"[✓] store rebuilt: {store_out}")
-+
-+
-+def main() -> int:
-+    global CURATED
-+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
-+    ap.add_argument("--node", nargs="+", metavar="KEY=VALUE",
-+                    help="node fields: id type title passage [tag source]")
-+    ap.add_argument("--edge", nargs="+", metavar="KEY=VALUE",
-+                    help="edge fields: src dst rel [evidence]")
-+    ap.add_argument("--list", action="store_true",
-+                    help="list curated node ids + edges")
-+    ap.add_argument("--no-rebuild", action="store_true",
-+                    help="skip the store rebuild (rarely wanted)")
-+    ap.add_argument("--curated", type=Path, default=CURATED,
-+                    help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # test hook: curated dir override
-+    ap.add_argument("--store-out", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT,
-+                    help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # test hook
-+    args = ap.parse_args()
-+
-+    CURATED = args.curated
-+
-+    if args.list:
-+        nodes = read_json(CURATED / "nodes.json", {"nodes": []})
-+        edges = read_json(CURATED / "edges.json", {"edges": []})
-+        for n in nodes["nodes"]:

+## App identity & tray (v0.9) — logo, blended title bar, close-to-tray
+
+The window itself became a first-class part of the app (all of it in the
+GUI, no new dependencies):
+
+- **Your logo everywhere**: the window icon, the taskbar entry, the
+  title bar and the tray icon all use the attached logo image
+  (re-generated at build time by `scripts/make_logo_assets.py` —
+  stdlib-only PNG decode, emblem crops for the small sizes, full lockup
+  for 256 px).
+- **Chromium-style title bar**: the native window chrome is replaced by
+  an in-app strip on the SAME surface as the page — logo + app name on
+  the left, minimize/maximize/close on the right, and every other pixel
+  of the strip drags the window (a fast second press maximizes, like a
+  double-click on a classic title bar).
+- **Close-to-tray toggle** (Settings → Window & tray): when ON, the ✕
+  button hides the window into the tray instead of exiting — the tunnel
+  keeps running. OFF (default) closing really closes.
+- **A persistent tray icon** while the app is open or hidden
+  (Windows; raw Win32, same approach as the legacy `multitunnel-tray`
+  companion): left-click reopens the window, and it survives an
+  explorer.exe restart.
+- **Quick Settings on right-click**: the tray menu is built fresh from
+  live state — Connect/Disconnect (state-reflecting), the server list
+  (radio-checked on the active profile), Open MultiTunnel and Exit.
+  Selections ride the same paths as the GUI (switching a server from the
+  tray reconnects exactly like the Status dropdown does).
+
+On platforms without a tray the toggle degrades honestly: the window
+minimizes instead of hiding, so it stays reachable.
+
 ## Rendering fixes (v0.6, v0.6.1)
 
 v0.5.1 shipped three rendering defects, all root-caused and fixed via

+    fn handle_close_requested(&mut self) -> iced::Task<Message> {
+        let tray_alive = self.tray.is_some();
+        match close_action(self.settings.close_to_tray, tray_alive) {
+            CloseAction::Hide => {
+                if let Some(id) = self.window_id {
+                    util::push_log(

+                        "INFO  gui: hidden to tray — reopen from the tray icon \
+                         (right-click it for Quick Settings)"
+                            .to_string(),
+                    );
+                    return iced::window::run_with_handle(id, hide_window).map(Message::Event);
+                }
+            }
+            CloseAction::Minimize => {
+                util::push_log(
+                    &mut self.logs,
+                    "INFO  gui: close-to-tray is on but this platform has no tray \
+                     — minimizing instead (the window stays reachable)"
+                        .to_string(),
+                );
+                if let Some(id) = self.window_id {
+                    return iced::window::minimize(id, true);
+                }
+            }
+            CloseAction::Exit => return self.begin_exit(),
+        }

+    }

+    /// Real exit: tray down first (icon + thread), then close the window
+    /// (with `exit_on_close_request: false`, closing is OUR call).
+    fn begin_exit(&mut self) -> iced::Task<Message> {
+        if let Some(tray) = self.tray.take() {
+            tray.shutdown(std::time::Duration::from_millis(600));
+        }
+        if let Some(id) = self.window_id {
+            return iced::window::close(id);
+        }

+            self.tray_model = Some(model.clone());

+}
+
+/// The close-request decision: only Windows-with-a-live-tray can truly
+/// hide; everywhere else close-to-tray degrades to minimize; off = exit.
+pub fn close_action(close_to_tray: bool, tray_alive: bool) -> CloseAction {
+    if !close_to_tray {
+        return CloseAction::Exit;
+    }
+    if tray_alive && cfg!(windows) {
+        CloseAction::Hide
+    } else {
+        CloseAction::Minimize
+    }
+}
+
+/// Titlebar double-click window (a bit above the OS default 500 ms to be
+/// forgiving over a drag that never started).
+const DOUBLE_CLICK_MS: u64 = 450;
+
+/// Pure double-press detector for the titlebar strip.
+pub fn is_double_click(last: Option<std::time::Instant>, now: std::time::Instant) -> bool {
+    last.is_some_and(|t| now.duration_since(t) <= std::time::Duration::from_millis(DOUBLE_CLICK_MS))
+}
+
+/// Hide the main window via its native handle (run on the iced runtime
+/// through `window::run_with_handle`; Windows-only effect — on other
+/// platforms the caller already chose Minimize).
+fn hide_window(handle: iced::window::raw_window_handle::WindowHandle<'_>) -> ServiceEvent {
+    #[cfg(windows)]
+    {
+        use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{ShowWindow, SW_HIDE};
+        if let iced::window::raw_window_handle::RawWindowHandle::Win32(w) = handle.as_raw() {
+            // SAFETY: w.hwnd is the live main window's handle handed to us
+            // by the iced runtime; SW_HIDE is a plain visibility toggle.
+            unsafe { ShowWindow(w.hwnd.get() as _, SW_HIDE) };
+        }
+    }
+    #[cfg(not(windows))]
+    {
+        // Unreachable in practice (the caller chose Minimize on this
+        // platform); kept for cross-platform compilation of the closure.
+        let _ = &handle;
+    }
+    ServiceEvent::LogLine("INFO  gui: window hidden to tray".to_string())
+}
+
+/// Restore the main window from the tray (inverse of [`hide_window`]).
+fn show_window(handle: iced::window::raw_window_handle::WindowHandle<'_>) -> ServiceEvent {
+    #[cfg(windows)]
+    {
+        use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{ShowWindow, SW_SHOW};
+        if let iced::window::raw_window_handle::RawWindowHandle::Win32(w) = handle.as_raw() {
+            // SAFETY: see hide_window; SW_SHOW restores without focus
+            // stealing rules (gain_focus follows separately).
+            unsafe { ShowWindow(w.hwnd.get() as _, SW_SHOW) };
+        }
+    }
+    #[cfg(not(windows))]
+    {
+        // Unreachable in practice (the tray is Windows-only); kept for
+        // cross-platform compilation of the closure.
+        let _ = &handle;
+    }
+    ServiceEvent::LogLine("INFO  gui: window restored from tray".to_string())
+}

+
+    /// S15: the close-request decision table (D25 §3). The platform arm
+    /// is compiled per-target; this test pins the reachable arms.
+    #[test]
+    fn close_action_decision() {
+        // Off (the default) always really closes.
+        assert_eq!(close_action(false, false), CloseAction::Exit);
+        assert_eq!(close_action(false, true), CloseAction::Exit);
+        // On: Windows + live tray hides; everything else minimizes.

+/// The embedded 24×24 titlebar emblem (RGBA8; `scripts/make_logo_assets.py`).
+const LOGO_24: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../../../assets/logo_24.rgba");
+
+/// S15 (D25): the app-drawn title bar — the window runs with
+/// `decorations: false`, so this strip IS the chrome. Chromium-style: the
+/// strip sits on the page surface (no separator, it blends), the logo +
+/// title live on the left, the window controls on the right, and every
+/// non-button pixel drags the window (double-press maximizes).
+pub fn titlebar(app: &App) -> Element<'_> {
+    let s = app.theme.scheme;
+    let ts = app.theme.ts;
+    let logo = image(image::Handle::from_rgba(24, 24, LOGO_24.to_vec()))
+        .width(Length::Fixed(20.0))
+        .height(Length::Fixed(20.0));
+    let title = text("MultiTunnel")
+        .size(ts.title_m.size)
+        .color(s.on_surface_variant);
+    let identity = row![logo, title]
+        .spacing(10)
+        .align_y(iced::Alignment::Center);
+    // The whole strip (minus the buttons — inner widgets capture first)
+    // drags the window; a fast second press maximizes.
+    let drag = mouse_area(
+        container(identity)
+            .width(Length::Fill)
+            .height(Length::Fill)
+            .padding(Padding::new(0.0).left(14.0)),
+    )
+    .on_press(Message::TitleDrag);
+    let make_ctl = |label: &str, msg: Message| {
+        button(text(label.to_string()).size(ts.headline_s.size))
+            .style(t3::text_button(s))
+            .padding(Padding::new(0.0).left(14.0).right(14.0))
+            .height(Length::Fill)
+            .on_press(msg)
+    };
+    let max_glyph = if app.window_maximized { "▣" } else { "□" };
+    let controls = row![
+        make_ctl("—", Message::TitleMinimize),
+        make_ctl(max_glyph, Message::TitleMaximize),
+        make_ctl("×", Message::TitleClose),
+    ]
+    .height(Length::Fill);
+    container(row![drag, controls].height(Length::Fill))
+        .height(Length::Fixed(40.0))
+        .width(Length::Fill)
+        .into()
+}
