new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a363a2c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crates/mt-app/src/tray.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,540 @@
+//! mt-app's in-app notification-area tray (S15, D25): a persistent icon
+//! while the app is open or minimized-to-tray, with the Quick Settings
+//! menu on right-click.
+//!
+//! CONTRACT (mirrors the S3-proven `src/tray.rs` shapes — raw Win32 via
+//! windows-sys per D4, NOT the tray-icon crate):
+//! - [`spawn`] creates the icon and returns `(TrayHandle, Receiver)`; the
+//!   handle sends [`TrayCommand`]s (tooltip/model/shutdown) and the
+//!   receiver yields [`TrayEvent`]s (open/connect/disconnect/server/exit).
+//!   The tray thread owns a HIDDEN TOP-LEVEL STATIC window (subclassed via
+//!   `GWLP_WNDPROC` — top-level, NOT message-only, so `TaskbarCreated`
+//!   reaches it and the pre-menu `SetForegroundWindow` works), polls the
+//!   command channel on a 50 ms `WM_TIMER`, and tears down cleanly
+//!   (`NIM_DELETE` + `DestroyIcon` + ack) on [`TrayCommand::Shutdown`].
+//! - LEFT click → [`TrayEvent::Open`] (restore the window). RIGHT click →
+//!   the Quick Settings menu (KB Q135788 dismissal pattern).
+//! - The menu is built FRESH from the last [`TrayCommand::Model`] at every
+//!   open (pure, host-testable model — see [`quick_menu`]); selections map
+//!   back through [`action_for_id`] and ride the event channel to the app,
+//!   which reuses its existing Message paths (no new service calls).
+//! - Non-Windows: [`spawn`] returns `None` (stub) — the GUI keeps working;
+//!   `TrayHandle` exists as an uninhabited type so app state compiles.
+//!
+//! Unsafe-FFI review protocol (D6, same as src/tray.rs): every `unsafe`
+//! block carries a `SAFETY:` comment; all logic that can be pure lives in
+//! the host-testable helpers below and is unit tested on Linux.
+
+use mt_service::{ProfileView, ServiceState, StatusSnapshot};
+
+/// The Quick Settings menu model (pure; built by the app from live state,
+/// rendered by the tray thread). [`assign_ids`] flattens it into the id
+/// space `TrackPopupMenuEx` reports back via `WM_COMMAND`.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
+pub enum QuickEntry {
+    /// Horizontal rule.
+    Separator,
+    /// Grayed, unselectable info line (the header).
+    Header(String),
+    /// Selectable action.
+    Item {
+        label: String,
+        action: QuickAction,
+        enabled: bool,
+        /// Radio-style check mark.
+        checked: bool,
+    },
+    /// Submenu (the server list).
+    Submenu {
+        label: String,
+        items: Vec<QuickEntry>,
+    },
+}
+
+/// What a menu selection asks the app to do.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum QuickAction {
+    Connect,
+    Disconnect,
+    /// Make this profile id active (reconnects, like the GUI picker).
+    Server(String),
+    /// Restore/focus the main window.
+    Open,
+    /// Really exit (bypasses close-to-tray).
+    Exit,
+}
+
+/// Id space layout: the header and separators are unselectable (id 0);
+/// items get consecutive ids starting at 1, submenus flattened after
+/// their parent. `u16` is exactly `WM_COMMAND`'s LOWORD(wParam).
+pub(crate) const FIRST_ID: u16 = 1;
+
+/// The Quick Settings menu from live app state. The shape is STABLE
+/// (pinned by tests): header, state-appropriate connect/disconnect,
+/// server submenu (radio-checked active, labels are the GUI's profile
+/// tags), Open, Exit.
+pub fn quick_menu(
+    state: Option<ServiceState>,
+    profiles: &[ProfileView],
+    active_tag: &str,
+) -> Vec<QuickEntry> {
+    let state = state.unwrap_or(ServiceState::Disconnected);
+    let connected = state == ServiceState::Connected;
+    let busy = state == ServiceState::Connecting;
+    let header = match state {
+        ServiceState::Connected => "MultiTunnel — connected",
+        ServiceState::Connecting => "MultiTunnel — connecting…",
+        ServiceState::Failed => "MultiTunnel — connection failed",
+        ServiceState::Disconnected => "MultiTunnel — disconnected",
+    };
+    let mut items = vec![
+        QuickEntry::Header(header.to_string()),
+        QuickEntry::Separator,
+    ];
+    // One state-appropriate item; disabled while a transition is in
+    // flight (the same rule the legacy tray's menu_plan applies).
+    if connected {
+        items.push(QuickEntry::Item {
+            label: "Disconnect".to_string(),
+            action: QuickAction::Disconnect,
+            enabled: !busy,
+            checked: false,
+        });
+    } else {
+        items.push(QuickEntry::Item {
+            label: "Connect".to_string(),
+            action: QuickAction::Connect,
+            enabled: !busy,
+            checked: false,
+        });
+    }
+    if !profiles.is_empty() {
+        let servers = profiles
+            .iter()
+            .map(|p| QuickEntry::Item {
+                label: p.tag.clone(),
+                action: QuickAction::Server(p.id.clone()),
+                enabled: true,
+                checked: p.tag == active_tag,
+            })
+            .collect();
+        items.push(QuickEntry::Submenu {
+            label: "Server".to_string(),
+            items: servers,
+        });
+    }
+    items.push(QuickEntry::Separator);
+    items.push(QuickEntry::Item {
+        label: "Open MultiTunnel".to_string(),
+        action: QuickAction::Open,
+        enabled: true,
+        checked: false,
+    });
+    items.push(QuickEntry::Item {
+        label: "Exit".to_string(),
+        action: QuickAction::Exit,
+        enabled: true,
+        checked: false,
+    });
+    items
+}
+
+/// Assign the flat `(id, action)` map for a model (ids are stable for a
+/// given model shape; the tray stores this alongside the model). Disabled
+/// items keep their slot (ids stay stable when only enablement changes);
+/// grayed rows can never be selected, so their ids simply never fire.
+pub fn assign_ids(model: &[QuickEntry]) -> Vec<(u16, QuickAction)> {
+    fn walk(entries: &[QuickEntry], out: &mut Vec<QuickAction>) {
+        for e in entries {
+            match e {
+                QuickEntry::Separator | QuickEntry::Header(_) => {}
+                QuickEntry::Item { action, .. } => out.push(action.clone()),
+                QuickEntry::Submenu { items, .. } => walk(items, out),
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let mut flat = Vec::new();
+    walk(model, &mut flat);
+    flat.into_iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .map(|(i, action)| (FIRST_ID + i as u16, action))
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// Resolve a `WM_COMMAND` id back to its action (None for 0/unknown).
+pub fn action_for_id(ids: &[(u16, QuickAction)], id: u16) -> Option<QuickAction> {
+    ids.iter().find(|(i, _)| *i == id).map(|(_, a)| a.clone())
+}
+
+/// Tray tooltip (NIF_TIP caps at 128 UTF-16 units incl. NUL; the caller
+/// may pass any string — the FFI side truncates safely).
+pub fn tooltip(state: ServiceState, active_tag: &str) -> String {
+    let word = match state {
+        ServiceState::Connected => "connected",
+        ServiceState::Connecting => "connecting…",
+        ServiceState::Failed => "connection failed",
+        ServiceState::Disconnected => "disconnected",
+    };
+    if active_tag.is_empty() {
+        format!("MultiTunnel — {word}")
+    } else {
+        format!("MultiTunnel — {word} [{active_tag}]")
+    }
+}
+
+/// True when the tray event stream must be wired (state derived, not
+/// cfg'd, so the decision is unit-testable on every platform).
+pub fn tray_available() -> bool {
+    cfg!(windows)
+}
+
+/// Build the menu model from a status snapshot + profile list (the exact
+/// input the app has at hand on every tick). `active_tag` is what the
+/// snapshot reports (the GUI dropdown matches on it too).
+pub fn model_from(status: Option<&StatusSnapshot>, profiles: &[ProfileView]) -> Vec<QuickEntry> {
+    let state = status.map(|s| s.state);
+    let active_tag = status
+        .and_then(|s| s.active_profile.clone())
+        .unwrap_or_default();
+    quick_menu(state, profiles, &active_tag)
+}
+
+// ---- commands / events (cross-thread API) -----------------------------------
+
+/// App → tray.
+#[derive(Debug)]
+pub enum TrayCommand {
+    /// Replace the tooltip (sent on tick, only when the text changed).
+    Tooltip(String),
+    /// Replace the Quick Settings model.
+    Model(Vec<QuickEntry>),
+    /// Tear down (NIM_DELETE + ack on the returned channel).
+    Shutdown(std::sync::mpsc::SyncSender<()>),
+}
+
+/// Tray → app.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum TrayEvent {
+    /// Left click / "Open MultiTunnel" — restore + focus the window.
+    Open,
+    Connect,
+    Disconnect,
+    Server(String),
+    /// "Exit" — really exit (bypasses close-to-tray).
+    Exit,
+}
+
+impl From<&QuickAction> for TrayEvent {
+    fn from(a: &QuickAction) -> Self {
+        match a {
+            QuickAction::Connect => TrayEvent::Connect,
+            QuickAction::Disconnect => TrayEvent::Disconnect,
+            QuickAction::Server(id) => TrayEvent::Server(id.clone()),
+            QuickAction::Open => TrayEvent::Open,
+            QuickAction::Exit => TrayEvent::Exit,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+// ---- embedded icon (shared with the legacy tray: same assets/icon.ico) ------
+// FFI-only helpers: used by the win module and the host tests below
+// (same cfg as the legacy src/tray.rs).
+#[cfg(any(windows, test))]
+pub(crate) mod ffi_helpers {
+    /// The app logo as a multi-size ICO (see `scripts/make_logo_assets.py`).
+    pub(crate) static ICON_BYTES: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../../../assets/icon.ico");
+
+    /// Preferred icon edge for the tray slot (the ICO carries 16/32/48/256).
+    pub(crate) const ICON_SIZE: u32 = 32;
+
+    /// One ICO directory entry (bounds-checked in [`ico_entries`]).
+    pub(crate) struct IcoEntry {
+        pub width: u32,
+        pub height: u32,
+        pub offset: u32,
+        pub bytes: u32,
+    }
+
+    /// Parse the ICO directory (ICONDIR + ICONDIRENTRY array). Rejects empty
+    /// files, non-icon types, bogus counts and entries pointing outside the
+    /// file (fail closed).
+    pub(crate) fn ico_entries(ico: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<IcoEntry>> {
+        if ico.len() < 6 {
+            return None;
+        }
+        let reserved = u16::from_le_bytes([ico[0], ico[1]]);
+        let kind = u16::from_le_bytes([ico[2], ico[3]]);
+        let count = u16::from_le_bytes([ico[4], ico[5]]) as usize;
+        if reserved != 0 || kind != 1 || count == 0 || ico.len() < 6 + 16 * count {
+            return None;
+        }
+        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
+        for i in 0..count {
+            let e = &ico[6 + 16 * i..6 + 16 * i + 16];
+            let w = e[0] as u32;
+            let h = e[1] as u32;
+            let bytes = u32::from_le_bytes([e[8], e[9], e[10], e[11]]);
+            let offset = u32::from_le_bytes([e[12], e[13], e[14], e[15]]);
+            let end = offset.checked_add(bytes)?;
+            if end as usize > ico.len() {
+                return None;
+            }
+            out.push(IcoEntry {
+                width: if w == 0 { 256 } else { w },
+                height: if h == 0 { 256 } else { h },
+                offset,
+                bytes,
+            });
+        }
+        Some(out)
+    }
+
+    /// RT_ICON payload for the preferred square size (exact match, else the
+    /// closest fit, else the largest) — the bytes
+    /// `CreateIconFromResourceEx` wants (NOT the directory header).
+    pub(crate) fn ico_image_bytes(ico: &[u8], preferred: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {
+        let entries = ico_entries(ico)?;
+        let best = entries
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|e| e.width == e.height)
+            .min_by_key(|e| {
+                let d = e.width.abs_diff(preferred);
+                // Prefer >= preferred on ties (sharper downscale than up).
+                (d, if e.width < preferred { 1 } else { 0 })
+            })
+            .or_else(|| entries.iter().max_by_key(|e| e.width))?;
+        let s = best.offset as usize;
+        let e = s.checked_add(best.bytes as usize)?;
+        ico.get(s..e)
+    }
+
+    /// NUL-terminated UTF-16 for the FFI.
+    pub(crate) fn to_wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {
+        s.encode_utf16().chain(std::iter::once(0)).collect()
+    }
+
+    /// Tooltip as the fixed NOTIFYICONDATAW.szTip array (128 units, always
+    /// NUL-terminated; a surrogate pair that would straddle the terminator
+    /// is dropped whole — a lone lead surrogate is invalid UTF-16).
+    pub(crate) fn tip_array(s: &str) -> [u16; 128] {
+        let mut out = [0u16; 128];
+        let mut units = s.encode_utf16().peekable();
+        let mut i = 0;
+        while i < 127 {
+            let Some(u) = units.next() else { break };
+            if (0xD800..0xDC00).contains(&u) {
+                // Lead surrogate: place the pair only if BOTH units fit in
+                // the writable window (0..=126); the trail always follows
+                // from Rust's encoder.
+                if i + 1 < 127 {
+                    if let Some(t) = units.next() {
+                        out[i] = u;
+                        out[i + 1] = t;
+                        i += 2;
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                }
+                // Pair would straddle the terminator (or no trail — never
+                // from encode_utf16): drop it whole and stop.
+                break;
+            }
+            out[i] = u;
+            i += 1;
+        }
+        out
+    }
+}
+
+// ---- public spawn API ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+/// Spawn the tray (Windows) or report it unavailable (stub elsewhere).
+/// The tooltip/model are seeded so the icon is correct before the app's
+/// first tick lands.
+pub fn spawn(
+    initial_tooltip: String,
+    initial_model: Vec<QuickEntry>,
+) -> Option<(TrayHandle, tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<TrayEvent>)> {
+    crate::tray_win::spawn_impl(initial_tooltip, initial_model)
+}
+
+/// App-side handle: sends commands; joins on drop-free explicit shutdown.
+pub struct TrayHandle(pub(crate) crate::tray_win::HandleInner);
+
+impl TrayHandle {
+    pub fn send(&self, cmd: TrayCommand) {
+        self.0.send(cmd)
+    }
+
+    /// Best-effort teardown: asks the thread to exit and waits up to
+    /// `wait`; on timeout the thread is detached (the process is exiting
+    /// — the icon would be cleaned by Explorer on hover, but the ack
+    /// path makes that a non-issue in practice).
+    pub fn shutdown(self, wait: std::time::Duration) {
+        self.0.shutdown(wait)
+    }
+}
+
+// ---- tests (host: the pure model, ids, tooltip, ICO parse) -------------------
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::ffi_helpers::{ico_entries, ico_image_bytes, tip_array, ICON_BYTES, ICON_SIZE};
+    use super::*;
+
+    fn profile(id: &str, name: &str) -> ProfileView {
+        ProfileView {
+            id: id.to_string(),
+            tag: name.to_string(),
+            protocol: "vless".to_string(),
+            endpoint: "203.0.113.1:443".to_string(),
+            remark: String::new(),
+            active: false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn item_label(e: &QuickEntry) -> Option<&str> {
+        match e {
+            QuickEntry::Item { label, .. } => Some(label),
+            QuickEntry::Submenu { label, .. } => Some(label),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn menu_disconnected_shows_connect() {
+        let m = quick_menu(Some(ServiceState::Disconnected), &[], "");
+        assert_eq!(item_label(&m[2]), Some("Connect"));
+        assert_eq!(item_label(m.last().unwrap()), Some("Exit"));
+        let header = match &m[0] {
+            QuickEntry::Header(h) => h.clone(),
+            _ => panic!(),
+        };
+        assert_eq!(header, "MultiTunnel — disconnected");
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn menu_connected_shows_disconnect_and_servers() {
+        let profiles = vec![profile("a", "VM-1"), profile("b", "VM-2")];
+        let m = quick_menu(Some(ServiceState::Connected), &profiles, "VM-2");
+        assert_eq!(item_label(&m[2]), Some("Disconnect"));
+        let QuickEntry::Submenu { label, items } = &m[3] else {
+            panic!("expected server submenu");
+        };
+        assert_eq!(label, "Server");
+        // radio check on the ACTIVE profile only (matched by tag, like
+        // the GUI dropdown)
+        let checks: Vec<bool> = items
+            .iter()
+            .map(|e| matches!(e, QuickEntry::Item { checked: true, .. }))
+            .collect();
+        assert_eq!(checks, vec![false, true]);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn menu_transition_disables_the_toggle() {
+        let m = quick_menu(Some(ServiceState::Connecting), &[], "");
+        let QuickEntry::Item { enabled, .. } = &m[2] else {
+            panic!();
+        };
+        assert!(!enabled);
+        let m2 = quick_menu(Some(ServiceState::Connected), &[], "");
+        let QuickEntry::Item { enabled, .. } = &m2[2] else {
+            panic!();
+        };
+        assert!(enabled);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn menu_failed_is_disconnected_shape_with_honest_header() {
+        let m = quick_menu(Some(ServiceState::Failed), &[], "");
+        assert_eq!(item_label(&m[2]), Some("Connect"));
+        assert!(matches!(&m[0], QuickEntry::Header(h) if h.contains("failed")));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn ids_roundtrip_and_skip_zero() {
+        let profiles = vec![profile("a", "VM-1")];
+        let m = quick_menu(Some(ServiceState::Connected), &profiles, "VM-1");
+        let ids = assign_ids(&m);
+        assert!(ids.iter().all(|(i, _)| *i >= FIRST_ID));
+        // 1 = Disconnect, 2 = server "a", 3 = Open, 4 = Exit
+        assert_eq!(ids[0].1, QuickAction::Disconnect);
+        assert_eq!(ids[1].1, QuickAction::Server("a".into()));
+        assert_eq!(ids[2].1, QuickAction::Open);
+        assert_eq!(ids[3].1, QuickAction::Exit);
+        assert_eq!(action_for_id(&ids, 0), None);
+        assert_eq!(action_for_id(&ids, 999), None);
+        assert_eq!(action_for_id(&ids, 3), Some(QuickAction::Open));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn tooltip_states() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            tooltip(ServiceState::Connected, "VM-1"),
+            "MultiTunnel — connected [VM-1]"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            tooltip(ServiceState::Disconnected, ""),
+            "MultiTunnel — disconnected"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            tooltip(ServiceState::Connecting, ""),
+            "MultiTunnel — connecting…"
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn tip_array_never_overruns_or_splits_surrogates() {
+        let mut a = tip_array("");
+        assert_eq!(a[0], 0);
+        // A 200-unit string caps at 127 + NUL.
+        let long = "x".repeat(200);
+        a = tip_array(&long);
+        assert_eq!(a[126], b'x' as u16);
+        assert_eq!(a[127], 0);
+        // Surrogate pair at the boundary: the last unit must not be a lone
+        // lead surrogate — the encoder drops the pair, keeping a NUL.
+        let boundary = format!(
+            "{}{}", /* 126 ascii + 1 astral char */
+            "x".repeat(126),
+            "𝕏"
+        );
+        a = tip_array(&boundary);
+        let last = a[126];
+        assert!(last == 0 || !(0xD800..0xDC00).contains(&last));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn to_wide_is_nul_terminated() {
+        let w = super::ffi_helpers::to_wide("MultiTunnel");
+        assert_eq!(*w.last().unwrap(), 0);
+        assert_eq!(w.len(), "MultiTunnel".encode_utf16().count() + 1);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn ico_embedded_asset_parses_with_32_entry() {
+        let b = ico_image_bytes(ICON_BYTES, ICON_SIZE).expect("32px entry");
+        // BMP-format RT_ICON payload starts with a 40-byte BITMAPINFOHEADER
+        // whose biWidth == 32 and biHeight == 64 (XOR + AND masks).
+        assert!(b.len() > 40);
+        assert_eq!(u32::from_le_bytes(b[4..8].try_into().unwrap()), 32);
+        assert_eq!(u32::from_le_bytes(b[8..12].try_into().unwrap()), 64);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn ico_rejects_bad_directories() {
+        assert!(ico_entries(b"").is_none());
+        assert!(ico_entries(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]).is_none()); // count without entries
+                                                             // entry pointing past EOF
+        let mut bogus = vec![0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0];
+        bogus.extend_from_slice(&[32, 32, 0, 0, 1, 0, 32, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
+        assert!(ico_entries(&bogus).is_none());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn model_from_snapshot_states() {
+        // None status → disconnected, Connect offered.
+        let m = model_from(None, &[]);
+        assert_eq!(item_label(&m[2]), Some("Connect"));
+    }
+}
diff --git a/crates/mt-app/src/tray_win.rs b/crates/mt-app/src/tray_win.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..274460e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crates/mt-app/src/tray_win.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,641 @@
+//! The Windows half of the in-app tray (S15, D25) + the non-Windows stub.
+//! All FFI shapes are lifted from the S3-reviewed `src/tray.rs` (D4: raw
+//! Win32 via windows-sys, not the tray-icon crate) — see that module's
+//! docs for the full safety analysis; the SAFETY comments here mirror it.
+
+#[cfg(windows)]
+mod win {
+    use std::cell::RefCell;
+    use std::sync::mpsc::{Receiver, SyncSender};
+    use std::time::Duration;
+
+    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{HWND, LPARAM, LRESULT, POINT, WPARAM};
+    use windows_sys::Win32::UI::Shell::{
+        Shell_NotifyIconW, NIF_ICON, NIF_MESSAGE, NIF_TIP, NIM_ADD, NIM_DELETE, NIM_MODIFY,
+        NOTIFYICONDATAW,
+    };
+    use windows_sys::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{
+        AppendMenuW, CreateIconFromResourceEx, CreatePopupMenu, CreateWindowExW, DefWindowProcW,
+        DestroyIcon, DestroyMenu, DestroyWindow, DispatchMessageW, GetCursorPos, GetMessageW,
+        KillTimer, LoadIconW, PostMessageW, PostQuitMessage, RegisterWindowMessageW,
+        SetForegroundWindow, SetTimer, SetWindowLongPtrW, TrackPopupMenuEx, TranslateMessage,
+        GWLP_WNDPROC, HICON, HMENU, IDI_APPLICATION, LR_DEFAULTCOLOR, MF_CHECKED, MF_GRAYED,
+        MF_POPUP, MF_SEPARATOR, MF_STRING, MSG, TPM_BOTTOMALIGN, TPM_RIGHTBUTTON, WM_APP,
+        WM_COMMAND, WM_DESTROY, WM_LBUTTONUP, WM_NULL, WM_RBUTTONUP, WM_TIMER, WS_OVERLAPPED,
+    };
+
+    use crate::tray::ffi_helpers::{ico_image_bytes, tip_array, to_wide, ICON_BYTES, ICON_SIZE};
+    use crate::tray::{action_for_id, assign_ids, QuickAction, QuickEntry, TrayCommand, TrayEvent};
+
+    /// Tray icon id (NOTIFYICONDATAW.uID) — one icon per window.
+    const TRAY_ID: u32 = 1;
+    /// Callback message the shell sends for icon events.
+    const TRAY_CALLBACK: u32 = WM_APP + 1;
+    /// Command-poll timer id + period (the app's commands are rare; 50 ms
+    /// is imperceptible and keeps Exit teardown under ~100 ms).
+    const TIMER_ID: usize = 1;
+    const POLL_PERIOD_MS: u32 = 50;
+
+    /// Window/thread state. `ui` is only ever touched from the message-loop
+    /// thread (RefCell is enough — same as the legacy tray).
+    struct TrayCtx {
+        cmd_rx: Receiver<TrayCommand>,
+        event_tx: tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<TrayEvent>,
+        ui: RefCell<UiState>,
+    }
+
+    struct UiState {
+        hwnd: HWND,
+        icon: HICON,
+        /// True only when `icon` came from `CreateIconFromResourceEx` (must
+        /// then be `DestroyIcon`d). A `LoadIconW` fallback is a SHARED
+        /// system icon — never destroyed.
+        icon_owned: bool,
+        icon_added: bool,
+        /// Registered "TaskbarCreated" id (0 = registration failed).
+        taskbar_msg: u32,
+        last_tip: String,
+        /// Current Quick Settings model + its flat id map.
+        model: Vec<QuickEntry>,
+        ids: Vec<(u16, QuickAction)>,
+    }
+
+    thread_local! {
+        static CTX: RefCell<Option<&'static TrayCtx>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
+    }
+
+    fn ctx() -> Option<&'static TrayCtx> {
+        CTX.with(|c| *c.borrow())
+    }
+
+    fn log_err(op: &str) {
+        tracing::warn!("tray: {op} failed: {}", std::io::Error::last_os_error());
+    }
+
+    /// The message loop thread body: create window → add icon → pump until
+    /// WM_QUIT → teardown. Errors before the loop turn into a `None`
+    /// (reported by the caller as "tray unavailable").
+    pub(crate) fn spawn_impl(
+        initial_tooltip: String,
+        initial_model: Vec<QuickEntry>,
+    ) -> Option<(
+        crate::tray::TrayHandle,
+        tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<TrayEvent>,
+    )> {
+        let (cmd_tx, cmd_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel(64);
+        let (event_tx, event_rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel();
+        let (ready_tx, ready_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel(1);
+        // Wake the parent even if the thread panics before signaling.
+        let _guard = DropSend(Some(ready_tx.clone()));
+        let initial_ids = assign_ids(&initial_model);
+        // TrayCtx (RefCell UI state + the command Receiver) is created ON
+        // the tray thread and leaked there — it never crosses a thread
+        // boundary (no Sync needed); the parent only holds the channels.
+        let thread = std::thread::Builder::new()
+            .name("mt-tray".into())
+            .spawn(move || {
+                let ctx: &'static TrayCtx = Box::leak(Box::new(TrayCtx {
+                    cmd_rx,
+                    event_tx,
+                    ui: RefCell::new(UiState {
+                        hwnd: std::ptr::null_mut(),
+                        icon: std::ptr::null_mut(),
+                        icon_owned: false,
+                        icon_added: false,
+                        taskbar_msg: 0,
+                        last_tip: initial_tooltip,
+                        model: initial_model,
+                        ids: initial_ids,
+                    }),
+                }));
+                run(ctx, ready_tx)
+            });
+        match thread {
+            Ok(handle) => {
+                let ok = ready_rx.recv().unwrap_or(false);
+                if ok {
+                    HANDLE_SLOT.with(|s| *s.borrow_mut() = Some(handle));
+                    Some((crate::tray::TrayHandle(HandleInner { cmd_tx }), event_rx))
+                } else {
+                    tracing::warn!("tray unavailable: init failed");
+                    None
+                }
+            }
+            Err(e) => {
+                tracing::warn!("tray unavailable: spawn mt-tray: {e}");
+                None
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Wake the parent even if the thread panics before signaling: sends
+    /// `false` on drop when the sender was not used.
+    struct DropSend(Option<SyncSender<bool>>);
+
+    impl Drop for DropSend {
+        fn drop(&mut self) {
+            if let Some(tx) = self.0.take() {
+                let _ = tx.try_send(false);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    thread_local! {
+        /// The tray thread's JoinHandle, held for `HandleInner::shutdown`.
+        static HANDLE_SLOT: RefCell<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>> =
+            const { RefCell::new(None) };
+    }
+
+    /// The app-facing half (the public wrapper lives in tray.rs).
+    pub(crate) struct HandleInner {
+        cmd_tx: SyncSender<TrayCommand>,
+    }
+    impl HandleInner {
+        pub(crate) fn send(&self, cmd: TrayCommand) {
+            use std::sync::mpsc::TrySendError;
+            // Full channel = the tray is wedged; dropping the command is
+            // the honest degradation (the app keeps running).
+            match self.cmd_tx.try_send(cmd) {
+                Ok(()) | Err(TrySendError::Full(_)) => {}
+                Err(TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => {
+                    tracing::warn!("tray: command channel closed (thread gone)");
+                }
+            }
+        }
+
+        pub(crate) fn shutdown(self, wait: Duration) {
+            let (ack_tx, ack_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel(1);
+            self.cmd_tx.try_send(TrayCommand::Shutdown(ack_tx)).ok();
+            if ack_rx.recv_timeout(wait).is_err() {
+                tracing::warn!("tray: teardown ack timeout — detaching thread");
+            }
+            // Join best-effort (the ack usually means the loop already
+            // exited; joining reaps the thread's resources).
+            HANDLE_SLOT.with(|s| {
+                if let Some(h) = s.borrow_mut().take() {
+                    let _ = h.join();
+                }
+            });
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn run(ctx: &'static TrayCtx, ready: SyncSender<bool>) {
+        // Window + icon first; failures go to the parent, and the thread
+        // ends without a message loop.
+        let hwnd = match create_window() {
+            Ok(h) => h,
+            Err(e) => {
+                tracing::warn!("tray: {e}");
+                let _ = ready.send(false);
+                return;
+            }
+        };
+        CTX.with(|c| *c.borrow_mut() = Some(ctx));
+        {
+            let mut ui = ctx.ui.borrow_mut();
+            ui.hwnd = hwnd;
+            let (icon, owned) = load_tray_icon();
+            ui.icon = icon;
+            ui.icon_owned = owned;
+            let tip = ui.last_tip.clone();
+            drop(ui);
+            if add_tray_icon(hwnd, icon, &tip).is_err() {
+                // SAFETY: hwnd was created on this thread.
+                unsafe { DestroyWindow(hwnd) };
+                CTX.with(|c| *c.borrow_mut() = None);
+                tracing::warn!("tray: Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_ADD) failed");
+                let _ = ready.send(false);
+                return;
+            }
+            ctx.ui.borrow_mut().icon_added = true;
+        }
+        {
+            let mut ui = ctx.ui.borrow_mut();
+            // SAFETY: registering a message by name never fails critically;
+            // id 0 just disables the explorer-restart recovery.
+            ui.taskbar_msg = unsafe { RegisterWindowMessageW(to_wide("TaskbarCreated").as_ptr()) };
+            // SAFETY: our own window + timer id; 50 ms period.
+            unsafe { SetTimer(hwnd, TIMER_ID, POLL_PERIOD_MS, None) };
+        }
+        if ready.send(true).is_err() {
+            // Parent went away before the ack: tear back down.
+            teardown(ctx, hwnd);
+            return;
+        }
+
+        // Classic pump; WM_QUIT arrives from WM_DESTROY (window died) or
+        // the Shutdown command.
+        let mut msg = MSG {
+            hwnd: std::ptr::null_mut(),
+            message: 0,
+            wParam: 0,
+            lParam: 0,
+            time: 0,
+            pt: POINT { x: 0, y: 0 },
+        };
+        loop {
+            // SAFETY: msg is a writable, aligned out-slot; the pump only
+            // runs on this thread (the procedure was installed on it).
+            let r = unsafe { GetMessageW(&mut msg, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, 0) };
+            if r <= 0 {
+                break;
+            }
+            // SAFETY: passthrough of a retrieved message.
+            unsafe { TranslateMessage(&msg) };
+            // SAFETY: passthrough of a translated message.
+            unsafe { DispatchMessageW(&msg) };
+        }
+        teardown(ctx, hwnd);
+    }
+
+    /// Final teardown: timer off, icon off, icon handle freed, window
+    /// gone (WM_DESTROY already quit the loop).
+    fn teardown(ctx: &'static TrayCtx, hwnd: HWND) {
+        // SAFETY: our own timer.
+        unsafe { KillTimer(hwnd, TIMER_ID) };
+        {
+            let mut ui = ctx.ui.borrow_mut();
+            if ui.icon_added && !hwnd.is_null() {
+                let d = nid_base(hwnd);
+                // SAFETY: d carries the icon identity; NIM_DELETE removes it.
+                let _ = unsafe { Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_DELETE, &d) };
+            }
+            if ui.icon_owned && !ui.icon.is_null() {
+                // SAFETY: icon came from CreateIconFromResourceEx.
+                unsafe { DestroyIcon(ui.icon) };
+            }
+            ui.icon_added = false;
+            ui.icon = std::ptr::null_mut();
+        }
+    }
+
+    // ---- icon / window ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+    fn load_tray_icon() -> (HICON, bool) {
+        if let Some(bytes) = ico_image_bytes(ICON_BYTES, ICON_SIZE) {
+            // SAFETY: bytes points into our read-only embedded ICO data
+            // with exactly the length from the directory entry; 0x00030000
+            // is the documented icon-resource version; fIcon=1.
+            let icon = unsafe {
+                CreateIconFromResourceEx(
+                    bytes.as_ptr(),
+                    bytes.len() as u32,
+                    1,
+                    0x0003_0000,
+                    ICON_SIZE as i32,
+                    ICON_SIZE as i32,
+                    LR_DEFAULTCOLOR,
+                )
+            };
+            if !icon.is_null() {
+                return (icon, true);
+            }
+        }
+        // SAFETY: IDI_APPLICATION is a system resource id; LoadIconW
+        // returns a SHARED icon (never destroyed — owned=false).
+        (
+            unsafe { LoadIconW(std::ptr::null_mut(), IDI_APPLICATION) },
+            false,
+        )
+    }
+
+    /// Hidden TOP-LEVEL STATIC window, subclassed with our procedure (see
+    /// the legacy tray's S3-REV-B P1 analysis: top-level, NOT message-only
+    /// — TaskbarCreated must reach it and SetForegroundWindow must be able
+    /// to activate it for menu dismissal).
+    fn create_window() -> Result<HWND, String> {
+        let class = to_wide("STATIC");
+        let title = to_wide("MultiTunnelAppTray");
+        // SAFETY: hidden top-level window from the predefined STATIC
+        // system class; WS_OVERLAPPED without WS_VISIBLE = never shown;
+        // both wide strings are NUL-terminated buffers we own.
+        let hwnd = unsafe {
+            CreateWindowExW(
+                0,
+                class.as_ptr(),
+                title.as_ptr(),
+                WS_OVERLAPPED,
+                0,
+                0,
+                0,
+                0,
+                std::ptr::null_mut(),
+                std::ptr::null_mut(),
+                std::ptr::null_mut(),
+                std::ptr::null(),
+            )
+        };
+        if hwnd.is_null() {
+            return Err(format!(
+                "CreateWindowExW(tray) failed: {}",
+                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
+            ));
+        }
+        // SAFETY: the fn-pointer→integer cast is the documented Win32
+        // idiom for GWLP_WNDPROC.
+        let prev = unsafe {
+            SetWindowLongPtrW(hwnd, GWLP_WNDPROC, wndproc as *const () as usize as isize)
+        };
+        if prev == 0 {
+            let e = format!(
+                "SetWindowLongPtrW(GWLP_WNDPROC) failed: {}",
+                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
+            );
+            // SAFETY: hwnd was created on this thread.
+            unsafe { DestroyWindow(hwnd) };
+            return Err(e);
+        }
+        Ok(hwnd)
+    }
+
+    // ---- window procedure ------------------------------------------------------
+
+    unsafe extern "system" fn wndproc(
+        hwnd: HWND,
+        msg: u32,
+        wparam: WPARAM,
+        lparam: LPARAM,
+    ) -> LRESULT {
+        if let Some(ctx) = ctx() {
+            let taskbar_msg = ctx.ui.borrow().taskbar_msg;
+            if taskbar_msg != 0 && msg == taskbar_msg {
+                on_taskbar_created(ctx, hwnd);
+                return 0;
+            }
+        }
+        match msg {
+            WM_TIMER if wparam == TIMER_ID => {
+                if let Some(ctx) = ctx() {
+                    on_timer(ctx, hwnd);
+                }
+                0
+            }
+            WM_COMMAND => {
+                let id = (wparam & 0xFFFF) as u16;
+                if let Some(ctx) = ctx() {
+                    let action = {
+                        let ui = ctx.ui.borrow();
+                        action_for_id(&ui.ids, id)
+                    };
+                    if let Some(a) = action {
+                        let _ = ctx.event_tx.send((&a).into());
+                    }
+                }
+                0
+            }
+            WM_DESTROY => {
+                // SAFETY: posts WM_QUIT to this thread's loop.
+                unsafe { PostQuitMessage(0) };
+                0
+            }
+            TRAY_CALLBACK => match lparam as u32 {
+                WM_LBUTTONUP => {
+                    if let Some(ctx) = ctx() {
+                        let _ = ctx.event_tx.send(TrayEvent::Open);
+                    }
+                    0
+                }
+                WM_RBUTTONUP => {
+                    if let Some(ctx) = ctx() {
+                        show_menu(ctx, hwnd);
+                    }
+                    0
+                }
+                _ => {
+                    // SAFETY: passthrough.
+                    unsafe { DefWindowProcW(hwnd, msg, wparam, lparam) }
+                }
+            },
+            _ => {
+                // SAFETY: passthrough.
+                unsafe { DefWindowProcW(hwnd, msg, wparam, lparam) }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // ---- handlers ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    /// Explorer restarted: re-add the SAME icon identity.
+    fn on_taskbar_created(ctx: &'static TrayCtx, hwnd: HWND) {
+        let (icon, added, tip) = {
+            let ui = ctx.ui.borrow();
+            (ui.icon, ui.icon_added, ui.last_tip.clone())
+        };
+        if !added || icon.is_null() {
+            return;
+        }
+        if add_tray_icon(hwnd, icon, &tip).is_err() {
+            log_err("Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_ADD after TaskbarCreated)");
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Poll the command channel (rare) + refresh the tooltip when the app
+    /// sent a new one.
+    fn on_timer(ctx: &'static TrayCtx, hwnd: HWND) {
+        while let Ok(cmd) = ctx.cmd_rx.try_recv() {
+            match cmd {
+                TrayCommand::Tooltip(tip) => {
+                    let changed = {
+                        let mut ui = ctx.ui.borrow_mut();
+                        if ui.last_tip == tip {
+                            false
+                        } else {
+                            ui.last_tip = tip.clone();
+                            true
+                        }
+                    };
+                    if changed {
+                        let mut d = nid_base(hwnd);
+                        d.uFlags = NIF_TIP;
+                        d.szTip = tip_array(&tip);
+                        // SAFETY: NIM_MODIFY only reads d; a missing
+                        // icon just returns FALSE.
+                        let _ = unsafe { Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_MODIFY, &d) };
+                    }
+                }
+                TrayCommand::Model(model) => {
+                    let ids = assign_ids(&model);
+                    let mut ui = ctx.ui.borrow_mut();
+                    ui.model = model;
+                    ui.ids = ids;
+                }
+                TrayCommand::Shutdown(ack) => {
+                    // Stop the icon first (best effort), ack, then let
+                    // WM_DESTROY quit the loop.
+                    {
+                        let ui = ctx.ui.borrow();
+                        if ui.icon_added && !hwnd.is_null() {
+                            let d = nid_base(hwnd);
+                            // SAFETY: icon identity; NIM_DELETE.
+                            let _ = unsafe { Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_DELETE, &d) };
+                        }
+                    }
+                    ctx.ui.borrow_mut().icon_added = false;
+                    let _ = ack.send(());
+                    // SAFETY: our own window; WM_DESTROY → PostQuitMessage.
+                    unsafe { DestroyWindow(hwnd) };
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn show_menu(ctx: &'static TrayCtx, hwnd: HWND) {
+        let model = ctx.ui.borrow().model.clone();
+        // SAFETY: fresh popup menu owned by this thread.
+        let hmenu = unsafe { CreatePopupMenu() };
+        if hmenu.is_null() {
+            log_err("CreatePopupMenu");
+            return;
+        }
+        // Ids are handed out in the same depth-first walk order as
+        // `assign_ids` (items only), so WM_COMMAND lookups agree.
+        let mut next_id: u16 = crate::tray::FIRST_ID;
+        append_entries(hmenu, &model, &mut next_id);
+        let mut pt = POINT { x: 0, y: 0 };
+        // SAFETY: pt is a writable out-slot.
+        let have_pos = unsafe { GetCursorPos(&mut pt) } != 0;
+        if have_pos {
+            // SAFETY: hwnd is our (foreground-able, top-level) window.
+            let _ = unsafe { SetForegroundWindow(hwnd) };
+        }
+        // SAFETY: hmenu valid; modal loop re-enters the procedure safely
+        // (no borrow guard is held here).
+        let _ = unsafe {
+            TrackPopupMenuEx(
+                hmenu,
+                TPM_RIGHTBUTTON | TPM_BOTTOMALIGN,
+                pt.x,
+                pt.y,
+                hwnd,
+                std::ptr::null(),
+            )
+        };
+        if have_pos {
+            // SAFETY: WM_NULL is the documented post-menu no-op (KB
+            // Q135788 second half).
+            let _ = unsafe { PostMessageW(hwnd, WM_NULL, 0, 0) };
+        }
+        // SAFETY: destroys the menu we created.
+        unsafe { DestroyMenu(hmenu) };
+    }
+
+    /// Append model entries; `next_id` is consumed in the same depth-first
+    /// order as [`crate::tray::assign_ids`], keeping menu ids and the
+    /// stored id map in lockstep.
+    fn append_entries(hmenu: HMENU, entries: &[QuickEntry], next_id: &mut u16) {
+        for e in entries {
+            let ok = match e {
+                QuickEntry::Separator => {
+                    // SAFETY: MF_SEPARATOR requires a NULL lpNewItem.
+                    unsafe { AppendMenuW(hmenu, MF_SEPARATOR, 0, std::ptr::null()) }
+                }
+                QuickEntry::Header(label) => {
+                    let wide = to_wide(label);
+                    // SAFETY: grayed rows are unselectable (id 0 unused).
+                    unsafe { AppendMenuW(hmenu, MF_STRING | MF_GRAYED, 0, wide.as_ptr()) }
+                }
+                QuickEntry::Item {
+                    label,
+                    enabled,
+                    checked,
+                    ..
+                } => {
+                    let id = *next_id;
+                    *next_id = next_id.wrapping_add(1);
+                    let wide = to_wide(label);
+                    let mut flags = MF_STRING;
+                    if !enabled {
+                        flags |= MF_GRAYED;
+                    }
+                    if *checked {
+                        flags |= MF_CHECKED;
+                    }
+                    // SAFETY: id maps back through action_for_id on
+                    // WM_COMMAND.
+                    unsafe { AppendMenuW(hmenu, flags, id as usize, wide.as_ptr()) }
+                }
+                QuickEntry::Submenu { label, items } => {
+                    // SAFETY: fresh popup owned by this thread.
+                    let sub = unsafe { CreatePopupMenu() };
+                    if sub.is_null() {
+                        log_err("CreatePopupMenu(submenu)");
+                        continue;
+                    }
+                    append_entries(sub, items, next_id);
+                    let wide = to_wide(label);
+                    // SAFETY: sub is a valid menu; MF_POPUP makes the id
+                    // parameter the submenu HANDLE.
+                    let ok = unsafe { AppendMenuW(hmenu, MF_POPUP, sub as usize, wide.as_ptr()) };
+                    if ok == 0 {
+                        log_err("AppendMenuW(submenu)");
+                        // SAFETY: not attached — destroy to avoid a leak.
+                        unsafe { DestroyMenu(sub) };
+                    }
+                    continue;
+                }
+            };
+            if ok == 0 {
+                log_err("AppendMenuW");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // ---- Shell_NotifyIconW glue ---------------------------------------------------
+
+    fn nid_base(hwnd: HWND) -> NOTIFYICONDATAW {
+        NOTIFYICONDATAW {
+            cbSize: std::mem::size_of::<NOTIFYICONDATAW>() as u32,
+            hWnd: hwnd,
+            uID: TRAY_ID,
+            ..Default::default()
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn add_tray_icon(hwnd: HWND, icon: HICON, tip: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
+        let mut d = nid_base(hwnd);
+        d.uFlags = NIF_MESSAGE | NIF_ICON | NIF_TIP;
+        d.uCallbackMessage = TRAY_CALLBACK;
+        d.hIcon = icon;
+        d.szTip = tip_array(tip);
+        // SAFETY: d fully initialized for NIM_ADD.
+        if unsafe { Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_ADD, &d) } != 0 {
+            Ok(())
+        } else {
+            Err(format!(
+                "Shell_NotifyIconW(NIM_ADD) failed: {}",
+                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
+            ))
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(windows)]
+pub(crate) use win::{spawn_impl, HandleInner};
+
+#[cfg(not(windows))]
+mod stub {
+    use crate::tray::{QuickEntry, TrayCommand, TrayEvent};
+
+    /// Non-Windows: no tray (the app keeps working; close-to-tray
+    /// degrades to minimize — see D25 §3).
+    pub fn spawn_impl(
+        _initial_tooltip: String,
+        _initial_model: Vec<QuickEntry>,
+    ) -> Option<(
+        crate::tray::TrayHandle,
+        tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<TrayEvent>,
+    )> {
+        tracing::info!("tray: not available on this platform (Windows only)");
+        None
+    }
+
+    pub struct HandleInner;
+
+    impl HandleInner {
+        pub fn send(&self, _cmd: TrayCommand) {}
+        pub fn shutdown(self, _wait: std::time::Duration) {}
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(not(windows))]
+pub(crate) use stub::{spawn_impl, HandleInner};

+#[cfg(test)]
+mod close_to_tray_migration_tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    /// S15: settings.json written by v0.7/v0.8 (no `close_to_tray` key)
+    /// loads with close_to_tray = false — the serde-default migration
+    /// (D8 version-free, D20 precedent), so the toggle starts honest.
+    #[test]
+    fn old_settings_without_close_to_tray_default_off() {
+        let json = r#"{
+            "theme_seed": 42,
+            "dark_mode": false,
+            "system_proxy": true,
+            "merge_policy": "balanced",
+            "autostart": false,
+            "bonded_adapters": ["wifi"],
+            "bond_mode": "per-connection",
+            "merge_port": 7443,
+            "socks_port": 10808,
+            "http_port": 10809,
+            "allow_lan": false,
+            "log_level": "info",
+            "probe_target": "connectivitycheck.gstatic.com:80",
+            "exit_probe_url": "http://ip-api.com/json"
+        }"#;
+        let v: SettingsView = serde_json::from_str(json).expect("old settings load");
+        assert!(!v.close_to_tray);
+        assert_eq!(v.merge_policy, "balanced", "unrelated fields intact");
+    }
+
+    /// The round trip: a file written by S15 reads back the same value.
+    #[test]
+    fn close_to_tray_roundtrips() {
+        let mut v = SettingsView::default_settings_for_tests();
+        v.close_to_tray = true;
+        let json = serde_json::to_string(&v).expect("serialize");
+        assert!(json.contains("\"close_to_tray\":true"));
+        let back: SettingsView = serde_json::from_str(&json).expect("reload");
+        assert!(back.close_to_tray);
+    }
+
+    impl SettingsView {
+        fn default_settings_for_tests() -> Self {
+            Self {
+                theme_seed: 0,
+                dark_mode: false,
+                system_proxy: false,
+                merge_policy: "balanced".into(),
+                autostart: false,
+                bonded_adapters: vec![],
+                bond_mode: "per-connection".into(),
+                merge_port: 7443,
+                socks_port: 10808,
+                http_port: 10809,
+                allow_lan: false,
+                log_level: "info".into(),
+                probe_target: String::new(),
+                exit_probe_url: String::new(),
+                close_to_tray: false,
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}

+## D25 — S15: in-app tray + Chromium-style title bar + the user's logo (2026-11-20)
+
+User asks (task E UI half): use the attached image as the logo; title bar
+blends with the window like Chromium; toggleable close-to-tray; a
+persistent tray icon while the app is open or minimized; Quick Settings
+on tray right-click.
+
+1. LOGO PIPELINE (assets, all runtime — no exe resource embedding):
+   `scripts/make_logo_assets.py` (stdlib-only; deterministic) decodes the
+   user's PNG (zlib + unfilter, no image crate) and emits:
+   `assets/logo.png` (verbatim source, ~197 KB), `assets/logo_24.rgba`
+   (titlebar emblem, 24x24), `assets/logo_64.rgba` (window icon 64x64 —
+   iced `window::Settings::icon` via `Icon::from_rgba`), and regenerates
+   `assets/icon.ico` (BMP-format entries 16/32/48 = emblem crop, 256 =
+   full lockup — small sizes use the emblem so the mark stays legible;
+   the legacy `src/tray.rs` ICO parser and the new mt-app tray both
+   consume it). The window/taskbar icon is set at RUNTIME (Settings::icon
+   + WM_SETICON) — Explorer's .exe file icon stays default (a resource
+   object would need windres/llvm-rc, neither cross-compiles in the
+   sandbox; D4-style hand-rolled COFF .rsrc deferred until asked).
+2. TITLE BAR: `decorations: false` + an in-app strip ABOVE the nav rail
+   (emblem + "MultiTunnel" + drag area + – □ × buttons) on the SAME
+   surface color as the page (the Chromium blend). Drag = `window::drag`
+   on press; double-click-to-maximize = time-based (450 ms) second-press
+   detect (mouse_area has no double-click in iced 0.13.4); maximize glyph
+   state via `window::get_maximized`; min/max/close via window Tasks.
+3. CLOSE-TO-TRAY: `exit_on_close_request: false` ALWAYS (the app owns
+   both paths); `close_to_tray: bool` settings field (serde default
+   false — version-free migration, D8/D20 precedent). CloseRequested
+   with close_to_tray: Windows + tray alive → hide via
+   `window::run_with_handle` (HWND → ShowWindow SW_HIDE); non-Windows →
+   minimize + log line (honest fallback; a hidden window with NO tray on
+   Linux would be unreachable). Without close_to_tray → `window::close`.
+   iced 0.13 has NO hide Action — RunWithHandle is the escape hatch (no
+   vendored patch needed).
+4. IN-APP TRAY (mt-app/src/tray.rs, cfg(windows), raw Win32 per D4 —
+   the S3 patterns reused: hidden top-level STATIC window subclassed via
+   GWLP_WNDPROC (NOT message-only — TaskbarCreated must reach it),
+   Shell_NotifyIconW, TrackPopupMenuEx with TPM_RETURNCMD +
+   SetForegroundWindow, icon from the embedded ICO, TaskbarCreated
+   re-add): dedicated thread + 50 ms WM_TIMER command poll; commands
+   (tooltip/model/shutdown) via std mpsc IN, events via tokio mpsc OUT
+   (bridged into iced by the existing EVENTS_SUB_ID-style stream
+   subscription). Left click = open window; right click = menu; the
+   tray spawns in App::init (both mock and real backends — run_app is
+   shared with `multitunnel gui`), tears down (NIM_DELETE + bounded
+   join) on every real exit path. Non-Windows: stub (None) — the Linux
+   GUI keeps working, covered by the rig; the win32 half is covered by
+   windows clippy + zigbuild + the S3-proven FFI shapes.
+5. QUICK SETTINGS MENU = the tray right-click menu, built FRESH from a
+   pure, host-tested model (menu_model: Vec of items with id/label/
+   checked/disabled + submenu): Connect/Disconnect (state-reflecting),
+   Server → radio list of profiles, Open MultiTunnel, Exit. Selections
+   ride TrayEvent → existing Message paths (ConnectToggle/SetActive) —
+   no new service calls. Tooltip: "MultiTunnel — <state> [<profile>]",
+   refreshed on tick only when changed.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/gui_drive.py
@@ -0,0 +1,250 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gui_drive.py — one-shot Xvfb GUI drive rig (S10/S13/S15).
+
+Usage:
+    python3 scripts/gui_drive.py <binary> <out_dir> <screen_WxH> <sf> <verbs...>
+
+Verbs (comma-separated list, executed in order):
+    wait:<sec>            sleep
+    shot:<name>           screenshot to <out_dir>/<name>.png (ffmpeg x11grab)
+    click:<x>,<y>         XTEST button-1 press+release at LOGICAL coords
+    dclick:<x>,<y>        two clicks 60 ms apart
+    type:<text>           XTEST typed ASCII (keymap-level shift handling)
+    key:<keysym>          XTEST single keysym (e.g. Return, Escape)
+    scroll:<x>,<y>        one XTEST wheel-down (button 5) at coords
+                          (append ",up" for button 4, ",N" to repeat)
+    resize:<W>x<H>        XConfigureWindow on the app window (no WM runs)
+    alive                 assert the app process is still alive (exit 4 if not)
+    gone                  assert the app process EXITED (exit 5 if not)
+
+Exit 0 = all verbs done + the alive/gone assertions passed. Everything is
+one-shot: the whole process tree (Xvfb, app, ffmpeg) is torn down at the
+end (the sandbox kills daemons between tool calls anyway).
+"""
+
+import os
+import shutil
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+
+sys.path.insert(0, "/home/z/my-project/tools/pypkgs-xlib")
+
+XKBLIBS = "/tmp/xkblibs/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu"
+DISPLAY = ":99"
+
+KEYSYM_NAMES = {
+    "Return": 0xFF0D,
+    "Escape": 0xFF1B,
+    "BackSpace": 0xFF08,
+    "Tab": 0xFF09,
+    "space": 0x20,
+}
+
+SHIFTED = {
+    "~": "`", "!": "1", "@": "2", "#": "3", "$": "4", "%": "5", "^": "6",
+    "&": "7", "*": "8", "(": "9", ")": "0", "_": "-", "+": "=",
+    "{": "[", "}": "]", ":": ";", '"': "'", "<": ",", ">": ".", "?": "/",
+    "|": "\\",
+}
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    binary, out_dir, screen, sf, verbs = (
+        sys.argv[1],
+        sys.argv[2],
+        sys.argv[3],
+        sys.argv[4],
+        sys.argv[5:],
+    )
+    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/.X11-unix/X99", ignore_errors=True)
+
+    xvfb = subprocess.Popen(
+        ["Xvfb", DISPLAY, "-screen", "0", f"{screen}x24", "-nolisten", "tcp"],
+        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+    )
+    time.sleep(1.2)
+
+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    env["DISPLAY"] = DISPLAY
+    env["LD_LIBRARY_PATH"] = XKBLIBS
+    env["WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR"] = sf
+    env["RUST_LOG"] = "info"
+    app = subprocess.Popen(
+        [binary], env=env, stdout=open(f"{out_dir}/app.log", "w"),
+        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+    )
+    time.sleep(3.0)
+
+    # XTEST driver -----------------------------------------------------------
+    from Xlib import X, display as xdisplay
+    from Xlib.ext import xtest
+
+    d = xdisplay.Display(DISPLAY)
+    root = d.screen().root
+
+    def find_app_window():
+        """The REAL app window: winit also creates an UNMAPPED helper
+        window ('winit window') under Xvfb — SetInputFocus on an unviewable
+        window is a BadMatch protocol error. Match by WM_NAME + viewable."""
+        best = None
+        for child in root.query_tree().children:
+            try:
+                name = child.get_wm_name() or ""
+                viewable = child.get_attributes().map_state == X.IsViewable
+            except Exception:
+                continue
+            if viewable and ("MultiTunnel" in name or name):
+                best = child
+                if "MultiTunnel" in name:
+                    return child
+        return best
+
+    app_win = find_app_window()
+
+    def focus():
+        nonlocal app_win
+        if app_win is None:
+            app_win = find_app_window()
+        if app_win is not None:
+            app_win.configure(stack_mode=X.Above)
+            # explicit input focus (no WM under Xvfb — never granted
+            # otherwise)
+            d.set_input_focus(app_win, X.RevertToPointerRoot, X.CurrentTime)
+        d.flush()
+
+    def click(x, y):
+        xtest.fake_input(d, X.MotionNotify, x=int(x), y=int(y))
+        d.flush()
+        time.sleep(0.05)
+        xtest.fake_input(d, X.ButtonPress, 1)
+        d.sync()
+        time.sleep(0.06)
+        xtest.fake_input(d, X.ButtonRelease, 1)
+        d.sync()
+        time.sleep(0.15)
+
+    def key(code, press):
+        xtest.fake_input(d, X.KeyPress if press else X.KeyRelease, code)
+        d.sync()
+
+    def type_text(t):
+        for ch in t:
+            base, shifted = ch, False
+            if ch.isupper():
+                base, shifted = ch.lower(), True
+            elif ch in SHIFTED:
+                base, shifted = SHIFTED[ch], True
+            code = d.keysym_to_keycode(ord(base))
+            if shifted:
+                shift_code = d.keysym_to_keycode(0xFFE1)
+                key(shift_code, True)
+            key(code, True)
+            time.sleep(0.02)
+            key(code, False)
+            if shifted:
+                key(shift_code, False)
+            time.sleep(0.03)
+
+    def press_named(name):
+        code = d.keysym_to_keycode(
+            KEYSYM_NAMES.get(name, ord(name) if len(name) == 1 else 0xFF1B)
+        )
+        key(code, True)
+        time.sleep(0.02)
+        key(code, False)
+
+    def shot(name):
+        w, h = screen.split("x")
+        subprocess.run(
+            [
+                "ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-f", "x11grab",
+                "-video_size", f"{w}x{h}", "-i", DISPLAY, "-frames:v", "1",
+                f"{out_dir}/{name}.png",
+            ],
+            check=False,
+        )
+
+    def scroll(x, y, up=False, n=1):
+        # XTEST wheel needs generous timings under Xvfb: a 0.2 s settle
+        # after the warp, 80 ms hold, 200 ms between clicks (fast
+        # press/release pairs get coalesced and lost).
+        xtest.fake_input(d, X.MotionNotify, x=int(x), y=int(y))
+        d.flush()
+        time.sleep(0.2)
+        for _ in range(n):
+            xtest.fake_input(d, X.ButtonPress, 4 if up else 5)
+            d.sync()
+            time.sleep(0.08)
+            xtest.fake_input(d, X.ButtonRelease, 4 if up else 5)
+            d.sync()
+            time.sleep(0.2)
+
+    code = 0
+    try:
+        focus()
+        for v in verbs:
+            op, _, arg = v.partition(":")
+            if op == "wait":
+                time.sleep(float(arg))
+            elif op == "shot":
+                shot(arg)
+            elif op == "click":
+                x, y = arg.split(",")
+                focus()
+                click(int(x), int(y))
+            elif op == "dclick":
+                x, y = arg.split(",")
+                focus()
+                click(int(x), int(y))
+                click(int(x), int(y))
+            elif op == "type":
+                focus()
+                type_text(arg)
+            elif op == "key":
+                focus()
+                press_named(arg)
+            elif op == "scroll":
+                parts = arg.split(",")
+                up = len(parts) > 2 and parts[2] == "up"
+                n = int(parts[3]) if len(parts) > 3 else 1
+                focus()
+                scroll(int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), up, n)
+            elif op == "resize":
+                if app_win is not None:
+                    w, h = arg.split("x")
+                    app_win.configure(width=int(w), height=int(h))
+                    d.flush()
+                    time.sleep(0.6)
+                    focus()
+            elif op == "alive":
+                if app.poll() is not None:
+                    print(f"ALIVE-ASSERT-FAILED rc={app.returncode}")
+                    code = 4
+            elif op == "gone":
+                for _ in range(40):
+                    if app.poll() is not None:
+                        break
+                    time.sleep(0.25)
+                if app.poll() is None:
+                    print("GONE-ASSERT-FAILED still running")
+                    code = 5
+            elif op == "focus":
+                focus()
+    finally:
+        time.sleep(0.4)
+        for p in (app, xvfb):
+            if p.poll() is None:
+                p.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
+        time.sleep(0.6)
+        for p in (app, xvfb):
+            if p.poll() is None:
+                p.kill()
+    return code
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
diff --git a/scripts/make_logo_assets.py b/scripts/make_logo_assets.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cb8f2f3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/make_logo_assets.py
@@ -0,0 +1,338 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Generate the MultiTunnel logo assets from the user's source image.
+
+The source (assets/logo.png, kept verbatim) is the logo the user attached:
+an emblem (a mark) above a wordmark, drawn on a uniform light-blue canvas.
+This script decodes it with the stdlib only (zlib + per-scanline unfilter
+— the repo carries no image crate), splits the two segments, and emits:
+
+    assets/logo.png     verbatim copy of the source (reference/repro)
+    assets/logo_24.rgba titlebar emblem, 24x24 RGBA8 (iced image Handle)
+    assets/logo_64.rgba window icon,    64x64 RGBA8 (window::Settings icon)
+    assets/icon.ico     tray icon: BMP-format entries 16/32/48 (emblem,
+                        tight crop keeps the mark legible) + 256 (full
+                        lockup) — the same file src/tray.rs (legacy tray)
+                        and the mt-app tray parse at runtime.
+
+Small squares are the EMBLEM on the logo's own background color (the
+source art is a solid-color canvas, so letterboxing is seamless); the
+256 entry is the full lockup (emblem + wordmark). Deterministic: the
+same input produces byte-identical outputs.
+
+Usage: python3 scripts/make_logo_assets.py [src.png] [--out assets]
+"""
+
+import os
+import struct
+import sys
+import zlib
+
+# ---- PNG decode (stdlib) ---------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def decode_png(data):
+    """Minimal PNG reader: 8-bit depth, gray/RGB/RGBA/gray+alpha, no
+    interlace. Returns (w, h, rgba_bytes)."""
+    if data[:8] != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n":
+        raise SystemExit("not a PNG")
+    pos, idat, meta, palette, trns = 8, b"", None, None, None
+    while pos < len(data):
+        (ln,) = struct.unpack(">I", data[pos : pos + 4])
+        typ = data[pos + 4 : pos + 8]
+        body = data[pos + 8 : pos + 8 + ln]
+        if typ == b"IHDR":
+            w, h, depth, ctype = struct.unpack(">IIBB", body[:10])
+            if depth != 8:
+                raise SystemExit("unsupported bit depth %d" % depth)
+            if body[12] != 0:
+                raise SystemExit("interlaced PNG unsupported")
+            meta = (w, h, ctype)
+        elif typ == b"PLTE":
+            palette = body
+        elif typ == b"tRNS":
+            trns = body
+        elif typ == b"IDAT":
+            idat += body
+        elif typ == b"IEND":
+            break
+        pos += 12 + ln
+    if meta is None:
+        raise SystemExit("missing IHDR")
+    w, h, ctype = meta
+    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
+    nch = {0: 1, 2: 3, 3: 1, 4: 2, 6: 4}[ctype]
+    stride = w * nch
+    out = bytearray(w * h * 4)
+    prev = bytearray(stride)
+    p = 0
+    for y in range(h):
+        f = raw[p]
+        p += 1
+        line = bytearray(raw[p : p + stride])
+        p += stride
+        if f == 1:
+            for x in range(nch, stride):
+                line[x] = (line[x] + line[x - nch]) & 0xFF
+        elif f == 2:
+            for x in range(stride):
+                line[x] = (line[x] + prev[x]) & 0xFF
+        elif f == 3:
+            for x in range(stride):
+                a = line[x - nch] if x >= nch else 0
+                line[x] = (line[x] + ((a + prev[x]) >> 1)) & 0xFF
+        elif f == 4:
+            for x in range(stride):
+                a = line[x - nch] if x >= nch else 0
+                b = prev[x]
+                c = prev[x - nch] if x >= nch else 0
+                q = a + b - c
+                pa, pb, pc = abs(q - a), abs(q - b), abs(q - c)
+                r = a if (pa <= pb and pa <= pc) else (b if pb <= pc else c)
+                line[x] = (line[x] + r) & 0xFF
+        for x in range(w):
+            o = (y * w + x) * 4
+            s = x * nch
+            if ctype == 2:
+                out[o : o + 3] = line[s : s + 3]
+                out[o + 3] = 255
+            elif ctype == 6:
+                out[o : o + 4] = line[s : s + 4]
+            elif ctype == 0:
+                g = line[s]
+                out[o : o + 3] = bytes((g, g, g))
+                out[o + 3] = 255
+            elif ctype == 4:
+                g, a = line[s], line[s + 1]
+                out[o : o + 3] = bytes((g, g, g))
+                out[o + 3] = a
+            elif ctype == 3:
+                i = line[s]
+                out[o : o + 3] = palette[i * 3 : i * 3 + 3]
+                out[o + 3] = trns[i] if trns and i < len(trns) else 255
+        prev = line
+    return w, h, bytes(out)
+
+
+# ---- raster helpers --------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def px(img, x, y):
+    w, h, buf = img
+    o = (y * w + x) * 4
+    return (buf[o], buf[o + 1], buf[o + 2], buf[o + 3])
+
+
+def dist(a, b):
+    return max(abs(a[c] - b[c]) for c in range(3))
+
+
+def content_bbox(img, bg, thresh=12):
+    """Tight [x0, x1) x [y0, y1) box of pixels differing from bg."""
+    w, h, _ = img
+    minx, maxx, miny, maxy = w, -1, h, -1
+    for y in range(h):
+        for x in range(w):
+            if dist(px(img, x, y), bg) >= thresh:
+                if x < minx:
+                    minx = x
+                if x > maxx:
+                    maxx = x
+                if y < miny:
+                    miny = y
+                if y > maxy:
+                    maxy = y
+    if maxx < 0:
+        raise SystemExit("image is uniform — no content found")
+    return minx, miny, maxx + 1, maxy + 1
+
+
+def row_has_content(img, y, x0, x1, bg, thresh=12):
+    return any(dist(px(img, x, y), bg) >= thresh for x in range(x0, x1))
+
+
+def split_lockup(img, bbox, bg):
+    """Split emblem (top) from wordmark (bottom) at the widest empty row
+    band inside the bbox. Returns (emblem_box, lockup_box_is_full)."""
+    x0, y0, x1, y1 = bbox
+    gap_start = None
+    y = y1 - 2
+    gap_rows = []
+    while y > y0:
+        if not row_has_content(img, y, x0, x1, bg):
+            gap_rows.append(y)
+            if gap_start is None:
+                gap_start = y
+            elif y != gap_rows[-2] - 1:
+                # not contiguous — restart the band
+                gap_rows = [y]
+                gap_start = y
+        elif gap_rows:
+            break
+        y -= 1
+    if not gap_rows or len(gap_rows) < 3:
+        # no clear split: treat everything as one emblem
+        return bbox
+    return (x0, y0, x1, gap_rows[0] + 1)
+
+
+def crop(img, box):
+    w, h, buf = img
+    x0, y0, x1, y1 = box
+    cw, ch = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
+    out = bytearray(cw * ch * 4)
+    for y in range(ch):
+        s = ((y0 + y) * w + x0) * 4
+        d = (y * cw) * 4
+        out[d : d + cw * 4] = buf[s : s + cw * 4]
+    return (cw, ch, bytes(out))
+
+
+def resize_bilinear(img, dw, dh):
+    """Bilinear resample of an RGBA raster to dw x dh."""
+    w, h, buf = img
+    if (w, h) == (dw, dh):
+        return img
+    out = bytearray(dw * dh * 4)
+    xr = (w - 1) / max(dw - 1, 1)
+    yr = (h - 1) / max(dh - 1, 1)
+    for dy in range(dh):
+        sy = dy * yr
+        y0 = int(sy)
+        y1 = min(y0 + 1, h - 1)
+        fy = sy - y0
+        for dx in range(dw):
+            sx = dx * xr
+            x0 = int(sx)
+            x1 = min(x0 + 1, w - 1)
+            fx = sx - x0
+            for c in range(4):
+                a = buf[(y0 * w + x0) * 4 + c]
+                b = buf[(y0 * w + x1) * 4 + c]
+                cc = buf[(y1 * w + x0) * 4 + c]
+                d = buf[(y1 * w + x1) * 4 + c]
+                top = a + (b - a) * fx
+                bot = cc + (d - cc) * fx
+                out[(dy * dw + dx) * 4 + c] = int(round(top + (bot - top) * fy))
+    return (dw, dh, bytes(out))
+
+
+def square_on_bg(img, size, bg, margin=0.08):
+    """Scale img to fit a size x size canvas of `bg`, centered."""
+    w, h, _ = img
+    inner = size * (1.0 - 2 * margin)
+    scale = min(inner / w, inner / h)
+    tw, th = max(1, int(round(w * scale))), max(1, int(round(h * scale)))
+    scaled = resize_bilinear(img, tw, th)
+    ox, oy = (size - tw) // 2, (size - th) // 2
+    out = bytearray(bytes(bg[:3]) + b"\xff") * (size * size)
+    for y in range(th):
+        d = ((oy + y) * size + ox) * 4
+        out[d : d + tw * 4] = scaled[2][(y * tw) * 4 : (y * tw + tw) * 4]
+    return (size, size, bytes(out))
+
+
+# ---- ICO writing (BMP-format entries, same layout as make_icon.py) ---------
+
+
+def ico_image(img):
+    """Encode a square RGBA raster as RT_ICON bytes (BITMAPINFOHEADER with
+    doubled height, bottom-up 32-bpp XOR rows, 1-bpp AND mask)."""
+    size, _, buf = img
+    xor = b"".join(
+        bytes(
+            c
+            for x in range(size)
+            for c in (
+                buf[((y * size + x) * 4) + 2],
+                buf[((y * size + x) * 4) + 1],
+                buf[(y * size + x) * 4],
+                buf[((y * size + x) * 4) + 3],
+            )
+        )
+        for y in range(size - 1, -1, -1)
+    )
+    row_bytes = (size + 31) // 32 * 4
+    and_mask = bytearray(row_bytes * size)
+    for i, y in enumerate(range(size - 1, -1, -1)):
+        row = bytearray(row_bytes)
+        for x in range(size):
+            if buf[(y * size + x) * 4 + 3] == 0:
+                row[x // 8] |= 0x80 >> (x % 8)
+        and_mask[i * row_bytes : (i + 1) * row_bytes] = row
+    total = 40 + len(xor) + len(and_mask)
+    header = struct.pack(
+        "<IiiHHIIiiII",
+        40,
+        size,
+        size * 2,
+        1,
+        32,
+        0,
+        total,
+        0,
+        0,
+        0,
+        0,
+    )
+    return header + xor + bytes(and_mask)
+
+
+def write_ico(path, images):
+    count = len(images)
+    out = bytearray(struct.pack("<HHH", 0, 1, count))
+    offset = 6 + 16 * count
+    for size, data in images:
+        out += struct.pack(
+            "<BBBBHHII", size & 0xFF, size & 0xFF, 0, 0, 1, 32, len(data), offset
+        )
+        offset += len(data)
+    for _, data in images:
+        out += data
+    with open(path, "wb") as f:
+        f.write(out)
+    return len(out)
+
+
+# ---- main -------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    src = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join("assets", "logo.png")
+    outdir = os.path.join("assets", "")
+    data = open(src, "rb").read()
+    img = decode_png(data)
+    w, h, _ = img
+    bg = px(img, 0, 0)
+    bbox = content_bbox(img, bg)
+    emblem = split_lockup(img, bbox, bg)
+    emblem_img = crop(img, emblem)
+    lockup_img = crop(img, bbox)
+    print(
+        f"source {w}x{h}, bg rgb{bg[:3]}, "
+        f"lockup {bbox[2]-bbox[0]}x{bbox[3]-bbox[1]}, "
+        f"emblem {emblem[2]-emblem[0]}x{emblem[3]-emblem[1]}"
+    )
+
+    # keep the source verbatim
+    with open(os.path.join(outdir, "logo.png"), "wb") as f:
+        f.write(data)
+
+    # titlebar emblem + window icon (square canvases on the logo's bg)
+    for size in (24, 64):
+        sq = square_on_bg(emblem_img, size, bg)
+        with open(os.path.join(outdir, f"logo_{size}.rgba"), "wb") as f:
+            f.write(sq[2])
+        print(f"logo_{size}.rgba: {len(sq[2])} bytes ({size}x{size})")
+
+    # tray icon: 16/32/48 emblem squares + 256 full lockup
+    entries = []
+    for size in (16, 32, 48, 256):
+        sq = square_on_bg(emblem_img if size < 64 else lockup_img, size, bg)
+        entries.append((size, ico_image(sq)))
+    n = write_ico(os.path.join(outdir, "icon.ico"), entries)
+    print(f"icon.ico: {n} bytes (16/32/48 emblem + 256 lockup, BMP entries)")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
diff --git a/scripts/rig_analyze.py b/scripts/rig_analyze.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..45a0411
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/rig_analyze.py
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Pixel-cluster analysis for the S15 rig screenshots (pure stdlib PNG)."""
+import struct
+import sys
+import zlib
+
+
+def load(path):
+    d = open(path, "rb").read()
+    pos, idat = 8, b""
+    while pos < len(d):
+        (ln,) = struct.unpack(">I", d[pos : pos + 4])
+        typ = d[pos + 4 : pos + 8]
+        if typ == b"IHDR":
+            w, h, depth, ctype = struct.unpack(">IIBB", d[pos + 8 : pos + 18])
+        elif typ == b"IDAT":
+            idat += d[pos + 8 : pos + 8 + ln]
+        elif typ == b"IEND":
+            break
+        pos += 12 + ln
+    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
+    nch = {0: 1, 2: 3, 3: 1, 4: 2, 6: 4}[ctype]
+    stride = w * nch
+    out = bytearray(w * h * 3)
+    prev = bytearray(stride)
+    p = 0
+    for y in range(h):
+        f = raw[p]
+        p += 1
+        line = bytearray(raw[p : p + stride])
+        p += stride
+        if f == 1:
+            for x in range(nch, stride):
+                line[x] = (line[x] + line[x - nch]) & 0xFF
+        elif f == 2:
+            for x in range(stride):
+                line[x] = (line[x] + prev[x]) & 0xFF
+        elif f == 3:
+            for x in range(stride):
+                a = line[x - nch] if x >= nch else 0
+                line[x] = (line[x] + ((a + prev[x]) >> 1)) & 0xFF
+        elif f == 4:
+            for x in range(stride):
+                a = line[x - nch] if x >= nch else 0
+                b = prev[x]
+                c = prev[x - nch] if x >= nch else 0
+                q = a + b - c
+                pa, pb, pc = abs(q - a), abs(q - b), abs(q - c)
+                r = a if (pa <= pb and pa <= pc) else (b if pb <= pc else c)
+                line[x] = (line[x] + r) & 0xFF
+        for x in range(w):
+            o = (y * w + x) * 3
+            s = x * nch
+            if ctype in (2, 6):
+                out[o : o + 3] = line[s : s + 3]
+            elif ctype == 0:
+                g = line[s]
+                out[o : o + 3] = bytes((g, g, g))
+            elif ctype == 4:
+                g = line[s]
+                out[o : o + 3] = bytes((g, g, g))
+        prev = line
+    return w, h, out
+
+
+def px(img, x, y):
+    w, h, b = img
+    o = (y * w + x) * 3
+    return (b[o], b[o + 1], b[o + 2])
+
+
+def clusters_in_row_band(img, y0, y1, bg, tol=18, gap=6, x0=0, x1=None):
+    """x-clusters of non-bg pixels in a horizontal band (rows y0..y1)."""
+    w, h, _ = img
+    x1 = x1 or w
+    cols = set()
+    for y in range(y0, y1):
+        for x in range(x0, x1):
+            p = px(img, x, y)
+            if max(abs(p[c] - bg[c]) for c in range(3)) > tol:
+                cols.add(x)
+    out = []
+    for x in sorted(cols):
+        if out and x - out[-1][1] <= gap:
+            out[-1][1] = x
+        else:
+            out.append([x, x])
+    return out
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    img = load(sys.argv[1])
+    w, h, _ = img
+    print(f"{sys.argv[1]}: {w}x{h}")
+    corners = [px(img, 2, 2), px(img, w - 3, 2), px(img, 2, h - 3), px(img, w - 3, h - 3)]
+    print("corners:", corners)
+    for y0, y1, label in [
+        (0, 40, "titlebar-band"),
+        (0, 4, "top-edge"),
